rows.title: Some of your cells are not genetically yours — what can they tell us about life and death?
rows.summary: A tiny population of cells that are passed across the placenta between mother and baby challenge basic tenets of human immunology.

rows.title: Economic inequality does not equate to poor well-being or mental health
rows.summary: A meta-analysis of 168 studies covering more than 11 million people found no reliable link between economic inequality and well-being or mental health. In other words, living in a place that has large gaps between the rich and poor does not affect these outcomes, with implications for policy.

rows.title: How to reduce the environmental impact of wearable health-care devices
rows.summary: A model quantifies the environmental footprint of wearable health-care electronics and identifies strategies to reduce their environmental toll.

rows.title: Sub-Saharan Africa has lost almost one-quarter of its pre-industrial biodiversity
rows.summary: To map the biodiversity of sub-Saharan Africa, 200 specialists in African plants and animals were asked to estimate local species abundances. This approach integrates contextual, place-based knowledge into a multi-scale, comparative biodiversity assessment that can be used to support policy decisions at national, regional and global scales.

rows.title: Highly efficient LED device built by stacking layers of light-emitting perovskite
rows.summary: Stacking light-generating layers in ‘tandem’ light-emitting diodes (LEDs) can enhance performance, but achieving efficient and stable tandem LEDs made with perovskite materials has remained a challenge. A tandem perovskite-based device that seems to benefit from ‘recycling’ of photons between stacked layers demonstrates highly efficient performance, surpassing the combined emissions of two single-unit devices.

rows.title: A chiral fermionic valve driven by quantum geometry
rows.summary: Fermionic currents of opposing chirality can be spatially filtered without the need for a magnetic field using the quantum geometry of topological bands in single-crystal PdGa.

rows.title: Random heteropolymers as enzyme mimics
rows.summary: Modulation of random heteropolymers results in globular polymer clusters with catalytic activity mimicking proteins.

rows.title: Quantifying the global eco-footprint of wearable healthcare electronics
rows.summary: An integrated systems engineering framework based on life-cycle inventories is used to quantify the global eco-footprint of wearable healthcare electronics and identify effective mitigation strategies.

rows.title: Can boomerangs bounce?
rows.summary: Privacy in the age of computers and a Nature reader questions eyewitness accounts of boomerangs in our weekly dip into the archive.

rows.title: Safe as houses
rows.summary: Constructive feedback.

rows.title: Science in 2050: the future breakthroughs that will shape our world — and beyond
rows.summary: Nuclear fusion. People on Mars. Artificial general intelligence. These are just some of the advances that could come by the mid-century mark.

rows.title: Mummies give up their secrets — but not their mystery
rows.summary: A challenging exhibition asks why we are so fascinated with the preserved bodies of our ancestors, and how we should treat them.

rows.title: Put pressure on publishers to follow best practice — external regulation is the answer
rows.summary: Journals that work hard to meet the needs of both authors and readers should be acknowledged publicly — encouraging others to follow suit.

rows.title: Daily briefing: Explore 2025 with Leif Penguinson
rows.summary: Can you spot the penguin in every game this year?

rows.title: Audio long read: Will blockbuster obesity drugs revolutionize addiction treatment?
rows.summary: Researchers are investigating whether GLP-1 drugs can help blunt cravings for nicotine, alcohol and opioids.

rows.title: Probing pollutants: how I use penguin faeces to measure contaminants in Antarctica
rows.summary: Buse Tuğba Zaman is developing a way to track tiny amounts of contaminants — and fulfilled a dream to visit Earth’s most remote continent.

rows.title: Why academics should do more consulting — and how to make it work
rows.summary: Encouraging academics to act as advisers to outside organizations is the most effective way to serve society’s needs.

rows.title: Let 2026 be the year the world comes together for AI safety
rows.summary: AI technologies need to be safe and transparent. There are few, if any, benefits from being outside efforts to achieve this.

rows.title: Nine books to help shape your science career in 2026
rows.summary: If you’ve hatched a New Year plan to move abroad, improve your presentations or chase happiness as a 20-something researcher, you’ll find advice aplenty in these books.

rows.title: The Nature Podcast highlights of 2025
rows.summary: The team select some of their favourite stories from the past 12 months.

rows.title: Author Correction: Rolling back human pluripotent stem cells to an eight-cell embryo-like stage
Seeding opportunities for Black atmospheric scientists
rows.summary: Vernon Morris inspires change in the geoscience community by calling on colleagues to commit to anti-racism in their scientific endeavours.

rows.title: NAC controls nascent chain fate through tunnel sensing and chaperone action
rows.summary: Selective ribosome profiling and biochemical approaches establish nascent polypeptide-associated complex (NAC) as a central co-translational chaperone integrating proteostasis, subcellular delivery and regulation of elongation kinetics during protein biogenesis.

rows.title: Non-equilibrium snapshots of ligand efficacy at the μ-opioid receptor
rows.summary: Time-resolved cryo-electron microscopy of the μ-opioid receptor bound to various ligands enables a detailed look at the mechanisms that underlie GTP-induced activation of G proteins, and how different ligands affect activation kinetics.

rows.title: Nature's News & Views roundup of 2025
rows.summary: From astrophysics to genetics, climate change to materials science — the News & Views team talk about some of their science highlights of 2025.

rows.title: Author Correction: Cryo-EM structure of a natural RNA nanocage
Oddly cool super-hot planet has an atmosphere it shouldn’t
rows.summary: It’s a mystery why TOI-561 b’s blanket of gases hasn’t boiled off.

rows.title: Are we living in a parallel universe? The strange physics of Stranger Things
rows.summary: Nature speaks to theoretical physicists to explore the real theories that inspired the hit series. Warning: contains spoilers.

rows.title: ‘A serious problem’: peer reviews created using AI can avoid detection
rows.summary: Tools fail to identify most AI-generated peer-review reports, say researchers, who warn that the issue is only getting worse.

rows.title: AI and quantum science take centre stage under Trump — but with little new proposed funding
rows.summary: The US administration is banking on public–private partnerships and an expanded workforce to deliver progress, but critics say that this strategy could be offset by other US policies.

rows.title: Publisher Correction: Covalent targeted radioligands potentiate radionuclide therapy
Living water and whispering rocks: Books in brief
rows.summary: Andrew Robinson reviews five of the best science picks.

rows.title: Hot spot: plants use infrared signals to say they’re ready to reproduce
rows.summary: Some cycads warm up their reproductive organs to attract specially equipped pollinating beetles in the dark.

rows.title: US–Africa bilateral health deals won’t help against diseases that ignore borders
rows.summary: The COVID-19 pandemic, Ebola, mpox and AIDS all show the importance of strengthening Africa-wide surveillance and response systems that protect everyone.

rows.title: Science in 2026: the events to watch for in the coming year
rows.summary: The rise of AI scientists, missions to explore the moons of Earth and Mars and a massive ocean-floor drill are among the developments set to shape research in 2026.

rows.title: Point of no returns: researchers are crossing a threshold in the fight for funding
rows.summary: With so little money to go round, the costs of competing for grants can exceed what the grants are worth. When that happens, nobody wins.

rows.title: Dogma-defying signalling through G proteins could lead to better pain relief
rows.summary: Unexpected behaviours in G proteins could be exploited to design next-generation opioid drugs that provide stronger, longer-lasting pain relief.

rows.title: How the Romans built their empire of concrete
rows.summary: A unique archaeological site at Pompeii, Italy, reveals the secrets of peculiarly durable Roman building materials.

rows.title: Biobanks reveal genetic complexity in human evolution
rows.summary: Tiny genetic variations between humans, Neanderthals and Denisovans might not be all they were cracked up to be.

rows.title: Is bird flu the next pandemic? The science so far
rows.summary: Key mutations and animal spread could raise the risk to humans.

rows.title: The hidden cost of video-call glitches
rows.summary: Video-call glitches might seem harmless, but they can reduce people’s chances of getting hired, closing a business deal or following a doctor’s recommendation. Human brains expect video calls to feel like in-person conversations. When glitches break that illusion, it feels unsettling and strange, harming judgements of trustworthiness, likeability and credibility.

rows.title: Stopping the next flu pandemic
rows.summary: Avian influenza is devastating poultry operations, spreading in dairy cattle and infecting farm workers. Why isn’t the United States doing more to stop it?

rows.title: Beauty is in the eye of the beholder
rows.summary: The colour of regret.

rows.title: Seven feel-good science stories to restore your faith in 2025
rows.summary: Immense progress in gene editing, drug discovery and conservation are just some of the reasons to be cheerful about 2025.

rows.title: I’ve earned my PhD — what now?
rows.summary: A chemist faces a classic early-career dilemma: what should they do next, and how do they start?

rows.title: Mechanism for water formation on rocky exoplanets demonstrated in the lab
rows.summary: Experiments have revealed that the interaction between a hydrogen-rich atmosphere and a molten planet leads to high levels of water production. Through this process, planets could be enriched with water during their formation, altering their chemistry, evolution and, possibly, habitability.

rows.title: Virology’s most wanted: the influenza virus
rows.summary: The death toll and economic damage associated with flu highlight its role as one of the most harmful viruses in history.

rows.title: MIT fusion-lab head shot dead: a horror ‘impossible to believe’
rows.summary: Plasma physicist Nuno Loureiro was helping to develop clean-energy fusion devices.

rows.title: Flu’s link to cardiovascular disease shows why vaccination is essential
rows.summary: Influenza isn’t just a respiratory disease. Measures to stop its transmission, such as vaccination, could prevent thousands of heart-attack deaths.

rows.title: Could tracking animals’ health help to avert the next pandemic?
rows.summary: Avian influenza is sweeping the globe and infecting dozens of species. Advocates of an approach called One Health are calling for broad surveillance of wildlife, livestock and pets.

rows.title: How common is Alzheimer’s? Blood-test study holds surprises
rows.summary: A survey of Alzheimer’s disease prevalence in Norway confirms earlier estimates and might show how education level relates to risk.

rows.title: Take the News & Views end-of-year quiz: vampire fungus, migratory moths and a 160-year-old mystery
rows.summary: Try these 12 questions to test your knowledge of News & Views and Research Briefing articles published in 2025.

rows.title: The Nature Podcast festive spectacular 2025
rows.summary: Memorable science-themed gifts, games, seasonal songs, and Nature ’s 10.

rows.title: The quest to hatch a bird-flu vaccine
rows.summary: Although development of a jab for the H5N1 strain of avian flu is well under way, other strains are receiving less attention — and political obstacles to research could hamper progress.

rows.title: A modular quantum processor made using phosphorus atoms in silicon
rows.summary: A high-performance silicon-based quantum processor has been developed in which the spins of nine phosphorus nuclei — divided into two groups, or registers — and two shared electrons act as quantum bits (qubits). The modular design of this 11-qubit processor opens the door to a scalable approach to building large, reliable quantum-computing processors.

rows.title: A universal flu vaccine has proved challenging — could it finally be possible?
rows.summary: Scientists are deploying an array of technologies that are making a vaccine against all varieties of influenza seem more achievable.

rows.title: Systematic maps reveal how human chromosomes are organized
rows.summary: Our genomes are highly structured, which facilitates gene regulation. An ambitious project has catalogued the organization of DNA in the nuclei of human cells.

rows.title: Restoring youth to old immune cells: mRNA therapy turns back the clock
rows.summary: Testing in mice suggests that rejuvenating T cells could make vaccines and some cancer therapies more effective.

rows.title: Trump team plans to break up ‘global mothership’ of climate science
rows.summary: Much of the National Center for Atmospheric Research’s non-climate portfolio will be dispersed, the White House says.

rows.title: Annual flu vaccines are far from ideal — this is why
rows.summary: Flu-jab efficacy is often unimpressive. Improvements could come through nasal delivery.

rows.title: Immunological sin: how a person’s earliest flu infections dictate life-long immunity
rows.summary: Researchers are striving to understand the impact a phenomenon known as original antigenic sin has on immunity to the virus.

rows.title: Author Correction: Neuroimmune cardiovascular interfaces control atherosclerosis
Transient hepatic reconstitution of trophic factors enhances aged immunity
rows.summary: Using lipid nanoparticle delivery of mRNAs to the liver in aged mice, T cell function and declining immune cues can be restored.

rows.title: Gene-specific selective sweeps are pervasive across human gut microbiomes
rows.summary: Development and application of the integrated linkage disequilibrium score (iLDS) reveals both selective pressures impacting the human gut microbiome and the mechanisms by which gut bacteria adapt to meet them.

rows.title: GTP release-selective agonists prolong opioid analgesic efficacy
rows.summary: Mu opioid receptor agonists with a preference for the non-GTP-bound state of the G protein promote GTP release, thereby potentiating antinociceptive effects of drugs such as morphine and fentanyl without also increasing their respiratory or cardiac effects.

rows.title: Programmable 200 GOPS Hopfield-inspired photonic Ising machine
rows.summary: An architecture inspired by Hopfield networks based on a programmable, stable, room-temperature optoelectronic oscillator-based photonics Ising machine is introduced that can be used to efficiently address optimization and combinatorics problems.

rows.title: An integrated view of the structure and function of the human 4D nucleome
rows.summary: The 4D Nucleome Project demonstrates the use of genomic assays and computational methods to measure genome folding and then predict genomic structure from DNA sequence, facilitating the discovery of potential effects of genetic variants, including variants associated with disease, on genome structure and function.

rows.title: Palaeometabolomes yield biological and ecological profiles at early human sites
rows.summary: Metabolic and proteomic profiles derived from fossilized skeletal remains of animals enable inferences regarding physiological health and disease as well as diet to provide reconstructions of ancient soil, vegetation and palaeoclimate characteristics.

rows.title: Astrocyte CCN1 stabilizes neural circuits in the adult brain
rows.summary: Neural circuits in adult mouse visual cortex are stabilized by astrocytes, which secrete CCN1, resulting in reduced plasticity and increased maturation of multiple cell types.

rows.title: An 11-qubit atom processor in silicon
rows.summary: An 11-qubit atom processor comprising two precision-placed nuclear spin registers of phosphorus in silicon is shown to achieve state-of-the-art Bell-state fidelities of up to 99.5%.

rows.title: The global hydrogen budget
rows.summary: Trends in global H 2 sources and sinks are analysed from 1990 to 2020, and a comprehensive budget for the decade 2010–2020 is presented.

rows.title: Visualizing interaction-driven restructuring of quantum Hall edge states
rows.summary: Scanning tunnelling microscopy is used to image pristine electrostatically defined quantum Hall edge states in graphene with high spatial resolution and demonstrate their interaction-driven restructuring.

rows.title: Prevalence of Alzheimer’s disease pathology in the community
rows.summary: The prevalence of Alzheimer’s disease neuropathological changes is reported based on blood-based biomarkers in a Norwegian population-based cohort.

rows.title: Titan’s strong tidal dissipation precludes a subsurface ocean
rows.summary: Reanalysis of radiometric data from Cassini indicates that Titan does not contain a subsurface ocean, as strong tidal dissipation observed in its gravity field is not consistent with the presence of a liquid layer.

rows.title: Human assembloids recapitulate periportal liver tissue in vitro
rows.summary: Hepatocyte organoids derived directly from human tissue enable long-term hepatocyte expansion and can be combined with portal mesenchyme and cholangiocyte organoids to form a donor-specific periportal liver assembloid system.

rows.title: Mazdutide versus placebo in Chinese adults with type 2 diabetes
rows.summary: The dual GLP-1 and glucagon receptor co-agonist mazdutide is a promising therapeutic option for type 2 diabetes (T2D) treatment, providing clinically meaningful glycaemic control and weight reduction in Chinese adults with T2D.

rows.title: Spatiotemporal cellular map of the developing human reproductive tract
rows.summary: A detailed spatiotemporal roadmap of the human female and male reproductive tracts during key periods of sexual differentiation provides new cellular and molecular insights into how early axial gradients lead to specific cell lineages and tissue structures.

rows.title: Lesion-remote astrocytes govern microglia-mediated white matter repair
rows.summary: After spinal cord injury, lesion-remote astrocytes acquire heterogeneous, spatially restricted reactivity states that shape neuroinflammation, neural repair and neurological recovery.

rows.title: Laser spectroscopy and CP-violation sensitivity of actinium monofluoride
rows.summary: Gas-phase actinium monofluoride (AcF) has been produced and spectroscopically studied at the CERN-ISOLDE radioactive ion beam facility; the results highlight the potential of 227 AcF for exceptionally sensitive searches of CP violation.

rows.title: 3D nanolithography with metalens arrays and spatially adaptive illumination
rows.summary: A three-dimensional (3D) nanofabrication platform based on metalens-generated focal spot arrays is introduced to parallelize two-photon lithography beyond centimetre-scale write field areas, revealing the potential of 3D nanolithography towards wafer-scale production.

rows.title: Mazdutide versus dulaglutide in Chinese adults with type 2 diabetes
rows.summary: The results of a clinical trial of mazdutide, a dual glucagon and GLP-1 receptor agonist, in the context of type 2 diabetes show that it could hold promise as an add-on therapy to conventional oral anti-diabetic drugs.

rows.title: Safety regulations for cloning and a compass that finds true north
rows.summary: Scientists discuss concerns that genetic manipulation could lead to disease outbreaks, and Nature is gifted an unusual scientific instrument, in our weekly dip into the archive.

rows.title: Science’s role in my Great British Sewing Bee success
rows.summary: A research background and a passion for sewing inspired by her father helped Yasmin Proctor-Kent to reach the finals of the 2025 television competition.

rows.title: Scientists skip key US meetings — and seize on smaller alternatives
rows.summary: Researchers are devising creative ways to get together as Trump’s policies curb travel to US gatherings.

rows.title: How my institution strengthened research despite chronic underfunding
rows.summary: Nurturing research talent at community-rooted universities and colleges is a necessity, not a luxury.

rows.title: AI is transforming the economy — understanding its impact requires both data and imagination
rows.summary: Controlled studies capture only a fraction of the effects of artificial intelligence. Economists should work with social scientists to find innovative ways to fully grasp this fast-moving field.

rows.title: Giving a voice to animals: Laos’s national herpetologist on her day-to-day
rows.summary: Somphouthone Phimmachak studies amphibians and reptiles as one of the country’s few conservation researchers.

rows.title: How fasting boosts breast cancer therapy
rows.summary: A discovery in mice reveals why fasting enhances a type of breast cancer treatment — a hormone-signalling pathway and gene-expression changes have key roles.

rows.title: NSF softens grant-review rules to cope with backlog
rows.summary: Agency staff members say that the changes are reasonable, but they are worried about the potential effects on review.

rows.title: The best science images of 2025 — Nature ’s picks
rows.summary: The Sun’s fiery surface, a tattooed tardigrade, rare red lightning and more.

rows.title: How 2025 showcased the power and resilience of science
rows.summary: There were huge disruptions to the global scientific enterprise this year — but immense bright spots for health, discovery, innovation and research collaboration.

rows.title: Grant cuts, arrests, lay-offs: Trump made 2025 a tumultuous year for science
rows.summary: How the Trump administration caused seismic disruptions to the world’s premier scientific superpower.

rows.title: Tracing pollution in the lives of Arctic seabirds
rows.summary: Olivier Chastel travels to Svalbard in northern Norway to study the impact of contaminants such as mercury on black-legged kittiwakes.

rows.title: More than half of researchers now use AI for peer review — often against guidance
rows.summary: A survey of 1,600 academics found that more than 50% have used artificial-intelligence tools while peer reviewing manuscripts.

rows.title: Author Correction: Distinct fibroblast subsets drive inflammation and damage in arthritis
In praise of inefficiency, failure and friendship: ten galvanizing reads for this festive season
rows.summary: In a world that can seem lacking in optimism, researchers share their opinions on books that stimulate thoughts — and actions — for a better future.

rows.title: Science sleuths raise concerns about scores of bioengineering papers
rows.summary: Prominent bioengineer Ali Khademhosseini has so far corrected more than 40 of the papers in question, but critics say some should have been retracted.

rows.title: Author Correction: Cancer SLC43A2 alters T cell methionine metabolism and histone methylation
Revised estimates of CO 2 sources and sinks improve global carbon accounting
rows.summary: Updated estimates of the worldwide sources and sinks of anthropogenic carbon dioxide provide a firmer basis for monitoring climate action.

rows.title: China leads research in 90% of crucial technologies — a dramatic shift this century
rows.summary: The United States tops the remaining areas in an assessment of 74 technologies.

rows.title: Author Correction: Unravelling cysteine-deficiency-associated rapid weight loss
Australia’s world-first social media ban is a ‘natural experiment’ for scientists
rows.summary: Researchers will study the effects of the policy on young people’s mental health, social interactions and political engagement.

rows.title: Giant 3D map shows almost every building in the world
rows.summary: A database of 2.75 billion buildings could help scientists to monitor urban planning, climate change, disaster risks and even corruption.

rows.title: Asteroids, antibiotics and ants: a year of remarkable science
rows.summary: Highlights from News & Views published in 2025.

rows.title: This AI model ‘studied’ physics — and learnt to forecast extreme weather
rows.summary: Combining artificial intelligence with a conventional climate model can predict heatwaves faster than the standard model alone.

rows.title: The gift that shaped my career in science
rows.summary: Nature asked about your most memorable scientific gifts. You delivered.

rows.title: Quantum computing ‘KPIs’ could distinguish true breakthroughs from spurious claims
rows.summary: Researchers are devising ways to make new machines face off, without the hype.

rows.title: Solar cells that combine multiple perovskite layers surpass 30% efficiency
rows.summary: Perovskites are promising materials for solar cells. A layer of dipolar molecules at the perovskite surface improves the efficiency of these devices.

rows.title: Author Correction: Conservation and alteration of mammalian striatal interneurons
Glimmers of hope for a deadly disease
rows.summary: New models, efforts for early detection and better therapies may help change pancreatic cancer’s aggressive course.

rows.title: Will young universities set the pace in the age of AI?
rows.summary: Why some institutions are betting on technology to stay relevant.

rows.title: Exposing a silent cancer
rows.summary: Pancreatic cancer is one of the deadliest malignancies, and it is increasingly occurring in young people — especially women. An uptick in research funding is a welcome development in the push to transform treatment.

rows.title: Neanderthals mastered fire — 400,000 years ago
rows.summary: Archaeological evidence makes a compelling case for Neanderthal-created fires 400,000 years ago in Suffolk, UK — plus, how chatbots can sway the opinions of voters.

rows.title: Pancreatic cancer is evasive. Is the nervous system the reason why?
rows.summary: A growing body of research suggests tumours rely on proteins and genes that are unique to the nervous system to persist in the body.

rows.title: Six highlights from pancreatic cancer research
rows.summary: Unpacking risk factors, disease aggressiveness and other key work.

rows.title: What would an AI university look like and how might it change education?
rows.summary: From lectures by avatars to entire qualifications, higher education centred around AI is just around the corner.

rows.title: A breathalyser-style test for detecting pancreatic cancer
rows.summary: Surgeon George Hanna is developing a non-invasive test to catch one of the deadliest cancers before it’s too late.

rows.title: Is your brain tired? Researchers are discovering the roots of mental fatigue
rows.summary: Better ways to measure cognitive exhaustion could point to treatments for long COVID and other debilitating disorders.

rows.title: A giant catalogue of microscopic species across Denmark
rows.summary: The Microflora Danica project has catalogued the microbial diversity of environmental habitats across Denmark and established an improved taxonomic reference database. As well as providing a special record of nitrogen-oxidizing microorganisms, the data set serves as a national baseline for tracking future microbial responses to factors such as land-use change and global warming.

rows.title: SOS: RNA-processing mechanism rescues genes from invasive DNA
rows.summary: Transposable elements can insert into genes, disrupting protein-coding potential. Researchers discover a mode of RNA processing, ‘SOS splicing’, that provides a quick fix.

rows.title: But only just
rows.summary: Making scents of things.

rows.title: The pancreatic cancer models helping to drive innovation in the field
rows.summary: Cellular, animal and computational models of the disease are providing fresh insights into biology and treatment.

rows.title: China is leading the world on AI governance: other countries must engage
rows.summary: The nation’s regulators are attempting to match the rapid pace at which AI is evolving. That needs to become a global initiative.

rows.title: Four young universities share their strategies for success
rows.summary: Nimble, responsive and collaborative, these institutions stand out in the Nature Index.

rows.title: A simple slipknot for precise force control
rows.summary: The tension of conventional surgical sutures can affect wound healing and is dependent on the surgeon’s experience. Imaging and simulations reveal that slipknots can reproducibly store and release force, enabling precise and consistent surgical knotting without the need for electronic sensors or specialized equipment.

rows.title: Nuclear clocks could use electrical signals to keep time
rows.summary: The emission of photons by excited nuclei has been explored for timekeeping and sensing, but nuclear processes that eject electrons offer practical advantages.

rows.title: Huge genetic study reveals hidden links between psychiatric conditions
rows.summary: Analysis of more than one million people shows that mental-health disorders fall into five clusters, each of them linked to a specific set of genetic variants.

rows.title: Genetically engineered mosquitoes block development of circulating malaria strains
rows.summary: The genetic engineering of mosquitoes offers a potentially transformative, self-sustaining opportunity for malaria control and elimination in Africa. By rendering mosquitoes unable to transmit the malaria parasite, even when they bite humans, the technology provides a mosquito-based intervention to complement existing efforts.

rows.title: Therapeutic vaccines can challenge pancreatic cancer before it takes hold
rows.summary: Specific protein targets and personalized vaccines have the potential to increase survival rates for the disease.

rows.title: The brain’s speech centre responds to universal and specific features of language
rows.summary: More than 7,000 languages are spoken around the world, but the human brain becomes highly specialized to process speech in an individual’s own language. Recordings from human brains reveal the shared and language-specific neural mechanisms that arise in the superior temporal gyrus to achieve this feat.

rows.title: Shared genetic risk in psychiatric disorders
rows.summary: Scientists have characterized the broad genetic patterns that are shared across 14 psychiatric disorders. Could it reframe how mental-health conditions are diagnosed?

rows.title: Early detection could improve pancreatic cancer’s poor survival rates
rows.summary: The disease is often caught too late to affect a person’s prognosis — scientists are looking to change that.

rows.title: Oldest known evidence of the controlled ignition of fire
rows.summary: A 400,000-year-old site excavated in England reveals signs of deliberate fires made using the mineral iron pyrite to produce sparks.

rows.title: A guide to the Nature Index
rows.summary: A description of the terminology and methodology used in this supplement, and a guide to the functionality that is available free online at natureindex.com.

rows.title: Fasting boosts breast cancer therapy efficacy via glucocorticoid activation
rows.summary: Beneficial effects of fasting combined with endocrine therapy for oestrogen receptor-α-expressing breast cancers can be recapitulated using exogenous glucocorticoid receptor ligands instead of fasting to reduce harmful effects.

rows.title: The influence of short-lived halogens on atmospheric chemistry and climate
rows.summary: A Review of the impacts of short-lived halogens on air quality and climate identifies gaps in our knowledge of short-lived halogen emissions, chemistry, and the environmental and climate impacts.

rows.title: Quantifying grain boundary deformation mechanisms in small-grained metals
rows.summary: Experimental observations in small-grained polycrystals suggest a new concept of considering metallic grain boundaries not as defects but as separate defect-containing lattices, providing a potential explanation for the deformation behaviour of nanocrystalline metals.

rows.title: Gene-drive-capable mosquitoes suppress patient-derived malaria in Tanzania
rows.summary: Engineering of local Anopheles gambiae under containment enables the generation of a transgenic strain equipped with non-autonomous gene drive capabilities that robustly inhibits genetically diverse Plasmodium falciparum isolates obtained from naturally infected children.

rows.title: Erythropoietin receptor on cDC1s dictates immune tolerance
rows.summary: The tolerogenic activity of type 1 conventional dendritic cells (cDC1s) is determined by EPOR, which is preferentially expressed in cDC1s and induces antigen-specific FOXP3-expressing regulatory T cells.

rows.title: Human gut M cells resemble dendritic cells and present gluten antigen
rows.summary: An intestinal organoid model recapitulates human microfold (M) cell function and transcriptomic profiling and biochemical assays demonstrate that M cells uptake and present antigens to the immune system via the class II major histocompatibility complex.

rows.title: Cross-regulation of [2Fe–2S] cluster synthesis by ferredoxin-2 and frataxin
rows.summary: A finely balanced ratio of ferredoxin-2 (FDX2) and frataxin (FXN) is essential for the synthesis of iron–sulfur clusters, and interventions targeting this ratio could provide a way to treat related diseases, such as Friedreich’s ataxia.

rows.title: Sterilization and contraception increase lifespan across vertebrates
rows.summary: Data collected from zoos and aquariums worldwide show that hormonal contraception or permanent surgical sterilization in mammals increase life expectancy, with different mechanisms in males and females.

rows.title: Earliest evidence of making fire
rows.summary: Baked sediment, heat-shattered artefacts and introduced pyrite in a 400,000-year-old Palaeolithic occupation site in Suffolk, UK provide evidence of intentional fire-making, marking a pivotal moment in human development.

rows.title: Observation of deuteron and antideuteron formation from resonance-decay nucleons
rows.summary: The ALICE Collaboration provides details on the microscopic mechanism that ends up creating antideuteron in high-energy proton–proton collisions at the Large Hadron Collider.

rows.title: Hot droughts in the Amazon provide a window to a future hypertropical climate
rows.summary: Thirty years of forest demographic data, combined with recent ecophysiological measurements, reveal that intense Amazon droughts sharply increase tree mortality once soil moisture falls below a threshold, and that these hot droughts will become more frequent and intense as Earth warms towards hypertropical conditions.

rows.title: A direct role for a mitochondrial targeting sequence in signalling stress
rows.summary: Cells can sense mitochondrial damage through signalling via an unimported mitochondrial targeting sequence.

rows.title: Neutrophils preserve energy storage in sympathetically activated adipocytes
rows.summary: Neutrophil-derived IL-1β has a role in preserving lipid stores during metabolic stress.

rows.title: Mapping the genetic landscape across 14 psychiatric disorders
rows.summary: Genomic analyses applied to 14 childhood- and adult-onset psychiatric disorders identifies five underlying genomic factors that explain the majority of the genetic variance of the individual disorders.

rows.title: An RNA splicing system that excises DNA transposons from animal mRNAs
rows.summary: A new type of mRNA splicing mechanism discovered in Caenorhabditis elegans that detects and removes inverted repeats also occurs in human cells, thereby providing another strategy to protect against the negative effects of transposable elements.

rows.title: Uncovering the role of LINE-1 in the evolution of lung adenocarcinoma
rows.summary: Lung adenocarcinomas bearing the ID2 mutational signature display increased LINE-1 retrotransposon activity, which contributes to their fast evolutionary dynamics and aggressive phenotype.

rows.title: Somatic evolution following cancer treatment in normal tissue
rows.summary: High-depth sequencing of non-cancerous tissue from patients with metastatic cancer reveals single-base mutational signatures of alcohol, smoking and cancer treatments, and reveals how exogenous factors, including cancer therapies, affect somatic cell evolution.

rows.title: Protected area management has significant spillover effects on vegetation
rows.summary: Analysis of effect sizes of vegetation spillovers from protected areas in Australia shows that 71% of over 3,063 analysed protected areas had a positive spillover effect, and that these effects covary with protected area management type.

rows.title: Laser-based conversion electron Mössbauer spectroscopy of 229 ThO 2

rows.title: Satellite megaconstellations will threaten space-based astronomy

rows.summary: The DNA of ancient individuals dating to between 10,000 and 150 years ago reveals the existence of a long-standing, yet previously uncharacterized, lineage in the Southern Cone of South America — a region comprising what is now Argentina, Chile and Uruguay. Genomic data from present-day inhabitants attest to the genetic continuity of the lineage in central Argentina.

rows.summary: A glasses-free three-dimensional display, which is as large as a conventional desktop screen and has a viewing angle larger than 100°, is achieved by an artificial intelligence-powered optimization algorithm, which adapts the virtual images sent around each eye in real time.

rows.title: Detection of triboelectric discharges during dust events on Mars
rows.summary: The SuperCam microphone aboard the Perseverance rover captured 55 triboelectric discharges during dust events on Mars over two Martian years, providing implications for examining the planet’s surface chemistry, habitability and human exploration.

rows.title: Progressive coevolution of the yeast centromere and kinetochore
rows.summary: Thousands of centromeres were identified and tracked across two major fungal clades, showing that new centromeres spread progressively and that the kinetochore acts as a filter to determine which new centromere variants are tolerated.

rows.title: Entanglement-enhanced nanoscale single-spin sensing
rows.summary: An entanglement-enhanced sensing strategy making use of entangled nitrogen–vacancy pairs is described, demonstrating a 3.4-fold improvement in sensitivity and a 1.6-fold improvement in spatial resolution relative to single nitrogen–vacancy centres under ambient conditions.

rows.title: Healthy forests safeguard traditional wild meat food systems in Amazonia
rows.summary: Data provided by Amazonian peoples are used to estimate the value of wild animals as a source of food, including its spatial distribution and nutritional value, providing information that will be key for improved management of forest ecosystems in the region.

rows.title: Operating two exchange-only qubits in parallel
rows.summary: Parallel operation of two exchange-only qubits consisting of six quantum dots arranged linearly is shown to be achievable and maintains qubit control quality compared with sequential operation, with potential for use in scaled quantum computing.

rows.title: Long-read metagenomics reveals phage dynamics in the human gut microbiome
rows.summary: Complex prophage integration dynamics, including low-level induction, cross-family host range and transposase-mediated mobilization, challenge existing paradigms and deepen our understanding of phage–bacterial interactions in the human gut microbiome.

rows.title: Lack of funding is pushing research in Romania to extinction
Chile must preserve international science in Antarctica

rows.title: Thirty years of Bose–Einstein condensation
rows.summary: In 1995, two papers reported long-sought proof of an exotic state of matter — with applications in fields as diverse as quantum computing and cosmology.

rows.title: We are all mosaics: vast genetic diversity found between cells in a single person
rows.summary: Technical advances allow researchers to trace the genetic changes that occur over time.

rows.title: Author Correction: An asymmetric fission island driven by shell effects in light fragments
The ocular microbiome: more than meets the eye
rows.summary: Bacteria, viruses and fungi that colonize the body — including some that live directly on eye surfaces — can have an important role in eye health.

rows.title: Polyclonal origins of human premalignant colorectal lesions
rows.summary: Many premalignant colorectal polyps in familial adenomatous polyposis arise polyclonally rather than from a single mutated cell, showing diverse early evolutionary trajectories that frequently occur without clonal APC or KRAS driver events.

rows.title: Chasing crayfish and the leeches that live on them
rows.summary: Maria Shrestha works to understand the evolutionary history of crayfish symbionts — and how they might be indicators of trouble.

rows.title: Hydrogen fuel isn’t always the green choice
rows.summary: Using hydrogen to power road transportation and heat homes doesn’t save more carbon emissions than direct electrification.

rows.title: The Internet is broken and the inventor of the World Wide Web wants to fix it
rows.summary: Tim Berners-Lee is calling for a return to a decentralized Internet and stronger data privacy, but his arguments could be more inspiring.

rows.title: What is the future of intelligence? The answer could lie in the story of its evolution
rows.summary: The advent of artificial intelligence might be just the latest stage in a guiding biological process that has produced ever more complex, mutually dependent organisms over the history of life.

rows.title: Putting nature on the balance sheet: how to account for the ecological costs of our actions
rows.summary: Economists should consider forests and wetlands as well as factories and farms.

rows.title: A ten-year drive to credit authors for their work — and why there’s still more to do
rows.summary: Information about the roles of each author of a paper can help to build trust, integrity and responsible research assessment. Coordinated efforts are needed to consolidate progress.

rows.title: MAPK-driven epithelial cell plasticity drives colorectal cancer therapeutic resistance
rows.summary: In colorectal cancer, therapeutic resistance is driven by MAPK-dependent epithelial cell plasticity.

rows.title: Of masks and Mayans: Books in brief

rows.title: Synthetic tongue rates chillies’ heat — and spares human tasters
rows.summary: Gel-based device inspired by the cooling powers of milk assesses peppers whose burn ranges from mild to dangerous.

rows.title: Psychedelics and immortality: Nature went to a health summit starring RFK and JD Vance
rows.summary: The Make America Healthy Again summit, attended by health secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr and vice-president JD Vance, gave a sense of what’s driving US health policy.

rows.title: Daily briefing: Where pigeons get their sense of direction
rows.summary: Pigeons sense magnetic fields by detecting tiny electrical currents in their inner ears, a study suggests. Plus, hear from the fraught final hours of COP30 and meet the researchers who do science with excrement.

rows.title: Cyberattacks’ harm to universities is growing — and so are their effects on research
rows.summary: Hackers are ramping up attacks on academic institutions to access valuable data and to demand ransoms.

rows.title: I encourage women to claim their space in astrophysics and beyond
rows.summary: Debarati Chatterjee’s mission is to make science in India more welcoming towards women.

rows.title: The origin of male seahorses’ brood pouch
rows.summary: Similarities to the womb and placenta of female mammals indicate a response to common evolutionary challenges in pregnancy.

rows.title: Neanderthal DNA reveals how human faces form
rows.summary: Subtle genomic variations between humans and Neanderthals provide clues to how DNA shapes our facial features.

rows.title: Bacterial cooperative weaves sustainable rainbow materials
rows.summary: Several microbial strains working together in a ‘one pot’ production process could provide an environmentally friendly route to clothing.

rows.title: Daily briefing: What happens to science if the ‘AI bubble’ bursts?
rows.summary: An artificial-intelligence market crash could drive AI researchers back into academia, experts say. Plus, the ethics of brain implants that detect ‘preconscious’ thoughts and a gene-editing tool that could tackle multiple diseases.

Has the mysterious ‘compass’ organ of birds been found at last?
rows.summary: Multiple lines of evidence suggest that pigeons sense magnetic fields by detecting electric currents in their inner ears.

rows.title: Waste not: how researchers harness pee and poo for science
rows.summary: It might seem gross, but these materials are treasure troves for research.

rows.title: A brain implant that could rival Neuralink’s enters clinical trials
rows.summary: Neurotechnology company Paradromics will test its device in a trial aimed at safely restoring speech for people with severe motor impairments.

rows.title: Author Correction: A metallic p -wave magnet with commensurate spin helix
Insulin cream offers needle-free option for diabetes
rows.summary: Skin-permeable polymer shows promise at insulin delivery in animal experiments — plus, how the brain responds to unfamiliar languages.

rows.title: Author Correction: AIM2 in regulatory T cells restrains autoimmune diseases

rows.summary: The rise in artificial-intelligence technologies is unprecedented, but some predict a stock-market crash that could have knock-on effects for funding and jobs.

rows.title: Science on shaky ground: Canadian research shifts in the wake of US cuts
rows.summary: Scientists hunt for the silver lining amid the changing funding landscape.

rows.title: Daily briefing: Kissing might have evolved 21.5 million years ago
rows.summary: Most large apes kiss, and Neanderthals probably did too. Plus, what a surge of measles in North America means for the world and what Canada’s bold talent-attraction program means for scientists.

rows.title: How do genetic association studies rank genes?
rows.summary: Genome-wide association studies and rare-variant burden tests are the two main tools for discovering links between genetic variants and traits. Comparisons of their results reveal that they systematically rank genes differently, and models have been developed to explain why. Ultimately, both methods are complementary, each highlighting distinct aspects of trait biology.

rows.title: Budget release: Canada courts US researchers and signals wider commitment to science
rows.summary: Artificial intelligence and international scientists are some of the big winners in the country’s spending plan this year.

rows.title: South Africa is right to put debt, climate and inequality at the heart of G20
rows.summary: The host of the high-level meeting must not be swayed from its priorities, which are in line with the evidence from research.

rows.title: Tuning into a massive stellar storm on the radio
rows.summary: A stellar radio burst has been detected that signals an ejection of plasma from a star other than the Sun. The signal reveals the severe space-weather conditions of the planets that orbit the Milky Way’s most common stars.

rows.title: Lanthanides go electric: promising light emitters used in LEDs
rows.summary: Nanoparticles containing lanthanide ions are excellent light emitters. The addition of organic molecules means that they can be activated using electric currents.

rows.title: Women seem to retract fewer papers than men — but why?
rows.summary: In an analysis of nearly 900 retracted medical-research studies, the number of female authors is disproportionately low.

rows.title: Circular DNA has a ticket to ride chromosomes
rows.summary: How circular extrachromosomal DNA is inherited during cell division is a puzzle. Key sequences enabling this DNA to journey with chromosomes have been identified.

rows.title: The asymmetric synthesis of an acyclic N -stereogenic amine
rows.summary: Catalytic asymmetric synthesis of stable, acyclic N -stereogenic amines by the addition of enol silanes to nitronium ions that ion pair to a confined chiral anion is described.

rows.title: Standing up for Inuit-led research in Canada’s changing Arctic
rows.summary: In Canada’s far north, sociologist Jessica Penney is mixing research with advocacy.

rows.title: The singular proposition of trees
rows.summary: Staying in sync.

rows.title: How to fix genetic ‘nonsense’: versatile gene-editing tool could tackle a host of diseases
rows.summary: Synthetic RNA molecules can program cells to ignore DNA mutations that interfere with protein production.

rows.title: Mind-reading devices can now predict preconscious thoughts: is it time to worry?
rows.summary: Ethicists say AI-powered advances will threaten the privacy and autonomy of people who use neurotechnology.

rows.title: Stop the nonsense: genome editing creates potentially therapeutic transfer RNAs
rows.summary: Genome editing has been used to generate a type of transfer RNA that overcomes the harmful effects of ‘nonsense’ gene variants — a possible remedy for a range of diseases.

rows.title: Connectivity underlying motor cortex activity during goal-directed behaviour
rows.summary: All-optical mapping of neural connectivity in motor cortex links network topology to network dynamics and computation underlying naturalistic goal-directed behaviour.

rows.title: Prime editing-installed suppressor tRNAs for disease-agnostic genome editing
rows.summary: A new strategy that uses prime editing to convert an endogenous tRNA into a suppressor tRNA shows therapeutic potential for multiple genetic diseases that are caused by premature stop codons.

rows.title: ZAK activation at the collided ribosome
rows.summary: The kinase ZAK is activated at collided ribosomes to mediate the ribotoxic stress response.

rows.title: Semantic design of functional de novo genes from a genomic language model
rows.summary: By learning a semantics of gene function based on genomic context, the genomic language model Evo autocompletes DNA prompts to generate novel genes encoding protein and RNA molecules with defined activities, whose sequences generalize beyond those found in nature.

rows.title: Repulsions instruct synaptic partner matching in an olfactory circuit
rows.summary: Transcriptomic screening identifies pairs of cell-surface proteins that mediate repulsive interactions between axons and dendrites of non-cognate partner neurons, thereby contributing to correct synaptic partner matching.

rows.title: Structural basis of regulated N-glycosylation at the secretory translocon
rows.summary: The structural mechanism of a natively isolated GRP94 folding intermediate tethered to a CCDC134-bound translocon is described, revealing how the nascent chain remodels the translocon to control N-glycosylation by OST.

rows.title: Tumour-reactive heterotypic CD8 T cell clusters from clinical samples
rows.summary: Tumour-reactive CD8 + T cells are enriched in functional clusters with tumour cells and/or antigen-presenting cells and can be isolated and expanded from clinical samples.

rows.title: Integrator dynamics in the cortico-basal ganglia loop for flexible motor timing
rows.summary: How the mouse frontal cortex and striatum interact to implement integrator dynamics controlling movement timing is explored.

rows.title: Hepatic zonation determines tumorigenic potential of mutant β-catenin
rows.summary: Zonal positioning in the liver determines whether the CTNNB1 oncogene can induce liver cancer.

rows.title: Electro-generated excitons for tunable lanthanide electroluminescence
rows.summary: The electroluminescence emitted from lanthanide fluoride nanocrystals functionalized with ligands is shown to be tunable, providing a method for exciton control in insulating nanocrystal systems and offering a pathway for spectrally precise electroluminescent materials.

rows.title: Rewiring an olfactory circuit by altering cell-surface combinatorial code
rows.summary: In Drosophila , changing the expression of a small set of cell-surface proteins in just one type of olfactory neuron rewires its connections almost entirely to a new postsynaptic partner neuron type, altering the fly’s odour response and courtship behaviour.

rows.title: Triplets electrically turn on insulating lanthanide-doped nanoparticles
rows.summary: To turn on and obtain emission from lanthanide-doped insulating nanoparticles, an electrical excitation pathway coupling them to organic optical molecules to form nanohybrids is described, enabling tunable electroluminescence properties of LEDs fabricated from such materials.

rows.title: A skin-permeable polymer for non-invasive transdermal insulin delivery
rows.summary: The fast skin-permeable polyzwitterion poly[2-( N -oxide- N,N -dimethylamino)ethyl methacrylate] may enable non-invasive transdermal delivery of insulin, and potentially facilitate the use of other protein- and peptide-based therapeutics through transdermal delivery.

rows.title: Topological nodal i -wave superconductivity in PtBi 2
rows.summary: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy shows that Weyl semimetal PtBi 2 harbours nodes in its superconducting gap, implying unconventional i -wave pairing symmetry.

rows.title: Rare microbial relict sheds light on an ancient eukaryotic supergroup
rows.summary: The discovery of an unusual protist named Solarion arienae , which has a mitochondrial genome with some intriguing features, provides insight into the early radiation of eukaryotic groups.

rows.title: Genetic elements promote retention of extrachromosomal DNA in cancer cells
rows.summary: A combination of genome-wide functional screening, imaging and chromatin profiling identifies a new class of highly prevalent genomic elements that help retain extrachromosomal DNA copies in dividing cells and persist across generations.

rows.title: Shared and language-specific phonological processing in the human temporal lobe
rows.summary: The human superior temporal gyrus processes acoustic–phonetic properties of speech regardless of whether the language is familiar to the listener, but only encodes word boundaries and language-specific sound sequences if the language is known.

rows.title: Panels of peers are needed to gauge AI’s trustworthiness — experts are not enough

rows.title: Google DeepMind won a Nobel prize for AI: can it produce the next big breakthrough?

rows.title: AI has a democracy problem — here’s why

rows.title: Daily briefing: This enigmatic figure reveals a common ancient myth

rows.title: Fall-prevention clinical trial in rural China shows promising results

rows.title: Introducing the j-metric: a true measure of what matters in academia

rows.title: Sinking cities: how China is moving subsidence research forward

rows.title: James Watson obituary: co-discoverer of DNA’s double helix who reshaped modern biology

rows.title: Multi-omics analysis of a pig-to-human decedent kidney xenotransplant

rows.title: Physiology and immunology of a pig-to-human decedent kidney xenotransplant

rows.title: The future of ageing: science aims to deliver another leap in lifespan

rows.title: How much protein do you really need? What the science says

rows.title: Extreme rainfall poses the biggest risk to Mumbai’s most vulnerable people
rows.summary: An assessment of death rates in India’s coastal megacity of Mumbai reveals the impact of rain, high tides and flooding. Climate change will probably exacerbate the effects.

rows.title: Global greenhouse-gas emissions are still rising: when will they peak?
rows.summary: Scientists say emissions could begin to decline in the next several years. What happens in China could determine when.

rows.title: Can UK science really spawn a $1-trillion company?

rows.title: Mathematicians put AI model AlphaProof to the test

rows.title: Influential list of highly cited researchers now shuts out more scientists: here’s why

rows.title: Material system enhances superconducting qubits
rows.summary: In the development of large-scale quantum processors, material improvements yield rapid progress because they can be readily translated to many devices and platforms. This work shows that, if they are built from tantalum and silicon, superconducting qubits can have millisecond-scale lifetimes and coherence times and reduced fabrication-related contamination.

rows.title: Could humans live to 150? Why some researchers think we’re on the cusp of a major longevity breakthrough

rows.title: Ultrathin films of a 2D polymer provide airtight seal

rows.title: Official statistics are vastly undercounting deaths from extreme weather

rows.title: Is ageing a disease? The debate that could reshape medicine

rows.title: To reform universities, first tackle global rankings
rows.summary: Universities are in thrall to a rankings system that prioritizes narrow aspects of academic life. Three changes would give institutions the freedom to explore fresh ways of working.

rows.title: Metabolite maps reveal spatial gradients in liver and intestinal tissue
rows.summary: The abundances and fluxes of metabolite molecules were measured at cellular resolution in the mouse liver and small intestine. The levels of most metabolites showed considerable gradients in both organs. Furthermore, intake of the sugar fructose triggered depletion of ATP molecules at foci in the liver.

rows.title: Daily briefing: The first person to be cited one million times is an AI trailblazer

rows.title: Chinese researchers reveal unexplored section of mysterious Arctic Ocean ridge

rows.title: First new type of malaria treatment in decades shows promise against drug resistance

rows.title: Controlling pyramidal nitrogen chirality by asymmetric organocatalysis

rows.title: In situ structural mechanism of epothilone-B-induced CNS axon regeneration
rows.summary: A combined cryo-electron tomography and cryo-electron microscopy pipeline was developed to inflict axonal damage and monitor the cellular response induced by epothilone B, revealing that microtubule polymerization at and beyond the lesion site promote axon regeneration.

rows.title: Ecology and spread of the North American H5N1 epizootic
rows.summary: The panzootic of highly pathogenic H5N1 since 2021 was driven by around nine introductions into the Atlantic and Pacific flyways, followed by rapid dissemination through wild migratory birds, primarily Anseriformes.

rows.title: Estimation and mapping of the missing heritability of human phenotypes
rows.summary: WGS data were used from 347,630 individuals with European ancestry in the UK Biobank to obtain high-precision estimates of coding and non-coding rare variant heritability for 34 complex traits and diseases.

rows.title: Spatial fibroblast niches define Crohn’s fistulae
rows.summary: Spatial transcriptomic analysis of cells in intestinal fistulae of patients with Crohn’s disease reveals the existence of specialized fistula-associated cell states with distinct signalling profiles and extracellular matrix architecture.

rows.title: Florigen activation complex forms via multifaceted assembly in Arabidopsis
rows.summary: In flowering plants, DNA–FD–14-3-3 recruits FT to the florigen activation complex both through DNA–FT interactions and by reducing liquid phase condensation of FD protein, which promotes dimerization, leading to FT recruitment.

rows.title: The contribution of rock strength to soil production
rows.summary: Findings from a tectonically active mountain range show that soil production is driven by bottom-up rock weakening rather than by soil thickness, challenging long-held top-down models.

rows.title: Mortality impacts of rainfall and sea-level rise in a developing megacity
rows.summary: High-resolution rainfall, tide and mortaility data are used to quantify the impact of rainfall and flooding on urban health in Mumbai, India, revealing an order-of-magnitude discrepency between observed and officially reported mortality impacts, with slum residents bearing most of the burden.

rows.title: Aligning machine and human visual representations across abstraction levels
rows.summary: Aligning foundation models with human judgments enables them to more accurately approximate human behaviour and uncertainty across various levels of visual abstraction, while additionally improving their generalization performance.

rows.title: Photoinduced twist and untwist of moiré superlattices
rows.summary: Femtosecond photoexcitation drives a coherent twist–untwist motion of the moiré superlattice in 2° and 57° twisted WSe 2 /MoSe 2 heterobilayers.

rows.title: A universal speed limit for spreading of coherence
rows.summary: Experiments reveal a speed limit for the spreading of spatial coherence during the formation of a weakly interacting Bose–Einstein condensate.

rows.title: Silicon solar cells with hybrid back contacts
rows.summary: Silicon solar cells with hybrid interdigitated back contacts have a power conversion efficiency approaching 95% of the theoretical limit and a fill factor approaching 98% of the theoretical limit.

rows.title: Rare genetic variants confer a high risk of ADHD and implicate neuronal biology
rows.summary: An analysis of rare genetic variants identifies three genes— MAP1A , ANO8 and ANK2 —that have a role in attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and investigates the potential underlying biological mechanisms.

rows.title: Synthesis of enantioenriched atropisomers by biocatalytic deracemization
rows.summary: A new method for deracemization of atropisomers is described which leverages a P450 enzyme-mediated process involving bond rotation for enantioenrichment.

rows.title: An ancient recombination desert is a speciation supergene in placental mammals
rows.summary: Deep learning methods identified a large and evolutionarily conserved X-linked low recombination region in placental mammals that serves as both a barrier to gene flow in hybridizing lineages and an accurate phylogenomic marker.

rows.title: A molecularly impermeable polymer from two-dimensional polyaramids
rows.summary: Two-dimensional polyaramid polymers are synthesized to form nanofilms that exhibit the lowest gas permeability of any polymer by orders of magnitude, despite lacking crystallinity, enabling molecular-scale nanomechanical resonators and barrier materials.

rows.title: Cytosolic acetyl-coenzyme A is a signalling metabolite to control mitophagy
rows.summary: Acetyl-coenzyme A functions as a non-canonical signal to trigger mitophagy, and the acetyl-coenzyme A–NLRX1 axis underlies the KRAS-inhibitor-induced mitophagy response and promotes drug resistance, providing a metabolic mechanism of KRAS inhibitor resistance.

rows.title: Potent neutralization of Marburg virus by a vaccine-elicited antibody
rows.summary: A newly developed monoclonal antibody, MARV16, broadly neutralizes all Marburg virus isolates and provides effective protection in guinea pigs with Marburg virus disease.

rows.title: GREGoR: accelerating genomics for rare diseases
rows.summary: The GREGoR consortium provides foundational resources and substrates for the future of rare disease genomics.

rows.title: Viral NblA proteins negatively affect oceanic cyanobacterial photosynthesis
rows.summary: Viral NblA accelerates the cyanophage infection cycle, directs degradation of the host phycobilisome and other proteins, and reduces host photosynthetic light-harvesting efficiency.

rows.title: Radio burst from a stellar coronal mass ejection
rows.summary: An analogue to a type II burst from the early M dwarf StKM 1-1262 exhibits identical frequency, time and polarization properties to fundamental plasma emission from a solar type II burst.

rows.title: iPEX enables micrometre-resolution deep spatial proteomics via tissue expansion
rows.summary: Isotropic tissue magnification is integrated with matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry imaging to enable untargeted spatial proteomics at micrometre resolution and with high protein identification rates in multiple tissue types.

rows.title: Emerging climate impact on carbon sinks in a consolidated carbon budget
rows.summary: A re-assessment of the global carbon budget shows the natural land sink is substantially smaller than previously estimated, indicating emerging impacts of climate change on the evolution of the carbon sinks.

rows.title: Convergent genome evolution shaped the emergence of terrestrial animals
rows.summary: Comparisons of 154 genomes from 21 animal phyla and outgroups have been used to reconstruct ancestral adaptation to life on land across 11 distinct terrestrialization events, revealing strong evidence for convergent genomic evolution across the animal kingdom and recurring periods of terrestrial colonization.

rows.title: SIGLEC12 mediates plasma membrane rupture during necroptotic cell death
rows.summary: CRISPR–Cas9-based genome-wide screening shows that SIGLEC12 mediates plasma membrane rupture in cells undergoing necroptosis, possibly through a human-specific mechanism, indicating its potential as a therapeutic target.

rows.title: Partnerships between academia and industry must serve the public good
COP meetings must evolve to turn climate promises into action
Insatiable squirrel ravages cherry blossoms for breakfast
rows.summary: A mischievous red squirrel wreaks havoc on a woodland in search of snacks, and a record of life blooming on the volcanic island of Surtsey, in our weekly dip in Nature ’s archives.

rows.title: Kenya’s black rhino revival is a story of hope for conservationists
Academic freedom is key to the future of universities
Be rational: chimp decision-making is guided by the strongest evidence
rows.summary: The ability to change your mind in response to better evidence is a hallmark of human cognition. Experiments now show that chimps are capable of rational thought too.

rows.title: Failure is not an option for Africa’s newly launched medicines agency
rows.summary: The inequitable distribution of vaccines during the COVID-19 pandemic was the final proof of the need for more home-grown manufacturing and regulatory capacity across Africa.

rows.title: Is HRT in menopause healthy? US label change triggers debate
rows.summary: The US FDA is removing serious health warnings from hormone replacement therapies. Scientists worry that more work is needed to get the message right.

rows.title: For real climate action, empower women
rows.summary: In Belize, women are tackling climate change and biodiversity loss on the ground, but gender equity is needed in government, too — COP30 should address this.

rows.title: Lessons from a long road to a first-author paper
rows.summary: Unlike my colleagues, I faced a five-year wait to publish my PhD project. Here’s how I coped.

rows.title: The computers that run on human brain cells
rows.summary: Move over silicon: scientists want to use neurons to make powerful computers with minuscule energy needs.

rows.title: I have Einstein, Bohr and Feynman in my pocket
rows.summary: Grappling with difficulties in your career? Try asking an AI-powered advisory panel of experts, suggests Carsten Lund Pedersen.

rows.title: China’s new scientist visa is a ‘serious bid’ for the world’s top talent
rows.summary: The country is easing migration for young researchers to boost its competitiveness in artificial intelligence, robotics and new materials.

rows.title: ‘Almost utopian’: how protecting the environment is boosting the economy in Brazil
rows.summary: This bold approach could galvanize countries attending the COP30 summit.

rows.title: Ethically sourced image data set encourages fairness in AI research
rows.summary: AI systems rely on data that often lack diversity, perpetuate biases and violate intellectual-property rights. An ethical human-image data set addresses these problems.

rows.title: Daily briefing: The Americas have lost their measles elimination status
rows.summary: A year-long outbreak of measles in Canada negates the country’s disease-free status. Plus, the benefits of being multilingual and computers that run on human brains.

rows.title: How genetically encoded sensors have lit up neuroscience
rows.summary: Tools that track specific molecules in neurons have enabled researchers to probe previously unexplored aspects of neurobiology — although important caveats remain.

rows.title: Comprehensive echocardiogram evaluation with view primed vision language AI
rows.summary: EchoPrime, a video-based foundation artificial intelligence model for echocardiography, is presented.

rows.title: High-performance tandem perovskite LEDs through interlayer photon recycling
rows.summary: Stacking perovskite LEDs in tandem structures to combine the luminance of individual units yielded efficiencies greater than the summed efficiencies of equivalent single-unit devices, suggested to result from photon recycling between individual light-emitting elements.

rows.title: Author Correction: The oldest known lepidosaur and origins of lepidosaur feeding adaptations
Witnessing chamois populations recover
rows.summary: Haritakis Papaioannou combines a mountaineer’s know-how with a scientific eye to track the slow recovery of chamois populations in western Greece.

rows.title: Want a younger brain? Learn another language
rows.summary: A vast study suggests that being multilingual can slow down cognitive ageing.

rows.title: Africa finally has its own drug-regulation agency — and it could transform the continent’s health
rows.summary: If it gets things right, the first major regulator of medicines to launch for 30 years could empower Africa to tackle African challenges around health and disease.

rows.title: Hamilton Smith obituary: molecular biologist who co-discovered precise molecular scissors for cutting DNA
rows.summary: Nobel laureate who helped to sequence the first bacterial and human genomes.

rows.title: Publisher Correction: Radiation-induced amphiregulin drives tumour metastasis
Daily briefing: The complex legacy of James Watson
rows.summary: How James Watson changed the world, and how it all went wrong. Plus, the African Medicines Agency might transform the continent’s health and a surprising feature of a familiar galaxy.

rows.title: Rebuilding Ukraine — one university’s bold vision
rows.summary: Rector and AI researcher Nataliya Shakhovska tells Nature how her institution is supporting students and staff members amid the war and about her hopes for the future.

rows.title: Don’t despair, collective action can address climate change
rows.summary: Even small acts can make a big difference in driving positive environmental impacts.

rows.title: Vaccine advice based on science: US centre fills gaps in public-health information
rows.summary: Epidemiologist Michael Osterholm talks about efforts by the Center for Infectious Disease Research and Policy to inform vaccine recommendations and maintain public-health awareness during the Trump administration.

rows.title: A fault-tolerant neutral-atom architecture for universal quantum computation
rows.summary: Reconfigurable arrays of up to 448 neutral atoms are used to implement and combine the key elements of a universal, fault-tolerant quantum processing architecture and experimentally explore their underlying working mechanisms.

rows.title: Flexible perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells with 33.6% efficiency
rows.summary: A certified flexible perovskite/crystalline silicon tandem solar cell has efficiencies rivalling its rigid counterparts and demonstrates exceptional mechanical robustness and stability.

rows.title: Flexible perovskite/silicon tandem solar cell with a dual-buffer layer
rows.summary: A flexible perovskite/silicon tandem solar cell making use of a dual-buffer layer comprising a compact SnO x layer deposited first followed by a loose SnO x layer is described, showing efficiencies rivalling rigid counterparts and good durability.

rows.title: DNA pioneer James Watson has died ― colleagues wrestle with his legacy
rows.summary: The co-discoverer of the structure of DNA helped to strengthen a US research institute and wrote a classic textbook, but also earned a reputation for racist and sexist comments.

rows.title: Surprise ‘tail’ found on an iconic galaxy may rewrite its history
rows.summary: First image from Vera C. Rubin telescope reveals a previously unverified feature of galaxy M61 that may explain its mysterious properties.

rows.title: A host of ‘exocomets’ swarms a distant star
rows.summary: Dimming of the starlight from RZ Piscium reveals that 24 unseen bodies are whizzing around the star.

rows.title: Preprint site arXiv is banning computer-science reviews: here’s why
rows.summary: The repository is taking steps to tackle a surge in low quality, AI-generated content.

rows.title: Pressure to publish is rising as research time shrinks, finds survey of scientists
rows.summary: Researchers feel that pressures to publish are increasing, but the time and resources available to do research are decreasing, according to a survey by Elsevier.

rows.title: Outside the window
rows.summary: A life well lived.

rows.title: How scientists exposed to other people’s trauma find support
rows.summary: Vicarious trauma is an occupational risk for some researchers. But there are strategies to cope.

rows.title: Daily briefing: A ‘Google Maps’ for Roman roads
rows.summary: The full glory of the network of roads that connected the Roman empire. Plus, meet some of the scientists running for public office in the United States and how a tiny tyrannosaur is putting a palaeontological controversy to bed.

rows.title: International PhD student numbers in US hold steady — for now
rows.summary: Trend flies in face of Trump-administration policies, but could yet see a rapid decrease, especially in science fields.

rows.title: Author Correction: The emergence of transcriptional identity in somatosensory neurons
Author Correction: TNF-mediated inflammatory skin disease in mice with epidermis-specific deletion of IKK2
Shadow scholars: inside Kenya’s multibillion-dollar fake-essay industry
rows.summary: Sociologist Patricia Kingori is helping to expose contract cheating by scholars in high-income countries.

rows.title: ‘Google Maps’ for Roman roads reveals vast extent of ancient network
rows.summary: A high-resolution digital map nearly doubles the known length of the ancient road network.

rows.title: Daily briefing: ‘Mind captioning’ AI describes the images in your head
rows.summary: AI model can translate scenes in your head into sentences. Plus, iguanas were wrongly accused of invading a Mexican island and the ‘shadow scholars’ paid to write for others.

rows.title: First-ever atlas of brain development shows how stem cells turn into neurons
rows.summary: A collection of studies that chart how mammalian brain cells grow and differentiate is a ‘very valuable’ tool for neuroscientists.

rows.title: An ATP-gated molecular switch orchestrates human mRNA export
rows.summary: The ATPase UAP56 acts as an ATP-gated molecular switch that directs mRNA ribonucleoprotein complexes from TREX to nuclear-pore-complex-anchored TREX-2 complexes for mRNA export from the nucleus.

rows.title: Meet the ‘Wee-rex’. Tiny tyrannosaur is its own species
rows.summary: Growth rings in fossilized bones suggest the diminutive dinosaur, Nanotyrannus , would never grow up to become a T. rex — plus, a small breast cancer prevention trial shows promise.

rows.title: Antibody drugs show promise for treating bird flu and HIV
rows.summary: Scientists are developing antibodies to track the evolution of these viruses and better treat infections.

rows.title: Anosophoros
rows.summary: Parting gifts.

rows.title: Ultrashort laser pulse amplified by back-and-forth propagation
rows.summary: It is challenging to generate ultrashort laser pulses at high powers, but repeatedly overlapping light pulses in a crystal can efficiently amplify a weak signal.

rows.title: Daily briefing: UK science is ‘bleeding to death’, says report
rows.summary: Failures to scale and retain the economic benefits of research in the United Kingdom are killing the country’s science sector, say lawmakers. Plus, how AI might influence how we define creativity and the biggest black-hole outburst ever seen.

rows.title: Chinese scientists increasingly lead joint projects with the UK, US and Europe
rows.summary: Although China needs to strengthen its leadership in artificial intelligence, semiconductors and energy, say researchers.

rows.title: Most Antarctic ice shelves are set to disappear if greenhouse-gas emissions remain high
rows.summary: The time points beyond which individual Antarctic ice shelves could no longer exist in their current form have been estimated under several anthropogenic emission scenarios. These projections take into account uncertainties related to ice, atmosphere and ocean processes, including those concerning poorly understood processes such as ice fracturing and iceberg formation.

rows.title: ‘Mind-captioning’ AI decodes brain activity to turn thoughts into text
rows.summary: A non-invasive imaging technique can translate scenes in your head into sentences. It could help to reveal how the brain interprets the world.

rows.title: Dispersion-engineered multipass optical parametric amplification
rows.summary: A multipass optical parametric amplifier leverages dispersion-engineered dielectric mirrors to overcome the gain versus bandwidth trade-off and achieve broadband amplification with high gain within a compact device.

rows.title: Myriad aryne derivatives from carboxylic acids
rows.summary: An aryne precursor is designed to overcome the lack of widespread adoption of arynes due to the undesirable means to generate them and harness their synthetic potential that rivals most functional groups.

rows.title: Images for AI use can be sourced responsibly
rows.summary: A high-quality image data set shows that tech companies can obtain informed consent and avoid data bias without breaking the bank.

rows.title: Can AI be truly creative?
rows.summary: Chatbots and AI models are challenging ideas about who — or what — can create art, music and more.

rows.title: Developmental maps of the brain trace when cell types emerge
rows.summary: A large consortium of researchers has mapped how brain cells establish diverse identities throughout neurodevelopment and across species.

rows.title: Targeting FSP1 triggers ferroptosis in lung cancer
rows.summary: The ferroptosis suppressor protein FSP1 has a critical role in ferroptosis protection of tumours across multiple in vivo models and is linked to worse prognosis in human lung adenocarcinoma, suggesting its potential as a therapeutic target in lung cancer.

rows.title: Secretome translation shaped by lysosomes and lunapark-marked ER junctions
