rows.title: Active energy compression of a laser-plasma electron beam
rows.summary: A laser-plasma electron beam generated using active energy compression demonstrates reduction in energy spread and jitter by an order of magnitude to below the permille level, comparable with modern radio-frequency accelerators.

rows.title: Swinging lever mechanism of myosin directly shown by time-resolved cryo-EM
rows.summary: A study using time-resolved cryogenic electron microscopy reveals the swinging lever mechanism of myosin, providing information on the molecular basis behind the production of force and movement by myosin.

rows.title: Foundation model of neural activity predicts response to new stimulus types
rows.summary: A foundation model trained on neural activity of visual cortex from multiple mice accurately predicts responses to video stimuli and cell types, dendritic features and connectivity within the MICrONS functional connectomics dataset.

rows.title: Leaf absorption contributes to accumulation of microplastics in plants
rows.summary: Absorption and accumulation of atmospheric microplastics by plant leaves occurs widely in the environment.

rows.title: Phenotypic complexities of rare heterozygous neurexin-1 deletions
rows.summary: How NRXN1 variants affect multiple neuropsychiatric disorders is explored.

rows.title: Human assembloid model of the ascending neural sensory pathway
rows.summary: A human ascending somatosensory assembloid model was developed, which integrates multiple organoids to simulate the spinothalamic pathway, demonstrating functional connectivity and responsiveness to stimuli and revealing insights into pain-related genetic mutations.

rows.title: Perisomatic ultrastructure efficiently classifies cells in mouse cortex
rows.summary: An analysis demonstrates that quantitative measurements of perisomatic ultrastructure features of neurons can be used to categorize them into cell types.

rows.title: Comprehensive interrogation of synthetic lethality in the DNA damage response
rows.summary: Combinatorial CRISPRi screening was used to map genetic interactions in DNA damage response pathways, revealing known and new connections, including the roles of WDR48 and USP1 in preventing under-replication and SMARCAL1 and FANCM in remodelling persistent cruciform DNA structures.

rows.title: Seismic imaging of a basaltic Lesser Antilles slab from ancient tectonics
rows.summary: Imaging of the mantle transition zone beneath the Lesser Antilles shows a basalt-rich region within the subducting slab near the proposed location of a subducted extinct spreading ridge, implying ancient tectonics play a role in influencing slab trajectories.

rows.title: Giant electrocaloric effect in high-polar-entropy perovskite oxides
rows.summary: Targeted multielement substitution of a lead-free relaxor ferroelectric perovskite distorts the lattice structure and induces strong polar disorder, leading to high-polar-entropy ferroelectric oxides with a high electrocaloric effect and long lifetime.

rows.title: A non-contact wearable device for monitoring epidermal molecular flux
rows.summary: A non-contact wearable device that defines and modulates a microclimate adjacent to the skin can measure incoming and outgoing streams of vapourized substances, offering valuable insights into physiological health, wound healing and environmental exposures.

rows.title: Reprogramming site-specific retrotransposon activity to new DNA sites
rows.summary: A study of retrotransposon activity repurposes a retroelement called R2 Tocc to create a programmable system called STITCHR that enables diverse genome edits including efficient, scarless large payload insertions.

rows.title: Hunter-gatherer sea voyages extended to remotest Mediterranean islands
rows.summary: Archaeological discoveries from Malta suggest that humans were present on the Maltese islands from around 8,500 years ago, providing evidence that Mesolithic hunter-gatherers made sea crossings as long as 100 km.

rows.title: NEURD offers automated proofreading and feature extraction for connectomics
rows.summary: Neural Decomposition (NEURD) is a software package that decomposes neuronal data from high-resolution electron microscopy volumes into feature-rich graph representations to facilitate analysis for neuroscience research.

rows.title: Complete sequencing of ape genomes
rows.summary: Complete sequences of chromosomes telomere-to-telomere from chimpanzee, bonobo, gorilla, Bornean orangutan, Sumatran orangutan and siamang provide a comprehensive and valuable resource for future evolutionary comparisons.

rows.title: DNA-guided transcription factor interactions extend human gene regulatory code
rows.summary: A large-scale analysis of DNA-bound transcription factors (TFs) shows how the presence of DNA markedly affects the landscape of TF interactions, and identifies composite motifs that are recognized by complexes of TFs rather than by individual ones.

rows.title: Goal-specific hippocampal inhibition gates learning
rows.summary: Parvalbumin-positive interneurons in the hippocampal CA3 substantially reduce firing on approach to and at goal locations while food-deprived mice learn to find food.

rows.title: Transforming ceria into 2D clusters enhances catalytic activity
rows.summary: Treatment of supported ceria nanoparticles at high temperature in gasoline vehicle exhaust/steam results in their dispersion into atomically thin oxide domains with enhanced oxygen mobility and storage capacity.

rows.title: Inhibitory specificity from a connectomic census of mouse visual cortex
rows.summary: Using volumetric electron microscopy, the authors map and analyze the structure of cortical inhibition with synaptic resolution across a column of visual cortex.

rows.title: Water abundance in the lunar farside mantle
rows.summary: An estimate of water abundance in the lunar mantle indicates that the farside mantle is potentially drier than its nearside counterpart.

rows.title: Small molecules restore mutant mitochondrial DNA polymerase activity
rows.summary: An activator of DNA polymerase γ restores function to disease-causing mutant variants and demonstrates a potential route to treatments for inherited mitochondrial disorders involving POLG mutations.

rows.title: Translational genomics of osteoarthritis in 1,962,069 individuals
rows.summary: A genome-wide association study meta-analysis combined with multiomics data of osteoarthritis identifies 700 effector genes as well as biological processes with a convergent involvement of multiple effector genes; 10% of these genes express the target of approved drugs.

rows.title: Functional connectomics spanning multiple areas of mouse visual cortex
rows.summary: Dense calcium imaging combined with co-registered high-resolution electron microscopy reconstruction of the brain of the same mouse provide a functional connectomics map of tens of thousands of neurons of a region of the primary cortex and higher visual areas.

rows.title: A Jurassic acanthocephalan illuminates the origin of thorny-headed worms
rows.summary: An acanthocephalan body fossil, Juracanthocephalus daohugouensis , is described from the Middle Jurassic Daohugou biota of China, showing previously unrecognized diversity in ancient Acanthocephala and the origins of this group of living organisms.

rows.title: Evidence of star cluster migration and merger in dwarf galaxies
rows.summary: High-resolution images from the Hubble Space Telescope show evidence of star cluster migration and merger in dwarf galaxies.

rows.title: Stress dynamically modulates neuronal autophagy to gate depression onset
rows.summary: Acute stress activates autophagy in the lateral habenula, whereas chronic stress suppresses it, with this autophagy having a causal role in maintaining emotional homeostasis against stress, and its restoration through autophagy enhancers offers a novel antidepressant strategy.

rows.title: Universal photonic artificial intelligence acceleration
rows.summary: A photonic processor capable of running advanced artificial intelligence models with near-electronic precision is introduced, marking a substantial step towards post-transistor computing technologies.

rows.title: Recurrent humid phases in Arabia over the past 8 million years
rows.summary: A climatic record from desert speleothems shows that the central Arabian interior experienced recurrent humid intervals over the past 8 million years, which likely facilitated mammalian dispersals between Africa and Eurasia.

rows.title: Intersectional analysis for science and technology
rows.summary: This Perspective offers a guide for researchers, peer-reviewed journals and funding agencies to make quantitative intersectional approaches a standard part of science and technology research design, where relevant, in efforts to enhance precision in science, and ultimately global equity and environmental sustainability.

rows.title: Multimodal cell maps as a foundation for structural and functional genomics
rows.summary: A global map of human subcellular architecture yields protein complex structures, reveals protein functions, identifies assemblies with multiple localizations or cell-type specificity and decodes paediatric cancer genomes.

rows.title: Supramolecular docking structure determination of alkyl-bearing molecules
rows.summary: A metal–organic framework (MOF)–pillar[5]arene hybrid can bind small molecules with long alkyl chains, such that single-crystal structures of the host–guest complexes can be obtained and therefore small molecular structures determined.

rows.title: Towards conversational diagnostic artificial intelligence
rows.summary: The conversational diagnostic artificial intelligence system AMIE (Articulate Medical Intelligence Explorer) has potential as a real-world tool for clinical history-taking and diagnostic dialogue, based on its performance in simulated consultations.

rows.title: An integrated large-scale photonic accelerator with ultralow latency
rows.summary: A large-scale photonic accelerator comprising more than 16,000 components integrated on a single chip to process MAC operations is described, demonstrating ultralow latency and reduced computing time compared with a commercially available GPU.

rows.title: Spatial multi-omics reveals cell-type-specific nuclear compartments
rows.summary: A genomic barcoding scheme called two-layer DNA seqFISH+ enables the simultaneous mapping of more than 100,000 loci and has been used to identify cell-type-specific subnuclear compartments in the mouse brain.

rows.title: Functional connectomics reveals general wiring rule in mouse visual cortex
rows.summary: The MICrONS mouse visual cortex dataset shows that neurons with similar response properties preferentially connect, a pattern that emerges within and across brain areas and layers, and independently emerges in artificial neural networks where these ‘like-to-like’ connections prove important for task performance.

rows.title: Timing and trajectory of BCR::ABL1- driven chronic myeloid leukaemia
rows.summary: Explosive growth is attributed to the BCR::ABL1 gene 3–14 years before diagnosis of chronic myeloid leukaemia, highlighting the oncogenic potency of gene fusion and the slow and sequential trajectories of most other cancers.

rows.title: The US is against the world on sustainable development
Cannabis studies were informing fundamental neuroscience in the 1970s
rows.summary: Research on cannabis was hotting up 50 years ago, and accessible lectures on the physics of matter from Nobel laureate William Bragg, in this week’s dip into Nature ’s archive.

rows.title: Europe must grasp chance to become a scientific powerhouse
Europe needs to step up on epidemic preparedness
Countries must consider their global footprint when using natural resources
‘Now is not the time for despair’ — how scientists can take a stand against political interference
rows.summary: Lessons from environmental and other social movements can help researchers to protect scientific integrity from attack.

rows.title: NSF slashes prestigious PhD fellowship awards by half
rows.summary: US National Science Foundation announces lowest number of Graduate Research Fellowship Program recipients in 15 years.

rows.title: 154 million lives and counting: 5 charts reveal the power of vaccines
rows.summary: But public-health specialists worry that misinformation and funding cuts could affect vaccination rates.

rows.title: Science’s big problem is a loss of influence, not a loss of trust
rows.summary: Evidence shows that science and scientists remain highly trusted. But genuine scientific voices are not shouting loud enough over the noise to hold sway.

rows.title: Norway set to scrap mandatory language training for foreign postdocs and PhD students
rows.summary: Researchers jubilant over swift ministerial response to rule they say would hamper international recruitment.

rows.title: Asilomar conference took courage and foresight — today, inclusivity would also be crucial
rows.summary: The 50th anniversary of a landmark biosafety conference is an opportunity to ensure its spirit lives on in today’s scientists.

rows.title: Daily briefing: Long-COVID activists fought Trump research cuts and won ― for now
rows.summary: Long-COVID advocates in the United States have managed to get millions of dollars in grants cancelled by the Trump administration restored. Plus, the origin of mpox might be a squirrel native to Africa and how vaccines have saved 154 million lives.

rows.title: Cells are swapping their mitochondria. What does this mean for our health?
rows.summary: Researchers are studying why the energy factories are moving between cells and whether the process can be harnessed to treat cancer and other diseases.

rows.title: An animal source of mpox emerges — and it’s a squirrel
rows.summary: Researchers solve the mystery of a disease outbreak through long-term surveillance of wildlife in Africa.

rows.title: Does US science have a future in Antarctica? Trump cuts threaten to cancel fieldwork and more
rows.summary: Funding for the National Science Foundation, which finances research at US bases on the icy continent, has already been reduced, and the agency faces steeper cuts soon.

rows.title: Tiger turnaround as populations grow in India
rows.summary: Tiger numbers in India are starting to rebound after decades of being perilously low. This recovery offers lessons for conserving other rare animals.

rows.title: A Nd@C 82 –polymer interface for efficient and stable perovskite solar cells
rows.summary: An endohedral metallofullerene–polymer layer, which features ultrafast electron extraction and in situ encapsulation, improves the efficiency and stability of perovskite solar cells.

rows.title: Author Correction: Recapitulation of premature ageing with iPSCs from Hutchinson–Gilford progeria syndrome
Studying seabirds with a cactus as a research assistant
rows.summary: Ecologist Cecilia Soldatini tracks the movements of magnificent frigatebirds.

rows.title: From Hippocrates to COVID-19: the scientific fight to prove diseases can be airborne
rows.summary: Science journalist and author Carl Zimmer joins us to talk about his new book Air-borne.

rows.title: We’ve misunderstood Uranus all these years
rows.summary: Hubble Space Telescope data show that the time taken for the planet to revolve around its axis is almost half a minute longer than was thought.

rows.title: Why more AI researchers should collaborate with governments
rows.summary: Academics can drive policy innovation — but they must shift their focus from publishing papers to creating practical products.

rows.title: Creating an ‘all comers’ research group in quantitative history
rows.summary: Nathan Alexander's laboratory welcomes ‘anyone and everyone’ to use a mix of mathematics and computing to solve challenges in society.

rows.title: AI for research: the ultimate guide to choosing the right tool
rows.summary: Curious about using artificial intelligence to boost your research? Here are the programs you shouldn’t miss.

rows.title: Long COVID activists fought Trump team’s research cuts and won ― for now
rows.summary: Success gives hope to scientists and advocates who managed to get millions of dollars in grants restored.

rows.title: AI race in 2025 is tighter than ever before
rows.summary: State of the industry report also shows that 2024 was a breakthrough year for small, sleek models to rival the behemoths.

rows.title: Where do proteins go in cells? Next-generation methods map the molecules’ hidden lives
rows.summary: Spatial proteomics is helping biologists to uncover how cells work by mapping where proteins operate.

rows.title: Why an overreliance on AI-driven modelling is bad for science
rows.summary: Without clear protocols to catch errors, artificial intelligence’s growing role in science could do more harm than good.

rows.title: Daily briefing: The physicist behind baseball’s new ‘torpedo’ bat
rows.summary: Meet Aaron Leanhardt, a physicist-turned-hitting coordinator for the New York Yankees. Plus, the top US vaccine regulator was pressured to provide conspiracy-confirming data and the winners of this year’s Breakthrough Prizes.

rows.title: Obesity-drug pioneers and 13,508 physicists win US$3-million Breakthrough Prizes
rows.summary: Advances recognized by science’s most lucrative awards include Large Hadron Collider experiments and groundbreaking weight-loss treatments.

rows.title: Author Correction: Record sea surface temperature jump in 2023–2024 unlikely but not unexpected
Revealed: where rare and giant starfish hide from an enigmatic killer
rows.summary: The sunflower star, which can be bigger than a hubcap, escapes a wasting disease by hunkering down in fjords.

rows.title: Neck deep in overdiagnosis: Books in brief
rows.summary: Andrew Robinson reviews five of the best science picks.

rows.title: Author Correction: Traversable wormhole dynamics on a quantum processor
Trump team removes senior NIH chiefs in shock move
rows.summary: Decision comes amidst mass layoffs — plus, administration instructs US biomedical agency to study ‘regret’ after transgender people transition.

rows.title: Tariffs hit science labs: Trump’s levies raise cost of supplies
rows.summary: Import taxes on staples such as microscopes, glassware and computer chips will affect institutions already feeling financial strain.

rows.title: International PhD students make emergency plans in fear of US immigration raids
rows.summary: Arrests of scholars by US President Donald Trump’s administration prompts lawsuit alleging that the government has violated the right to free speech.

rows.title: Daily briefing: This brain structure filters which thoughts we become aware of
rows.summary: Neuroscientists have observed how deep-brain structures are activated when the brain becomes aware of its own thoughts. Plus, the world’s tiniest pacemaker and how the Trump tariffs will affect US science labs.

rows.title: Solar cells made of Moon dust could power up a lunar base
rows.summary: Lunar soil processed to form ‘moonglass’ allows the creation of efficient, radiation-resistant solar panels.

rows.title: Take Nature ’s poll: How will Trump’s policies affect US science?
rows.summary: The new administration is reshaping the research landscape in the United States in profound ways. What do you think of all the changes?

rows.title: Strategic atom replacement enables regiocontrol in pyrazole alkylation
rows.summary: A prototypical example of a ‘strategic atom replacement’ approach enables synthesis of N -alkyl pyrazoles from isothiazoles by swapping the sulfur atom with a nitrogen atom and its associated alkyl fragment to deliver the alkylated pyrazole.

rows.title: How does the brain control consciousness? This deep-brain structure
rows.summary: In a world of constant stimulation, the thalamus filters which thoughts we become aware of and which we don’t.

rows.title: Exclusive: Trump White House directs NIH to study ‘regret’ after transgender people transition
rows.summary: After cancelling nearly all NIH projects studying transgender health, Trump’s team instructs the US biomedical agency to study negative consequences of transitioning.

rows.title: Journal targeted by paper mill still grappling with the aftermath years later
rows.summary: Dozens of problematic papers remain in the literature, after a publication hit by fraudsters pledged to tackle the issue.

rows.title: Hidden states and dynamics of fractional fillings in twisted MoTe 2 bilayers
rows.summary: Transient optical spectroscopy applied to studying twisted MoTe 2 for time-domain detection of fractional fillings of Chern bands reveals many hidden states that have not been previously observed and which could host exotic topological phases.

rows.title: World’s tiniest pacemaker could revolutionize heart surgery
rows.summary: Smaller than a grain of rice, this injectable device could allow for minimally invasive heart-surgery — plus, research suggesting that a shingles vaccination reduces the risk of dementia.

rows.title: What if human blood were toxic to mosquitoes? A drug can make it so
rows.summary: A single dose of the drug nitisinone could render a person’s blood lethal to mosquitoes for five days, modelling suggests.

rows.title: A toolkit for seeing how the fly brain’s visual system works
rows.summary: A complete inventory of the Drosophila visual system classifies about 53,000 neurons into 732 types. The shapes and connections of all the visual neurons have been quantified, and a large collection of genetically engineered fly lines have been shared, providing a comprehensive toolkit for studying fly vision.

rows.title: Are screens harming teens? What scientists can do to find answers
rows.summary: The fierce debate about smartphones and adolescent mental health rests on conflicting science. Researchers and technology companies must work to improve it.

rows.title: Photoinduced copper-catalysed deracemization of alkyl halides
rows.summary: A chiral copper catalyst, generated in situ from commercially available components, can be used to achieve photoinduced deracemization of alkyl halides through carbon–halogen bond cleavage.

rows.title: Revealed: first DNA profiles of ancient people who roamed a lush Sahara
rows.summary: The genomes of two women who lived 7,000 years ago in the Sahara when it was a green savannah reveal a remarkably isolated population.

rows.title: Sunflower ‘virgin births’ enable accelerated crop breeding
rows.summary: The discovery that sunflower seeds can develop without fertilization reveals a pathway to accelerate improvement of this crop — and potentially others.

rows.title: From bench to bread: how science can enhance your hobbies
rows.summary: Researchers describe how they are using skills honed in the laboratory in their creative pursuits.

rows.title: Daily briefing: Drug makes people’s blood poisonous to mosquitoes
rows.summary: A drug called nitisinone that is already approved to treat rare disorders can make human blood toxic to mosquitoes. Plus, what smartphones do to teens’ mental health and Trump’s cuts to HIV research.

rows.title: Light wins uphill battle to solve enduring problem in organic synthesis
rows.summary: Mirror-image isomer blends have been converted into a single isomer by a light-activated copper catalyst — a challenging reaction that prevents the waste of materials.

rows.title: Do smartphones and social media really harm teens’ mental health?
rows.summary: Researchers are debating the strength of evidence connecting technology to surging rates of adolescent mental illness. But they have some clear advice for parents.

rows.title: AI masters Minecraft : DeepMind program finds diamonds without being taught
rows.summary: The Dreamer system reached the milestone by ‘imagining’ the future impact of possible decisions.

rows.title: Intriguing features of the interface between water and oil droplets uncovered
rows.summary: Innovative experimental and computational techniques have been developed to study the interface of oil droplets suspended in water, a model system of hydrophobic interaction. These techniques reveal greater water structural disorder than in bulk water and an intense electric field at the water–oil interface.

rows.title: Unicorn slippers in space
rows.summary: Avoidance tactics.

rows.title: The neurons that mediate a psychedelic’s long-term antidepressive effects
rows.summary: Psilocybin, a classic psychedelic, has therapeutic potential for psychiatric disorders. A specific brain circuit and receptor have now been found to be required for psilocybin’s long-term effects on neural plasticity and depression-related behaviour.

rows.title: Rare ancient DNA from Sahara opens a window on the region’s verdant past
rows.summary: Sequencing of 7,000-year-old human genomes from when the Sahara Desert was green suggest that pastoralism spread through cultural exchange, not large-scale migration.

rows.title: Could the shingles vaccine help to prevent dementia?
rows.summary: Large-scale analyses of electronic health data suggest that the herpes zoster vaccine could protect against dementia — but it’s not yet clear how.

rows.title: A natural experiment on the effect of herpes zoster vaccination on dementia
rows.summary: Using a natural experiment that avoids common bias concerns, this study finds that the live-attenuated shingles vaccine reduced the probability of a new dementia diagnosis within a follow-up period of 7 years by approximately one-fifth.

rows.title: Mastering diverse control tasks through world models
rows.summary: A general reinforcement-learning algorithm, called Dreamer, outperforms specialized expert algorithms across diverse tasks by learning a model of the environment and improving its behaviour by imagining future scenarios.

rows.title: Bifidobacteria support optimal infant vaccine responses
rows.summary: Neonatal antibiotic use is shown to reduce immune response to infant vaccines, accompanied by reduced abundance of Bifidobacteria in the gut microbiota, with experiments in mice indicating that probiotic therapy could be beneficial.

rows.title: Near-field photon entanglement in total angular momentum
rows.summary: Non-classical correlations between two photons in the near-field regime give rise to entanglement in their total angular momentum, leading to a completely different structure of quantum correlations of photon pairs.

rows.title: Formation and composition of Earth’s Hadean protocrust
rows.summary: A modelling study shows that the trace-element composition of Earth’s Hadean protocrust is similar to that of the current average continental crust, severely compromising geochemical arguments for when and how plate tectonics began.

rows.title: Metal–support frontier orbital interactions in single-atom catalysis
rows.summary: The acetylene hydrogenation activity and stability of a palladium single-atom catalyst are both controlled by the lowest unoccupied molecular orbital of the oxide support.

rows.title: Millimetre-scale bioresorbable optoelectronic systems for electrotherapy
rows.summary: A millimetre-scale bioresorbable optoelectronic system with an onboard power supply and a wireless, optical control mechanism is developed for general applications in electrotherapy and specific uses in temporary cardiac pacing.

rows.title: A RISC-V 32-bit microprocessor based on two-dimensional semiconductors
rows.summary: A RISC-V microprocessor capable of executing standard 32-bit instructions has been designed with 5,900 MoS 2 transistors and a complete standard cell library based on 2D semiconductor technology.

rows.title: Psilocybin’s lasting action requires pyramidal cell types and 5-HT 2A receptors
rows.summary: A pyramidal cell type and the 5-HT 2A receptor in the medial frontal cortex have essential roles in psilocybin’s long-term drug action.

rows.title: Clinically relevant clot resolution via a thromboinflammation-on-a-chip
rows.summary: In thromboinflammation, early tissue plasminogen activator administration directly improves endothelial barrier function, prophylactic defibrotide and enoxaparin suppress microvascular thromboinflammation through endothelium-mediated mechanisms and combining enoxaparin with crizanlizumab reduces microvascular occlusion and protects endothelial function in sickle cell disease.

rows.title: A neural mechanism for learning from delayed postingestive feedback
rows.summary: Illness signals from the gut reactivate and strengthen flavour representations in the amygdala to support learning from delayed postingestive feedback.

rows.title: Global impoverishment of natural vegetation revealed by dark diversity
rows.summary: A comparison of alpha diversity (number of plant species) and dark diversity (species that are currently absent from a site despite being ecologically suitable) demonstrates the negative effects of regional-scale anthropogenic activity on plant diversity.

rows.title: Haploid facultative parthenogenesis in sunflower sexual reproduction
rows.summary: Spontaneous parthenogenesis in sunflower has been used to develop a scalable doubled haploid breeding system.

rows.title: The RAD52 double-ring remodels replication forks restricting fork reversal
rows.summary: A head-to-head double-ring complex of the human multifunctional DNA repair protein RAD52 mediates protection of stalled replication forks during replication stress, protecting them from reversal by SMARCAL1 motor.

rows.title: Acoustic modes in M67 cluster stars trace deepening convective envelopes
rows.summary: Measuring acoustic oscillations in 27 stars within the M67 cluster presents evidence of a rapidly evolving convective zone as stars evolve from subgiants to red giants.

rows.title: Ancient DNA from the Green Sahara reveals ancestral North African lineage
rows.summary: Pastoralism spread through cultural diffusion into the Green Sahara, where an isolated, distinct North African ancestry persisted.

rows.title: Minerals will shape future geopolitical order
China has already taken steps to reduce retractions of papers from its hospitals
The global scientific community must keep studying LGBT+ health
Action needed to mitigate effects of slashing USAID
How seahorses and pipefish inspired the design of a boat propeller
rows.summary: Why really good trombones sound the way they do, and the peculiar motion of creatures in the ocean, in this week’s dip into Nature ’s archive.

rows.title: Author Correction: Controlled patterning of crystalline domains by frontal polymerization
El Niños that linger are becoming less of a rarity
rows.summary: Multi-year episodes of the climatic pattern are much more frequent now than they were seven millennia ago.

rows.title: How to get rid of toxic ‘forever chemical’ pollution
rows.summary: Regulatory efforts to purge PFASs from drinking water have led to a rush for technologies that can capture and destroy the chemicals.

rows.title: CERN releases detailed plans for supercollider — but no hints about funding
rows.summary: Long-awaited report explores the practicalities of building a machine triple the size of the Large Hadron Collider.

rows.title: ‘One of the darkest days’: NIH purges agency leadership amid mass lay-offs
rows.summary: In shock move, four institute directors at the US biomedical agency are removed from their posts.

rows.title: Deadly Myanmar earthquake was probably a rare rupture, scientists say
rows.summary: ‘Supershear’ quake moved fast and far, amplifying the damage and human toll.

rows.title: A brain drain would impoverish the United States and diminish world science
rows.summary: Europe is advertising itself as a destination for embattled US scientists. It seems many are considering leaving.

rows.title: How Europe aims to woo US scientists and protect academic freedom
rows.summary: The European Union’s new research chief Ekaterina Zaharieva speaks to Nature about attracting disaffected US scientists and cutting grant bureaucracy.

rows.title: Superpowers want to control critical mineral supplies — local communities need a stronger say
rows.summary: As governments fight to regulate access to materials important for many technologies, the people mining them are left behind.

rows.title: Author Correction: Isoprene nitrates drive new particle formation in Amazon’s upper troposphere
Daily briefing: Mass layoffs across US health agencies
rows.summary: Thousands of leaders and staff are being purged at US agencies such as the NIH. Plus, the month’s best science images and how to clean up ‘forever chemicals’.

rows.title: Deep dive: How I use robots to survey coral reefs
rows.summary: Marine ecologist Gemma Galbraith builds remotely operated vehicles and uses them to assess how coral reefs are being affected by climate change.

rows.title: Brain implant translates thoughts to speech in an instant
rows.summary: Improvements to brain–computer interfaces are bringing the technology closer to natural conversational speed.

rows.title: Six roadblocks to net zero — and how to get around them
rows.summary: Overcoming these obstacles in carbon markets can speed up decarbonization.

rows.title: 23andMe plans to sell its huge genetic database: could science benefit?
rows.summary: Following the firm’s bankruptcy, researchers hope that they will still be able to access the valuable data set even if it is sold to new owners.

rows.title: Trump team guts AIDS-eradication programme and slashes HIV research grants
rows.summary: More than 200 federal grants for research related to HIV and AIDS have been abruptly terminated in the past few weeks.

rows.title: Daily briefing: What happens when you pay peer reviewers?
rows.summary: Two experiments show that small payments can speed up peer review, but there might be unintended consequences. Plus, US grant cuts are ending scientific careers and Lyft drivers’ data reveals speeding-ticket racism.

rows.title: Style over substance? What birds’ mating behaviours reveal about sexual selection
rows.summary: An exploration of weird and wonderful birds across the world sometimes takes theories of sexual selection to the extreme — but entertains throughout.

rows.title: Incredible close-up of colourful crab spiders — March’s best science images
rows.summary: The month’s sharpest science shots, selected by Nature ’s photo team.

rows.title: Audio long read: How quickly are you ageing? What molecular ‘clocks’ can tell you about your health
rows.summary: Researchers are looking to improve how ageing is measured, but the field is plagued with uncertainties.

rows.title: The best foods for healthy ageing ― and the worst
rows.summary: Study of more than 100,000 people supports your parents’ advice: eat your veggies.

rows.title: Can trauma from violence be genetically inherited? Scientists debate Syria refugee study
rows.summary: Study finds genetic imprints in three generations of Syrian refugees. Researchers urge caution in interpreting findings and call for replication.

rows.title: Publishers trial paying peer reviewers — what did they find?
rows.summary: Two journals embarked on efforts to compensate reviewers, with different results.

rows.title: These US labs risk imminent closure after Trump cuts
rows.summary: US researchers who must forage for their own salary by finding grants fear they will be the first to go as federal research dollars disappear.

rows.title: Daily briefing: Women’s work is missing from the scientific literature
rows.summary: The gender gap in research publishing is improving — but slowly. Plus, climate disasters are creating an insurance crisis and scientists discovered a promising antibiotic in a box of dirt they’d left under a lab bench for a year.

rows.title: ‘Open source’ AI isn’t truly open — here’s how researchers can reclaim the term
rows.summary: Many firms are misusing the ‘open source’ label. The scientific community, which relies on transparency and replicability, must resist this trend.

rows.title: 75% of US scientists who answered Nature poll consider leaving
rows.summary: More than 1,600 readers answered our poll; many said they were looking for jobs in Europe and Canada.

rows.title: How Trump is following Project 2025’s radical roadmap to defund science
rows.summary: Much of the Trump administration’s agenda for research is laid out in the 900-plus-page blueprint. Nature read it so you don’t have to.

rows.title: Showing ‘ability’ in ‘disability’ — how I mastered interviews while using a wheelchair
rows.summary: Learning how to influence the way people see me when I enter a room has been key to boosting my confidence in job interviews.

rows.title: Daily briefing: Pregnancy’s true toll on the body
rows.summary: A huge study paints the most detailed picture yet of the toll pregnancy and childbirth take on the body. Plus, scientists have discovered a new antibiotic in a lab technician’s garden and artificial intelligence tools are making their way into the process of peer review — to some researchers’ dismay.

rows.title: Trump’s bid for Greenland threatens to destabilize Arctic research
rows.summary: US science partnerships are on thin ice as geopolitical tensions soar.

rows.title: AlphaFold is running out of data — so drug firms are building their own version
rows.summary: Thousands of 3D protein structures locked up in big-pharma vaults will be used to create a new AI tool that won’t be open to academics.

rows.title: New lasso-shaped antibiotic kills drug-resistant bacteria
rows.summary: Antimicrobial molecule discovered in soil from lab technician’s garden — plus, a huge study assessing the nuances of humans’ impacts on biodiversity.

rows.title: A superbug rose to the top after gaining a chemical weapon
rows.summary: A newfound ability to produce an antibiotic helped a strain of antibiotic-resistant bacteria to take over a hospital.

rows.title: Mathematician who reshaped theory of symmetry wins Abel Prize
rows.summary: Masaki Kashiwara is the first Japanese person to be awarded the most prestigious prize in mathematics.

rows.title: Gender gap in research publishing is improving — slowly
rows.summary: A Nature Index data set shows which countries, institutions and topic areas are making the greatest progress towards gender equity in research.

rows.title: Global marine heatwave of 2023–24 was viewed as unlikely but not impossible given current warming
rows.summary: Global sea surface temperatures in 2023–24 exceeded the previous record by an unprecedented margin. Observation-based statistical models and climate models suggest that such jumps in ocean temperatures are unlikely to occur even with global warming but are almost impossible without it. In climate models, temperatures revert to the long-term warming trend in the years after such jumps.

rows.title: First map of human brain mitochondria is ‘groundbreaking’ achievement
rows.summary: Hundreds of cubes of human brain tissue help scientists to chart the energy-making capabilities of various brain regions.

rows.title: Exclusive: NIH to cut grants for COVID research, documents reveal
rows.summary: Studies on climate change and South Africa are also on the latest list of grants to be terminated, according to updated documents obtained by Nature .

rows.title: Pregnancy’s true toll on the body: huge birth study paints most detailed picture yet
rows.summary: Data from 300,000 births reveal how essential biological measurements are altered by carrying and delivering a baby.

rows.title: The full lethal impact of massive cuts to international food aid
rows.summary: The sudden withdrawal of almost half of global funding for nutrition suddenly will have dire consequences for decades.

rows.title: Empower families to lead the design of their ageing loved ones’ health care
rows.summary: Rather than assuming that relatives of older people will step up to fill systemic gaps in health care, communities need research and policies that align with families’ existing routines.

rows.title: New antibiotic that kills drug-resistant bacteria discovered in technician’s garden
rows.summary: The molecule targets bacteria in a way that other drugs don’t.

rows.title: Neuronal receptors at body temperature reveal their gating mechanics
rows.summary: Most communication between neurons is mediated by the neurotransmitter glutamate. The finding that temperature influences how glutamate binds to neuronal receptor proteins to initiate signal transduction reveals the mechanics of one of the brain’s most important processes.

rows.title: Crucial meeting: molecule helps vaccine to interact with killer T cells
rows.summary: Vaccines containing peptides called antigens are bad at stimulating key immune cells called killer T cells. A molecule now enables antigens to encounter these T cells.

rows.title: A map of mitochondrial biology reveals the energy landscape of the human brain
rows.summary: Mapping the density, molecular features and energy-transformation capacity of cell organelles called mitochondria in the brain reveals region- and cell-type-specific variability that tracks with evolutionary patterns. Correlations between mitochondrial and brain-imaging metrics could enable future non-invasive explorations of mitochondrial bioenergetics in the brain in health and disease.

rows.title: Track gender ratios in research to keep countries, institutions and publishers accountable
rows.summary: Nature Index data reveal how countries and fields differ in gender equity in research.

rows.title: Why is there more matter than antimatter? CERN result offers tantalizing new clue
rows.summary: Physicists have spotted a difference in the way matter and antimatter baryons decay, which could help to explain a major cosmic mystery.

rows.title: A lighthouse galaxy shines unexpectedly through the fog of the cosmic dawn
rows.summary: Ultraviolet light from a galaxy observed when the Universe was just 330 million years old has intriguing implications for understanding how the first generations of stars and black holes were formed.

rows.title: Recovery of fluoride from ‘forever chemicals’ could lead to circular economy for fluorine
rows.summary: A method for the degradation of ‘forever chemicals’ called per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) coupled with fluoride recovery has been developed by applying a phosphate‑enabled mechanochemical process. This approach reduces the environmental impact of PFAS and could supplement fluorspar, the fast-depleting mineral used for producing fluorochemicals.

rows.title: Some assembly required
rows.summary: The personal touch.

rows.title: Daily briefing: Why RNA hasn’t yet had its ‘AlphaFold’ moment
rows.summary: Protein-structure-prediction tools have transformed biology, but RNA is a tougher nut to crack. Plus, the NIH is cancelling COVID-19 research funds and how ‘qudits’ can boost quantum computing.

rows.title: AI is transforming peer review — and many scientists are worried
rows.summary: Artificial intelligence software is increasingly involved in reviewing papers, provoking interest and unease.

rows.title: Lasso-shaped molecule is a new type of broad-spectrum antibiotic
rows.summary: A natural antibacterial molecule shows clinical promise. Its unusual binding site is on an excellent target: protein-synthesis machinery known as the ribosome.

rows.title: Solidification of Earth’s mantle led inevitably to a basal magma ocean
rows.summary: As the early Earth solidified, gravitational segregation of dense, iron-rich melts drove mantle evolution, injecting geochemical signatures of shallow silicate fractionation into the deep mantle and inevitably forming a basal magma ocean.

rows.title: BRCA2 prevents PARPi-mediated PARP1 retention to protect RAD51 filaments
rows.summary: The tumour-suppressor protein BRCA2 is discovered to have a previously undescribed role in maintaining genomic integrity and the sensitivity of PARP1 inhibitors.

rows.title: Glutamate gating of AMPA-subtype iGluRs at physiological temperatures
rows.summary: Physiological temperatures augment activation of glutamate receptors, which enables the structural basis of neuronal excitation to be elucidated.

rows.title: Oxidation of retromer complex controls mitochondrial translation
rows.summary: Systematic base-editing and computational screens identify specific cysteine residues on VPS35 in the retromer complex as key sensors that decrease mitochondrial translation in response to reactive oxygen species signals.

rows.title: The contribution of de novo coding mutations to meningomyelocele
rows.summary: Exome sequencing of 851 trios from more than 2,500 individuals finds 187 genes with de novo mutations that contribute to meningomyelocele (spina bifida) and highlights critical pathways required for neural tube closure.

rows.title: Gene-modified pig-to-human liver xenotransplantation
rows.summary: A gene-edited pig liver transplanted into a human recipient remains functional after 10 days and indicates that porcine organs could help meet the growing demand for liver transplants.

rows.title: Deconstruction of rubber via C–H amination and aza-Cope rearrangement
rows.summary: Deconstruction of rubber is achieved using C–H amination and aza-Cope rearrangement to provide precursors for epoxy resins.

rows.title: irCLIP-RNP and Re-CLIP reveal patterns of dynamic protein assemblies on RNA
rows.summary: EGF-induced recruitment of UPF1 adjacent to HNRNPC induces splicing surveillance of cell proliferation mRNAs.

rows.title: Long-term impact and biological recovery in a deep-sea mining track
rows.summary: Four decades after a test mining experiment that removed nodules, the biological impacts in many groups of organisms persist, although populations of several organisms have begun to re-establish despite persistent physical changes at the seafloor.

rows.title: A broad-spectrum lasso peptide antibiotic targeting the bacterial ribosome
rows.summary: A new lasso peptide antibiotic exhibits broad-spectrum activity against Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria by interfering with bacterial protein synthesis, is unaffected by common resistance mechanisms and shows no toxicity towards human cells.

rows.title: Synaptic and neural behaviours in a standard silicon transistor
rows.summary: A standard commercial CMOS FET can exhibit synaptic-like long-term potentiation and depression or neuron-like leaky-integrate-and-fire and adaptive frequency-bursting behaviour when biased in a specific but unconventional way.

rows.title: Catalytic allylation of native hexoses and pentoses in water with indium
rows.summary: A longstanding challenge in organic synthesis—the catalytic allylation of unprotected saccharides in an aqueous medium, a key step for the synthesis of Millad NX 8000—is achieved through a simple and efficient indium-catalysed nucleophilic allylation using a three-carbon-unit allylboronic acid or its pinacol ester.

rows.title: Plasticity of the mammalian integrated stress response
rows.summary: A study describes the split integrated stress response, a cellular stress response mechanism characterized by reduced eIF2B activity without eIF2α phosphorylation, which activates the eIF4E–ATF4–PCK2 axis, enabling metabolic reprogramming.

rows.title: A coronavirus assembly inhibitor that targets the viral membrane protein
rows.summary: High-throughput screening and hit optimization have led to the development of a small molecule, CIM-834, that targets the SARS-CoV-2 membrane protein and blocks assembly of the virus.

rows.title: Macrophages harness hepatocyte glutamate to boost liver regeneration
rows.summary: Glutamate metabolically reprograms bone-marrow-derived macrophages, stabilizing HIF1α, which transcriptionally activates WNT3 to promote YAP1-dependent hepatocyte proliferation, boosting liver regeneration.

rows.title: The P-loop NTPase RUVBL2 is a conserved clock component across eukaryotes
rows.summary: A study finds that RUVBL2 is a conserved component of eukaryotic circadian clocks and suggests that slow ATPase activity, which was initially discovered in cyanobacteria, is a shared feature of eukaryotic clocks.

rows.title: Phosphate-enabled mechanochemical PFAS destruction for fluoride reuse
rows.summary: This study highlights a protocol that converts various perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs), including fluoroplastics, into valuable fluorochemicals through a solvent-free mechanochemical process, thereby enabling fluorine recovery and contributing to a sustainable circular fluorine economy.

rows.title: The global human impact on biodiversity
rows.summary: Key measures of biodiversity were quantified and found to be affected by human pressures that shifted community composition and decreased local diversity across terrestrial, freshwater and marine ecosystems.

rows.title: A human brain map of mitochondrial respiratory capacity and diversity
rows.summary: The ability to physically partition the human brain at a spatial resolution comparable to neuroimaging methods enabled the development of a brain-wide atlas of mitochondrial content, specialization and enzymatic oxidation and phosphorylation activities.

rows.title: Genome-wide CRISPR screen in human T cells reveals regulators of FOXP3
rows.summary: The RBPJ–NCOR repressor complex is identified as a negative regulator of FOXP3 expression through modulation of histone acetylation in induced regulatory T cells.

rows.title: Changes in neurotensin signalling drive hedonic devaluation in obesity
rows.summary: In mice, prolonged consumption of a high-fat diet decreases interest in calorie-rich foods as a result of reduced neurotensin expression and signalling, which uncouples hedonic feeding behaviour linked to neurons projecting from lateral nucleus accumbens to ventral tegmental area.

rows.title: A prospective code for value in the serotonin system
rows.summary: Merging ideas from reinforcement learning theory with recent insights into the filtering properties of the dorsal raphe nucleus, a unifying perspective is found explaining why serotonin neurons are activated by both rewards and punishments.

rows.title: A small-molecule SARS-CoV-2 inhibitor targeting the membrane protein
rows.summary: JNJ-9676—a small-molecule inhibitor targeting coronavirus M protein that shows excellent efficacy in Syrian golden hamster models—binds to and stabilizes the M protein dimer in an altered conformational state between its long and short forms, preventing the release of infectious virus.

rows.title: Connectome-driven neural inventory of a complete visual system
rows.summary: A connectome of the right optic lobe from a male fruitfly is presented together with an extensive collection of genetic drivers matched to a comprehensive neuron-type catalogue.

rows.title: Multimodal generative AI for medical image interpretation
rows.summary: This Perspective describes how recent advances in artificial intelligence could be used to automate medical image interpretation to complement human expertise and empower physicians and patients.

rows.title: Witnessing the onset of reionization through Lyman-α emission at redshift 13
rows.summary: Spectroscopy from the JWST Advanced Deep Extragalactic Survey of a galaxy at redshift 13 shows a singular, bright emission line identified as Lyman-α, suggesting the onset of reionization only 330 Myr after the Big Bang.

rows.title: STING agonist-based ER-targeting molecules boost antigen cross-presentation
rows.summary: STING agonist-based endoplasmic reticulum-targeting molecules can be conjugated directly onto antigens to deliver them to the cross-presentation pathway, improving CD8 + T cell responses against tumours and viruses.

rows.title: The other climate crisis
rows.summary: The standard approach of climate science is showing signs of a crisis owing to the emergence of discrepancies and disruptions in recent years; this Perspective discusses the policy implications and the paths forward.

rows.title: Certified randomness using a trapped-ion quantum processor
rows.summary: Certifiably random bits can be generated using the 56-qubit Quantinuum H2-1 trapped-ion quantum computer accessed over the Internet.

rows.title: Ancient shackles testify to brutality of Egypt’s gold mines
rows.summary: Greek engineers who moved to Egypt in the fourth century BC might have imported the devices.

rows.title: Lessons from Portugal on effects of cutting research funding
Life-giving oxygen is wafting out of lakes worldwide
rows.summary: Machine-learning method shows declining oxygen levels in thousands of lakes as their waters warm.

rows.title: Give grants to female scientists in war zones
Why is my cello howling?
rows.summary: A musician’s query as to the origin of a warped ‘wolf’ tone, and a review of a book by physicist Marie Curie, in our weekly dip into Nature’ s archive.

rows.title: Lesotho matters
How to get more women into mining
How a scientist–pop industry partnership slashed a live gig’s carbon emissions by 98%
rows.summary: Climate researchers collaborated with the trip-hop band Massive Attack to reduce the climate impact of live music.

rows.title: How the Atlantic jet stream has changed in 600 years — and what it means for weather
rows.summary: A multi-century climate record suggests that current Atlantic jet-stream variations are not the cause of an increase in extreme weather events.

rows.title: Daily briefing: Why women are far more likely to develop Alzheimer’s than men
rows.summary: Alzheimer’s disease might be partly linked to the hormonal changes that accompany menopause. Plus, the brain might temporarily ‘eat’ its own myelin to power through marathons and scientists in the United States and abroad are feeling anxious about crossing the US border.

rows.title: Climate change will send home insurance spiralling. Here’s how to control costs
rows.summary: Insurers rely on sophisticated catastrophe modelling to estimate risk exposure — and as climate risks are rising, so are the costs for protection.

rows.title: Fasting for weight loss is all the rage: what are the health benefits?
rows.summary: Intermittent fasting has gained a following, in part because of tantalizing hints that it can boost cognition, fend off cancer and even slow ageing.

rows.title: Trump administration sued over huge funding cuts at Columbia University
rows.summary: Two faculty organizations file suit after university makes concessions to Trump officials.

rows.title: Microbes can capture carbon and degrade plastic — why aren’t we using them more?
rows.summary: Interventions involving bacteria or fungi could help to sequester greenhouse gases, create more sustainable products and clean up pollution — in ways that are economically viable and safe.

rows.title: Meet ‘qudits’: more complex cousins of qubits boost quantum computing
rows.summary: Working with multi-dimensional entities could make calculations more efficient and reduce errors.

rows.title: MFSD6 is an entry receptor for enterovirus D68
rows.summary: The multipass membrane transporter MFSD6 localizes to the plasma membrane and acts as a host entry factor for enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) by binding directly to EV-D68 particles through its extracellular, third loop, offering a potential target to combat infections by this emerging pathogen.

rows.title: Reviving the biodiversity around an ancient palace
rows.summary: Juan Ramón Fernández Cardenete tends the Alhambra’s many water features and gardens.

rows.title: Glaciers are not just blocks of ice — plans to save them mustn’t overlook their hidden life
rows.summary: As glaciers begin to disappear, technological fixes to slow or halt ice melt are emerging. But regulations are urgently required before these fixes are used widely.

rows.title: RNA function follows form – why is it so hard to predict?
rows.summary: AlphaFold’s highly accurate structural models transformed protein biology,but RNA lags behind.

rows.title: How marathons change runners’ brains: scans point to surprise energy source
rows.summary: After the gruelling races, levels of the nerve-cell insulator myelin were lower, suggesting the brain uses the fatty substance as fuel.

rows.title: Does sharing first authorship on a paper carry a penalty? What the research says
rows.summary: Study dispels myth that order of names in a paper’s author list dictates perception of success.

rows.title: Shaking up earthquake safety in Nepal with a folk song
rows.summary: Geophysicist Shiba Subedi combines science and songwriting to raise awareness and debunk earthquake myths.

rows.title: Why Africans should be telling the story of human origins
rows.summary: Yohannes Haile-Selassie wants to shift the trajectory of palaeoanthropology in fossil-rich Ethiopia away from its long colonial heritage.

rows.title: What CERN does next matters for science and for international cooperation
rows.summary: The world’s largest particle-physics laboratory is approaching a pivotal moment in its history.

rows.title: Paralysed man stands again after receiving ‘reprogrammed’ stem cells
rows.summary: Another man also regained some movement, but two others experienced minimal improvement.

rows.title: The expanding Universe — do ongoing tensions leave room for new physics?
rows.summary: One century after Edwin Hubble revealed his astonishing discovery of a cosmos beyond the Milky Way, the most precise measurements still can’t agree on how fast galaxies are moving.

rows.title: Live-cell super-resolution microscopy reveals how molecules enter and exit the nucleus
rows.summary: The nuclear pore complex is the gateway to the nucleus of cells. Now an in vivo imaging technique can track the way in which molecules move through this complex.

rows.title: Winds on an ultrahot planet challenge climate models
rows.summary: The ultrahot exoplanet WASP‑121 b has strong winds that transport material in different directions depending on the altitude in the planet’s atmosphere. High-resolution observations have mapped these winds for the first time, challenging the current understanding of atmospheric dynamics.

rows.title: How to know whether a conference is right for you
rows.summary: Some low-profile meetings are helpful for parts of the scientific community. Others look like more of a cash grab.

rows.title: ‘Anxiety is palpable’: detention of researchers at US border spurs travel worries
rows.summary: Several high-profile incidents in the past month have scientists on edge.

rows.title: Daily briefing: Stunning Antarctic ecosystem revealed by calving iceberg
rows.summary: A thriving seafloor ecosystem has been revealed after an iceberg peeled away from the ice shelf of Antarctica. Plus, researchers are concerned that the Trump administration is taking aim at mRNA-vaccine research and the argument that the real job of a scientist is ‘writer’.

rows.title: Generalizing arene C–H alkylations by radical–radical cross-coupling
rows.summary: Using the concept of dynamic orbital selection distinct organic radical species can be differentiated, enabling direct coupling of aromatics with alcohols or carboxylic acids.

rows.title: Author Correction: Heritable polygenic editing: the next frontier in genomic medicine?
Author Correction: AI models collapse when trained on recursively generated data
Ship-pollution cuts have an electrifying effect: less lightning at sea
rows.summary: A crackdown on sulfur in ship fuel is linked to a steep drop in thunderclouds in the Indian Ocean and South China Sea.

rows.title: ‘Boggles the mind’: US defence department slashes research on emerging threats
rows.summary: Terminated projects include studies on the implications of artificial intelligence in combat and how extremism spreads online.

rows.title: Publisher Correction: A metagenomic ‘dark matter’ enzyme catalyses oxidative cellulose conversion
‘All this is in crisis’: US universities curtail staff and spending as Trump cuts take hold
rows.summary: Furloughs and more staff reductions loom as academic institutions contend with the prospect of even deeper cuts to federal funding.

rows.title: NIH has cut one mRNA-vaccine grant. Will more follow?
rows.summary: Concern rises among researchers after agency officials ask for a list of projects funded to study the jabs.

rows.title: Daily briefing: Babies make memories — so why don’t we recall them?
rows.summary: Babies as young as one year old can form memories, our adult brains just can’t access them. Plus, US-funded researchers outside the United States are being grilled about ideology and physicists suggest a ‘crazy’ new way we could generate electricity.

rows.title: How ‘animal methods bias’ is affecting research careers
rows.summary: Some early-career researchers report feeling pressure to use animal models to meet journal and grant requirements, even in disciplines and projects that don’t require them.

rows.title: Daily briefing: The mysterious force pushing galaxies apart might be getting weaker
rows.summary: Mysterious ‘dark energy’ — thought to be a cosmological constant — might have weakened over billions of years. Plus, skin immune cells form their own ‘bandage’ around wounds and how astronomers are tackling the growing problem of satellite pollution.

rows.title: Author Correction: Observation of an ultra-high-energy cosmic neutrino with KM3NeT
Babies do make memories — so why can’t we recall our earliest years?
rows.summary: MRI scans show that the brains of infants and toddlers can encode memories, even if we don’t remember them as adults.

rows.title: Author Correction: Spatially resolved multiomics of human cardiac niches
Trump team ‘survey’ sent to overseas researchers prompts foreign-interference fears
rows.summary: Document asks US-funded scientists in Australia, the United Kingdom and the European Union to declare links to China and to projects on diversity, equity and inclusion.

rows.title: Bulk superconductivity near 40 K in hole-doped SmNiO 2 at ambient pressure
rows.summary: Superconductivity at temperatures approaching 40 K for a hole-doped nickel oxide that is isostructural with cuprate superconductors demonstrates the existence of a broader family of materials and potential for achieving higher-temperature superconductivity.

rows.title: End-to-end data-driven weather prediction
rows.summary: Aardvark Weather, an end-to-end machine learning model, replaces the entire numerical weather prediction pipeline with a machine learning model, by producing accurate global and local forecasts without relying on numerical solvers, revolutionizing weather prediction with improved speed, accuracy and customization capabilities.

rows.title: Asia leads rise in clean-energy research
rows.summary: Insights from the Nature Index show that the boom in research related to affordable and clean energy is not a global trend.

rows.title: Why humans have puzzle-shaped cells
rows.summary: The specialized cells that let lymph leak (and why that's a good thing)

rows.title: World’s tiniest LED display has pixels smaller than a virus
rows.summary: See images of another tiny display with pixels the size of a human hair.

rows.title: The biggest machine in science: inside the fight to build the next giant particle collider
rows.summary: The European physics laboratory CERN is planning to build a mega collider by 2070. Critics say the plan could lead to its ruin.

rows.title: Ancient peat reveals that sea level surged rapidly twice at the end of the last ice age
rows.summary: An analysis of peat from ancient wetlands provides a reconstruction of how sea level increased millennia ago — and how it might rise again with global warming.

rows.title: Bird brains help scientists to unveil the secrets of speech
rows.summary: Neural recordings from parrots and songbirds reveal the ways in which vocal production is encoded in the brain, highlighting remarkable similarities between how parrots and humans learn to produce sounds.

rows.title: Mini-satellite paves the way for quantum messaging anywhere on Earth
rows.summary: A Chinese team has transmitted quantum-encrypted images a record 12,900 kilometres.

rows.title: Immune cells ‘bandage’ wounds with bacteria-trapping goo
rows.summary: Cells called neutrophils form gooey rings around sites where skin is punctured, study in mice shows.

rows.title: AI could soon tackle projects that take humans weeks
rows.summary: New metric assesses how AI is getting better at completing long tasks — but some researchers are wary of long-term predictions.

rows.title: Mutations that accrue through life set the stage for stomach cancer
rows.summary: Comprehensive maps of mutations in healthy and diseased gastric tissue give clues about how cancer arises and could inform early-detection strategies.

rows.title: Meeting the energy challenge posed by data centres is central to a green future
rows.summary: A ‘datacentric’ approach will allow consumers and producers to make informed decisions that aid the transition to clean power.

rows.title: New antifungal breaks the mould
rows.summary: A bacterium makes a molecule that kills drug-resistant fungi in an unusual way — by targeting various phospholipid molecules in membranes.

rows.title: Trump’s return puts renewables at a crossroads
rows.summary: Clean-energy research might be booming in Asia, but the energy transition has an uncertain future.

rows.title: Is dark energy getting weaker? Fresh data bolster shock finding
rows.summary: Physicists had long assumed that the elusive force has constant strength. But the latest results from a project to map the Universe’s expansion challenge this idea.

rows.title: A textbook assumption about the brain’s most abundant receptors needs to be rewritten
rows.summary: The AMPA group of brain receptors have mostly been assumed to be calcium impermeable and so were not thought to contribute to the calcium-dependent mechanisms underlying learning and memory. Observations of calcium permeability in some AMPA-receptor subtypes now overturn those assumptions about these receptors’ properties and their roles in neuronal communication.

rows.title: Battery researchers strive for standardization
rows.summary: Big data is key for the quality control needed to advance the field.

rows.title: Daily briefing: About 1% of children have genetic paternity other than that recorded by history
rows.summary: A geneticist gently prises open the branches of family trees to reveal hidden kinships. Plus, the world's oldest crater and a proposed energy plant in Chile threatens the dark skies over some of the world's most powerful telescopes.

rows.title: Can Earth’s rotation generate power? Physicists divided over controversial claim
rows.summary: Experiments suggest that an unusual magnetic material can help harness energy from the planet’s rotation. But not everyone is convinced.

rows.title: A guide to the Nature Index
rows.summary: A description of the terminology and methodology used in this supplement, and a guide to the functionality that is available free online at natureindex.com.

rows.title: A practical leap towards secure quantum communication over long distances
rows.summary: A network of quantum satellites that communicate with ground stations could offer a solution to enable a global quantum network. A quantum microsatellite that has been developed and launched can perform space-to-ground quantum communication using portable ground stations.

rows.title: Could libraries band together to ensure open access for all?
rows.summary: Through the ‘subscribe to open’ model, libraries’ annual subscriptions ensure that paywalled journals become freely accessible, benefiting researchers and the public alike.

rows.title: Light pollution threatens fleet of world-class telescopes in Atacama Desert
rows.summary: The effects of a proposed green-energy facility in Chile could be devastating for some of the most powerful instruments available to astronomers.

rows.title: How the US tech industry is shaping the transition to green energy
rows.summary: Major investments to fuel AI’s power demands are not the only way big tech is having an influence.

rows.title: What is the best type of tree to use for forest restoration?
rows.summary: In forest experiments, tree species capable of high rates of photosynthesis grow more slowly than species with lower maximum rates of photosynthesis — with implications for tree-planting projects.

rows.title: Measles is surging in the US: how bad could it get?
rows.summary: Researchers flag groups that should get an extra dose of measles vaccine as case numbers continue to rise in Texas and neighbouring states.

rows.title: Disconnections
rows.summary: An antisocial network.

rows.title: Tiny satellite sets new record for secure quantum communication
rows.summary: Laser-based system allows quantum-encrypted information to be beamed across the globe, plus — an AI that can improve other AIs via written feedback, and an update on science in the US in the wake of Trump team’s cuts.

rows.title: What is stopping a complete switch to clean energy?
rows.summary: Investment in renewables is hitting new heights, but uneven funding and geopolitical uncertainty are clouding the boom.

rows.title: Downscaling micro- and nano-perovskite LEDs
rows.summary: A process based on perovskite semiconductors is described to downscale micro-LEDs and nano-LEDs to below the conventional size limits, demonstrating average external quantum efficiencies maintained at around 20% across a wide range of pixel lengths.

rows.title: Fluctuating magnetism and Pomeranchuk effect in multilayer graphene
rows.summary: Itinerant magnetism in rhombohedral multilayer graphene shows a large excess entropy from magnetic fluctuations above its critical temperature—typically only associated with local moments—which implies the decoupling of charge and isospin degrees of freedom, and results in the isospin Pomeranchuk effect.

rows.title: Drivers of avian genomic change revealed by evolutionary rate decomposition
rows.summary: Genomic evolutionary rates are decomposed to identify the dominant lineages and genes driving rate variation across the phylogeny of birds.

rows.title: Widespread slow growth of acquisitive tree species
rows.summary: Under field conditions, acquisitive tree species generally grow slowly, whereas conservative species show generally higher realized growth, owing to their ability to tolerate unfavourable environmental conditions.

rows.title: A polyene macrolide targeting phospholipids in the fungal cell membrane
rows.summary: Mandimycin, a polyene macrolide, exhibits strong antifungal activity and possesses a mode of action that is distinct from other compounds of this class.

rows.title: VDAC2 loss elicits tumour destruction and inflammation for cancer therapy
rows.summary: VDAC2 deficiency elicits uncontrolled IFNγ-induced BAK activation and mitochondrial damage for improved cancer therapy.

rows.title: Regulated somatic hypermutation enhances antibody affinity maturation
rows.summary: Germinal centre B cells modify their mutation rate to preserve high-affinity receptors, thereby safeguarding high-affinity B cell lineages and enhancing the outcomes of antibody affinity maturation.

rows.title: Down-converted photon pairs in a high- Q silicon nitride microresonator
rows.summary: Spontaneous parametric down-conversion was used to generate narrowband photon pairs with a high spectral brightness in a high- Q silicon nitride microresonator.

rows.title: Convergent vocal representations in parrot and human forebrain motor networks
rows.summary: Using advanced brain-recording techniques, parrots were found to have a brain organization for vocal control similar to humans, making them an important model for studying speech and for developing potential treatments for communication disorders.

rows.title: Rapid emergence of latent knowledge in the sensory cortex drives learning
rows.summary: In mice, learning and performance on an auditory task is driven by higher-order signals in the auditory cortex that are no longer required when the mouse has achieved expert-level performance.

rows.title: Overlapping nuclear import and export paths unveiled by two-colour MINFLUX
rows.summary: High spatiotemporal precision tracking using 3D MINFLUX shows that nuclear import and export occur in overlapping regions of the central pore, providing insight into transport across the nuclear pore complex.

rows.title: Structural dynamics of DNA unwinding by a replicative helicase
rows.summary: Cryo-electron microscopy structures of DNA helicases in various conformations provide insight into an ATP-hydrolysis-dependent ‘entropy switch’ that drives unwinding of DNA for replication, with probable conservation across viral and eukaryotic systems.

rows.title: Water structure and electric fields at the interface of oil droplets
rows.summary: Raman spectroscopy measurements of water at the interface with oil droplets show a perturbed hydrogen-bond network and evidence for a strong interfacial electric field.

rows.title: Electroluminescence and energy transfer mediated by hyperbolic polaritons
rows.summary: Far-field mid-infrared spectroscopy reveals both the electroluminescence of hyperbolic phonon polaritons of hexagonal boron nitride excited by strongly biased graphene, and the associated radiative energy transfer through the material.

rows.title: Hyperbolic phonon-polariton electroluminescence in 2D heterostructures
rows.summary: All-electrical excitation of the hyperbolic phonon polaritons in hexagonal boron nitride by drifting charge carriers in nearby graphene results in electroluminescence at mid-infrared frequencies.

rows.title: Spatially resolved mapping of cells associated with human complex traits
rows.summary: Integration of spatial transcriptomics data with data from genome-wide association studies enables spatially resolved mapping of cells associated with human diseases and other complex traits.

rows.title: Oncolytic virus VG161 in refractory hepatocellular carcinoma
rows.summary: Results of a multicentre phase 1 clinical trial evaluating treatment with the engineered herpes simplex virus VG161 in advanced liver cancer indicate a good safety profile and promising efficacy.

rows.title: GluA2-containing AMPA receptors form a continuum of Ca 2+ -permeable channels
rows.summary: GluA2-containing AMPA receptors (AMPARs) are not Ca 2+ impermeable, and their ability to transport Ca 2+ is shaped by the subunit composition of AMPAR tetramers as well as the orientation of transmembrane AMPAR regulatory proteins and cornichon auxiliary subunits.

rows.title: Global sea-level rise in the early Holocene revealed from North Sea peats
rows.summary: An early Holocene sea-level curve based on data from the North Sea reveals two phases of accelerated sea-level rise owing to meltwater from the North American and Antarctic ice sheets.

rows.title: Dynamic cytoskeletal regulation of cell shape supports resilience of lymphatic endothelium
rows.summary: Dynamic cytoskeletal regulation of lymphatic endothelial cell shape, induced by isotropic stretch and crucial for dermal lymphatic capillary function, is identified and found to result from continuous remodelling of cellular overlaps that maintain vessel integrity.

rows.title: Long-term studies provide unique insights into evolution
rows.summary: Long-term studies provide insights into the complex interplay between evolutionary process and pattern across multiple systems and timescales.

rows.title: Cooper-pair density modulation state in an iron-based superconductor
rows.summary: Pair density modulation, an unusual superconducting state whose superconducting gap is modulated by the wavelength corresponding to the lattice periodicity, is described and observed in exfoliated thin flakes of the iron-based superconductor FeTe 0.55 Se 0.45 .

rows.title: The somatic mutation landscape of normal gastric epithelium
rows.summary: Whole-gene sequencing of microdissected gastric glands from individuals with and without gastric cancer reveals distinct patterns of somatic mutations and provides insights into influences on the somatic evolution of the gastric epithelium.

rows.title: Histological signatures map anti-fibrotic factors in mouse and human lungs
rows.summary: Transcriptomic and proteomic analyses of cells and matrix along the fibrotic trajectory in mouse lung identified PI16 as an anti-fibrotic factor with potential for therapeutic application in humans.

rows.title: Sleep pressure accumulates in a voltage-gated lipid peroxidation memory
rows.summary: Sleep-inducing neurons in Drosophila rely on Hyperkinetic, the β-subunit of the K V 1 channel Shaker, to monitor sleep need by translating lipid peroxidation events into changes in the oxidation state of a stably bound NADPH cofactor.

rows.title: Transient silencing of hypermutation preserves B cell affinity during clonal bursting
rows.summary: B cell germinal centres achieve a balance between clonal expansion and sequence diversification by suppressing somatic hypermutation during proliferative clonal bursts.

rows.title: Microsatellite-based real-time quantum key distribution
rows.summary: A quantum microsatellite, with a payload weighing only 23 kilograms, in combination with portable ground stations that weigh merely 100 kilograms, is capable of performing space-to-ground real-time quantum key distribution.

rows.title: Matrix-producing neutrophils populate and shield the skin
rows.summary: A population of neutrophils in the skin produces extracellular matrix, providing a defence strategy by reinforcing the barrier properties of the skin and helping to block the entry of pathogens.

rows.title: Optimizing generative AI by backpropagating language model feedback
rows.summary: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) systems can be optimized using TextGrad, a framework that performs optimization by backpropagating large-language-model-generated feedback; TextGrad enables optimization across diverse tasks, including radiotherapy treatment plans and molecule generation.

rows.title: An experiment in mass education using satellite TV
rows.summary: Plans to broadcast TV to villages in India to improve literacy rates, and camels that have settled in the Nevada desert, in our weekly dip into Nature ’s archive.

rows.title: US disruptions to science could transform global research landscape
Food-industry waste finds a second life as bioplastic
rows.summary: The protein keratin, the principle ingredient of wool and feathers, can be repurposed as strong, flexible plastic.

rows.title: Global cooperation is crucial for DeepSeek and broader AI research
AI demands a different approach to education
Iguanas reached Fiji by floating 8,000 kilometres across the sea
rows.summary: Genomic analysis suggests that the ancestors of lizards on Fiji today rafted from North America some 30 million years ago.

rows.title: Japan needs a fresh approach to innovation
Microsoft quantum-computing claim still lacks evidence: physicists are dubious
rows.summary: Some attendees at a packed presentation were curious about the prospect of the first ‘topological’ qubits, but left with questions unanswered.

rows.title: Vaccines save lives. Leaders must champion them
rows.summary: Attacks on vaccines and the cancellation of research into what causes vaccine hesitancy puts people in harm’s way.

rows.title: Daily briefing: Iguanas from the Americas might have rafted to Fiji
rows.summary: Iguanas from the Americas might have travelled 8,000 kilometres across the Pacific Ocean to Fiji on a raft of vegetation. Plus, US scientists are being told to avoid mentions of ‘mRNA vaccines’ in NIH grant applications.
