In pancreatic cancer, a common and deadly cancer, RNA vaccines that encode neoantigens — mutant proteins found only in cancer cells — induce substantial numbers of long-lived CD8 + T cells with preserved function, and their presence correlates with better clinical outcomes at a three-year follow-up.

rows.title: Why these scientists devote time to editing and updating Wikipedia
rows.summary: Researchers can recognize a reliable source of information, making them ideal contributors to the free global online encyclopaedia.

rows.title: Microsoft claims quantum-computing breakthrough — but some physicists are sceptical
rows.summary: The tech giant aims to make ‘topological’ quantum computers that will reach useful scales faster than competing technologies.

rows.title: Women need platforms to celebrate excellence in research and technology
rows.summary: Nature is proud to be associated with a new award for women in technology. The world needs more prizes for exceptional researchers and innovators.

rows.title: Putting the brakes on mitochondrial fusion to prevent escape of mitochondrial DNA
rows.summary: Cellular organelles called mitochondria contain DNA and can fuse together or split apart. It emerges that excess fusion is averted by stress-activated regulators, preventing the potentially harmful release of mitochondrial DNA.

rows.title: Why retractions data could be a powerful tool for cleaning up science
rows.summary: A Nature analysis of retractions hotspots around the world suggests institutions should pay close attention to retractions data.

rows.title: Reply to: Atlantic oceanic droughts do not threaten Asian water tower
Racial bias eliminated when ratings switch from five stars to thumbs up or down
rows.summary: Implementing a performance-rating system with a two-point scale instead of a five-point scale could be an easy way to temper racial prejudices and tangibly improve income equality for workers from under-represented groups.

rows.title: Daily briefing: Meet the scientists who edit Wikipedia
rows.summary: Which universities top the retraction chart? Plus, meet the scientists editing Wikipedia in their spare time.

rows.title: Exclusive: These universities have the most retracted scientific articles
rows.summary: A first-of-its-kind analysis by Nature reveals which institutions are retraction hotspots.

rows.title: Peptides from abnormal RNA processing in cancer offer an immunotherapy target
rows.summary: Tumour cells often have problems processing messenger RNA. The finding that these splicing errors result in commonly expressed peptides that are recognized by immune cells offers a target for cancer treatments.

rows.title: Cycles
rows.summary: The way of things.

rows.title: How chronic stress warps decision-making
rows.summary: Nerve-cell ‘highways’ identified in mice suggest that stress pushes the brain towards rigid habit and away from thoughtful choices.

rows.title: Author Correction: Seasonal advance of intense tropical cyclones in a warming climate
Sequence clustering confounds AlphaFold2
Racist ratings linger in five-star systems — a thumbs up could fix that
rows.summary: When an online platform changed the way customers rated workers, discrimination disappeared — plus, Nature investigates where the most retractions occur.

rows.title: The secrets of static electricity are finally being revealed
rows.summary: The mechanism that causes static electricity to build up is a mystery. Experiments now reveal that materials ‘remember’ past contacts with each other — and this determines how electric charge is transferred in future contacts.

rows.title: What’s next for the World Health Organization? US exit could reshape agency
rows.summary: US and Argentine departures loom — but strategic reform could strengthen the WHO, say experts.

rows.title: Biggest-ever AI biology model writes DNA on demand
rows.summary: An artificial-intelligence network trained on a vast trove of sequence data is a step towards designing completely new genomes.

rows.title: Key process in sex-cell formation can finally be studied in vitro
rows.summary: The enzyme SPO11 has a crucial role in meiosis, the process that forms sperm and egg cells. The activity of purified SPO11 has now been reconstituted in a cell-free system — enabling the enzyme’s role to be studied in detail.

rows.title: Microsoft builds AI that creates ‘impressive’ video-game worlds
rows.summary: Developers wanted tools that generate gameplay sequences that adhere to game rules; they say an engine called WHAM delivers.

rows.title: Atlantic oceanic droughts do not threaten Asian water tower
Mechanism for local attenuation of DNA replication at double-strand breaks
rows.summary: DNA double-strand breaks induce local genome maintenance and inhibition of replication initiation at nearby topologically associating domains without affecting global DNA synthesis.

rows.title: Clonal driver neoantigen loss under EGFR TKI and immune selection pressures
rows.summary: We show the evolution of a case of EGFR mutant lung cancer treated with a combination of erlotinib, osimertinib, radiotherapy and a personalized neopeptide vaccine targeting somatic mutations, including EGFR exon 19 deletion.

rows.title: World and Human Action Models towards gameplay ideation
rows.summary: A state-of-the-art generative artificial intelligence model of a video game is introduced to allow the support of human creative ideation, with the analysis of user study data highlighting three necessary capabilities, namely, consistency, diversity and persistency.

rows.title: RNA neoantigen vaccines prime long-lived CD8 + T cells in pancreatic cancer
rows.summary: In a phase 1 trial, patients with pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma who were treated with surgery and bespoke neoantigen mRNA vaccines combined with anti-PD-L1 and chemotherapy exhibited marked long-lived persistence of neoantigen-specific CD8 + T cell clones, which correlated with prolonged recurrence-free survival at a 3.2-year follow-up.

rows.title: De novo design of transmembrane fluorescence-activating proteins
rows.summary: A study describes the design of de novo ligand-binding transmembrane proteins, demonstrating their specific binding and activation of fluorogenic ligands.

rows.title: GABAergic neuron-to-glioma synapses in diffuse midline gliomas
rows.summary: Functional, tumour-promoting GABAergic neuron-to-glioma synapses in diffuse midline gliomas are identified.

rows.title: Nociceptive neurons promote gastric tumour progression via a CGRP–RAMP1 axis
rows.summary: Functional connectivity between gastric cancer cells and sensory neurons offers a potential therapeutic target.

rows.title: Thermal Ca 2+ /Mg 2+ exchange reactions to synthesize CO 2 removal materials
rows.summary: Reactions of Mg-rich silicates with calcium carbonates/sulfates result in the formation of materials that could potentially be used for low-cost carbon dioxide removal from the atmosphere.

rows.title: Modulated ringdown comb interferometry for sensing of highly complex gases
rows.summary: A new optical technique, modulated ringdown comb interferometry, is introduced for measuring the concentration of gas species in a complex sample and its efficacy demonstrated using exhaled human breath and ambient air in the mid-infrared.

rows.title: Perovskite heteroepitaxy for high-efficiency and stable pure-red LEDs
rows.summary: A heteroepitaxial-strain-based strategy for enhancing the stability of perovskite quantum dots for spectrally narrow (pure) red LEDs is reported.

rows.title: Global modules robustly emerge from local interactions and smooth gradients
rows.summary: The principle of peak selection is described, by which local interactions and smooth gradients drive self-organization of discrete global modules.

rows.title: SPO11 dimers are sufficient to catalyse DNA double-strand breaks in vitro
rows.summary: A biochemical system recapitulates the hallmarks of meiotic double-strand break formation, with mouse SPO11 catalysing break formation in the absence of any partners and remaining covalently attached to 5′ broken strands.

rows.title: Interferometric single-shot parity measurement in InAs–Al hybrid devices
rows.summary: A device architecture based on indium arsenide–aluminium heterostructures with a gate-defined superconducting nanowire allows single-shot interferometric measurement of fermion parity and demonstrates an assignment error probability of 1%.

rows.title: Reply to: Insufficient evidence for natural selection associated with the Black Death
In vitro reconstitution of meiotic DNA double-strand-break formation
rows.summary: The in vitro characterization of a key event in the early stages of meiosis—the induction of double-strand DNA breaks by the SPO11–TOP6BL complex—provides insight into the catalytic mechanism and evolution of SPO11.

rows.title: Reconstitution of SPO11-dependent double-strand break formation
rows.summary: Reconstitution of recombinantly expressed SPO11–TOP6BL complex recapitulates its DNA cleavage function and together with structural modelling and biochemical experiments, provides insights into the regulation and mechanism of SPO11 activity.

rows.title: Scale dichotomization reduces customer racial discrimination and income inequality
rows.summary: Changing from a five-point scale to a two-point scale for rating workers reduces racial discrimination by making customers focus on whether the work was good or bad instead of their own personal biases.

rows.title: Hypotaxy of wafer-scale single-crystal transition metal dichalcogenides
rows.summary: A new method ‘hypotaxy’ enables wafer-scale, single-crystal transition metal dichalcogenides growth directly on crystalline, lattice-mismatched and amorphous substrates.

rows.title: An opponent striatal circuit for distributional reinforcement learning
rows.summary: D1- and D2-expressing striatal neurons encode separate parts of a learned reward distribution, paralleling modern approaches in machine learning.

rows.title: Human-correlated genetic models identify precision therapy for liver cancer
rows.summary: As proof of principle, an analysis using a suite of human-aligned immunocompetent mouse models of hepatocellular carcinoma identifies a promising therapeutic candidate, cladribine, which acts in a highly effective subtype-specific manner in combination with standard-of-care therapy.

rows.title: Spontaneous ordering of identical materials into a triboelectric series
rows.summary: Nominally identical materials are found to spontaneously order into triboelectric series over repeated processes, which is found to be driven by the act of contact itself using experiments as well as numerical simulations.

rows.title: Cooperative nutrient scavenging is an evolutionary advantage in cancer
rows.summary: Nutrient-starved tumour cells cooperate by secreting aminopeptidases that digest oligopeptides in the microenvironment, creating a shared pool of free amino acids.

rows.title: Endogenous DNA damage at sites of terminated transcripts
rows.summary: Transcription termination or pausing during DNA replication in bacteria and humans results in DNA damage with exposed 3′ single-stranded DNA ends and mutations.

rows.title: Dual regulation of mitochondrial fusion by Parkin–PINK1 and OMA1
rows.summary: We find that, in mice, although the individual loss of Parkin or OMA1 does not affect mitochondrial integrity, their combined loss results in small body size, low locomotor activity, premature death, mitochondrial abnormalities and innate immune responses.

rows.title: Tumour-wide RNA splicing aberrations generate actionable public neoantigens
rows.summary: A study identifies public neoantigens generated by tumor-wide aberrant mRNA splicing activity across distinct cancer types.

rows.title: A dual-pathway architecture for stress to disrupt agency and promote habit
rows.summary: Adaptive decision-making often requires an understanding of our agency in a situation; however, chronic stress can disrupt agency and promote inflexible, habitual behaviour by turning off a brain pathway needed for agency and activating one that promotes habit.

rows.title: Plasmodium blood stage development requires the chromatin remodeller Snf2L
rows.summary: Plasmodium falciparum Snf2L is an ISWI-related ATPase that actively repositions P. falciparum nucleosomes in vivo.

rows.title: Continuous-variable multipartite entanglement in an integrated microcomb
rows.summary: Deterministic generation of a continuous-variable eight-mode entanglement on an integrated optical chip is reported.

rows.title: Community estimate of global glacier mass changes from 2000 to 2023
rows.summary: An intercomparison exercise reassesses mass loss from glaciers worldwide based on the main in situ and satellite methods from 2000 to 2023; the results are consistent with previous assessments and provide a refined and comprehensive observational baseline for future impact and modelling studies.

rows.title: Artificial intelligence for modelling infectious disease epidemics
rows.summary: This Perspective considers the application to infectious disease modelling of AI systems that combine machine learning, computational statistics, information retrieval and data science.

rows.title: A sustainable ocean needs thriving ocean societies
A giant leap for machine translation could be even bigger
The 1925 debate about adopting the word ‘scientist’ heats up
rows.summary: The pros and cons of a word gaining popularity, and publication of an updated edition of a book by Charles Darwin in this week’s pick from the Nature archive.

rows.title: Charles Darwin saw the importance of development in evolution
Don’t overlook the mental-health costs of California’s wildfires
Daily briefing: CAR-T-cell therapy recipient nears two decades in cancer remission
rows.summary: A woman who received CAR-T-cell therapy has now been in cancer remission for 19 years. Plus, a genetic swap makes mice squeak differently.

rows.title: A human gene makes mice squeak differently — did it contribute to language?
rows.summary: A gene variant present in most people might have contributed to cognitive differences between humans and their closest relatives.

rows.title: Could psychedelics be fine-tuned to relieve anxiety but skip the ‘trip’?
rows.summary: Interest in psychedelic substances as medicines is rising. Identifying the neural circuits that mediate the benefits of psychedelics could pave the way for long-lasting anxiety treatments without the short-term sensory disturbances.

rows.title: Pinpointing neurons that hinder cancer treatment
rows.summary: Pancreatic tumours hijack neuronal signalling mechanisms to boost cancer growth. A technology to identify and profile mouse neurons that connect the spinal cord to pancreatic cancer might improve treatment of this disease.

rows.title: Author Correction: Fetal hepatocytes protect the HSPC genome via fetuin-A
‘Unconventional’ nickel superconductor excites physicists
rows.summary: Compounds called nickelates can conduct electricity without resistance, well above absolute zero and at ambient pressure.

rows.title: Learn COVID pandemic lessons — before it’s too late
rows.summary: Five years after the start of the COVID-19 pandemic, public weariness and irresponsible politics are hampering an effective response to global infectious-disease outbreaks.

rows.title: Why is it so hard to rewrite a genome?
rows.summary: Synthetic biologists have the know-how and ambition to retool whole genomes. But the hidden complexity of biological systems continues to surprise them.

rows.title: China made waves with Deepseek, but its real ambition is AI-driven industrial innovation
rows.summary: The country is betting on AI to develop practical, cost-effective business tools for global markets, especially lower-income countries.

rows.title: Molecular glue unexpectedly mimics the effect of cancer mutations
rows.summary: Many conventional small-molecule drugs work by inhibiting proteins, affecting their function. One small molecule instead imbues a protein with a new function in a mechanism that could inform rational drug design.

rows.title: Migraine is more than a headache — a radical rethink offers hope to one billion people
rows.summary: Drugs that can prevent or relieve migraine attacks are only effective for some people. Research is starting to untangle the reasons why.

rows.title: Vertical structure of an exoplanet’s atmospheric jet stream
rows.summary: Ultra-hot Jupiters provide a unique window into atmospheric processes and this in-depth study enables integrated global snapshots of the atmosphere and more accurate identification of flow patterns, thus allowing for better comparison to models.

rows.title: Author Correction: FANCD2–FANCI surveys DNA and recognizes double- to single-stranded junctions
‘Talking won’t save the planet’: uniting efforts to save Panama’s parks
rows.summary: Juan Carlos Navarro shares his hopes and frustrations as he works to protect his country’s biodiversity and fight climate change.

rows.title: Here’s how to bag a hefty research prize to turbocharge innovation
rows.summary: ‘Challenge’ prizes are growing in popularity, but stimulating creativity takes more than financial incentives.

rows.title: Researchers overlooked airborne diseases for centuries — then COVID-19 changed everything
rows.summary: A fascinating exploration of microbes that can travel through the air reveals how the pandemic marked a turning point for a crucial research field.

rows.title: Money and murder: the dark side of the Asilomar meeting on recombinant DNA
rows.summary: The famed 1975 conference about a controversial genetic technology is feted as an example of how scientific self-regulation works. But more significant is what wasn’t discussed.

rows.title: Daily briefing: The ‘dark side’ of the Asilomar conference
rows.summary: A new theory on how intelligent life evolved on Earth. Plus, the ‘dark side’ of the Asilomar conference on recombinant DNA.

rows.title: Woman in cancer remission for record 19 years after CAR-T immune treatment
rows.summary: CAR-T-cell therapy treated a girl with a rare childhood cancer, raising hopes for future recipients of the approach.

rows.title: What are the best AI tools for research? Nature ’s guide
rows.summary: There are many large language models to choose from; some excel at coding, whereas others are better for synthesizing information.

rows.title: Characterization of single neurons reprogrammed by pancreatic cancer
rows.summary: A technique that combines retrograde axon tracing with single-cell transcriptomics is used to characterize neurons innervating pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma and healthy pancreas, providing insight into the role of neural connections in cancer progression.

rows.title: Ambient-pressure superconductivity onset above 40 K in (La,Pr) 3 Ni 2 O 7 films
rows.summary: Ambient-pressure superconductivity onset above the McMillan limit in bilayer nickelate epitaxial thin films is reported, paving the way for comprehensive investigations of superconductors and for exploring superconductivity at higher transition temperatures in heterostructures.

rows.title: ‘Researching climate change feels like standing in the path of an approaching train’
rows.summary: Studying the impacts of extreme weather events can exact a heavy mental toll. Finding your ‘happy place’ is an important coping strategy.

rows.title: Daily briefing: Scientists use AI to design life-like enzymes from scratch
rows.summary: What Robert F. Kennedy Jr might do with his newfound influence over US science. Plus, life-like enzymes designed from scratch can accelerate a four-step reaction.

rows.title: NASA embraced diversity. Trump’s DEI purge is hitting space scientists hard
rows.summary: Some researchers at NASA and outside it feel betrayed by the changes at the agency, which was known for promoting inclusion in science.

rows.title: Why I retracted part of my PhD dissertation
rows.summary: Psychologist Laura Steenbergen took the step after raising research-integrity concerns about a former mentor.

rows.title: Bats on film: scientific storytelling from a recovering academic
rows.summary: Scientific exchange is more than just research papers. Get your camera out to capture the beauty and intensity of your work, says Mariëtte van der Walt.

rows.title: ‘Targeted and belittled’: scientists at US environmental agency speak out as layoffs begin
rows.summary: President Donald Trump and his team view the Environmental Protection Agency as a threat to US prosperity. Workers have been waiting for the axe to fall.

rows.title: Are the Trump team’s actions affecting your research? How to contact Nature
rows.summary: Use this form to share information with Nature ’s news team, or to make suggestions for future coverage.

rows.title: Bullseye! Galaxy hosts a record-breaking nine starry rings
rows.summary: Astronomers trace the striking pattern to an encounter between a big galaxy and a much smaller one some 50 million years ago.

rows.title: Author Correction: India–Eurasia convergence speed-up by passive-margin sediment subduction
From farm to pharmacy: gene-edited plants produce a popular supplement
rows.summary: Widely grown crops can be bioengineered to make a form of coenzyme Q taken by people seeking a health boost.

rows.title: Daily briefing: A simple blood test could diagnose pancreatic cancer early
rows.summary: A new blood test could diagnose pancreatic cancer before it spreads. Plus, physicists have detected the highest-energy neutrino ever.

rows.title: Scientists use AI to design life-like enzymes from scratch
rows.summary: Combined approach takes AI-engineered enzymes one step closer to practical applications.

rows.title: Publisher Correction: Immune evasion through mitochondrial transfer in the tumour microenvironment
Royal Society will meet amid campaign to revoke Elon Musk’s fellowship
rows.summary: More than 1,300 scientists have signed a letter calling on the world’s oldest science society to reassess the billionaire’s membership after cuts to US science.

rows.title: Vaccine sceptic RFK Jr is now a powerful force in US science: what will he do?
rows.summary: Kennedy has expressed support for some fields, but has also declared he’d like a ‘break’ in infectious-disease research.

rows.title: Are PhDs losing their lustre? Why fewer students are enrolling in doctoral degrees
rows.summary: High living costs paired with stagnant stipends are being blamed for a drop in PhD enrolments in several countries.

rows.title: The researchers on a quest to protect the gut from antibiotics
rows.summary: The crucial drugs can have unintended consequences. Innovative therapies could shield the microbiome from their effects.

rows.title: Quantum-computing technology that makes qubits from atoms wins mega investment
rows.summary: Firms using ‘neutral atoms’ to create qubits are re-entering the race to build useful quantum machines.

rows.title: Cheap blood test detects pancreatic cancer before it spreads
rows.summary: The deadly cancer is often not found until it has spread to other parts of the body.

rows.title: Transylvanian diaries reveal centuries-old climate extremes
rows.summary: Droughts, extreme heat and destructive flooding plagued the region in the sixteenth century, historical documents show.

rows.title: Gourmet cockatoos like to fancy up their food
rows.summary: Make mine blueberry: Goffin’s cockatoos add flair to plain vegetables with a dip into fruity soya yogurt.

rows.title: Dozens of new obesity drugs are coming: these are the ones to watch
rows.summary: Next-generation obesity drugs will work differently from Ozempic and Wegovy — aiming to deliver greater weight loss with fewer side effects.

rows.title: Why is mathematics education failing some of the world’s most talented children?
rows.summary: A study shines a light on the remarkable arithmetic skills that young people acquire outside formal schooling. Education must evolve to enable them to fulfil their potential.

rows.title: Genetic data from Indigenous Greenlanders could help to narrow health-care gap
rows.summary: A study involving 14% of the people in Greenland makes a case for including under-represented groups in population genomics data — which could reduce inequalities in genetics-based clinical care and personalized medicine.

rows.title: Mysterious neutrino barrels through deep waters near Sicily
rows.summary: The observation of a neutrino in an enormous underwater detector has confounded physicists. It is much more energetic than any particle observed previously, suggesting that it came from a distant astrophysical source.

rows.title: Record-breaking neutrino detected by huge underwater telescope
rows.summary: Particle is estimated to have 30 times higher energy than any previously detected — plus, proposed cuts to NIH grants are put on hold by US judge.

rows.title: X-ray telescope casts a sharper gaze on galaxy clusters
rows.summary: Data from the XRISM X-ray satellite provide unprecedented detail on how ionized plasma moves in massive galaxy clusters — a question with huge cosmological and astrophysical implications.

rows.title: The lost long tail of early bird evolution
rows.summary: In the nineteenth century, the discovery of the fossil Archaeopteryx revealed how birds evolved from dinosaurs. A bird fossil of similar age to Archaeopteryx shows flight-aiding innovations such as the loss of a long tail.

rows.title: I work remotely — on Mars
rows.summary: Geochemist Nicolas Randazzo plans for research millions of kilometres away and decades into the future.

rows.title: How centuries of isolation shaped Greenlanders’ unique genetics
rows.summary: Centuries of isolation have given Greenlanders a genetic profile that includes Arctic-specific variants.

rows.title: Daily briefing: Why US scientists aren’t retiring
rows.summary: Centuries of isolation shaped Greenlanders’ unique genetics. Plus, why so many US scientists don’t want to retire.

rows.title: Sea turtles use magnetic ‘map’ and ‘compass’ to navigate the ocean
rows.summary: Loggerhead sea turtles ( Caretta caretta ) can learn to associate food with the geomagnetic signatures of various oceanic regions, suggesting that they are able to find known foraging areas using an internal magnetic ‘map’. This map and an internal magnetic ‘compass’ rely on distinct mechanisms, implying that turtles have two magnetic senses.

rows.title: Does a cell’s gene expression always reflect its function?
rows.summary: Defining a cell’s ‘type’ by the RNA transcripts it expresses is popular in biological research, but evidence from zebrafish neurons suggests that transcriptionally similar cells can be functionally diverse.

rows.title: Record-breaking neutrino is most energetic ever detected
rows.summary: Although still under construction, the sea-floor KM3NeT detector spotted a neutrino 20 times more powerful than any previously detected.

rows.title: Dear Leader
rows.summary: The follies of youth.

rows.title: Socio-economic status explains one-third of the racial disparity in top academic achievement
rows.summary: Excellence gaps — disparities in advanced academic achievement — between racial groups appear by age 8 or 9 and persist throughout secondary school in the United States. About one-third of the gap is due to socio-economic status and one-tenth to school factors, indicating that policies should address both educational and local environments.

rows.title: A bacterial antiviral system detects and directly fights against infection
rows.summary: Bacteria have developed many strategies to defend themselves from phages — the viruses that infect them. The Zorya defence system uses a previously undescribed antiviral strategy. An inner-membrane-anchored complex detects phage infection, resulting in recruitment of enzymes inside the cell that digest incoming phage DNA, thereby rapidly preventing infection.

rows.title: Observation of an ultra-high-energy cosmic neutrino with KM3NeT
rows.summary: A very high-energy muon observed by the KM3NeT experiment in the Mediterranean Sea is evidence for the interaction of an exceptionally high-energy neutrino of cosmic origin.

rows.title: Learning produces an orthogonalized state machine in the hippocampus
rows.summary: Insight into the algorithmic form and learning principles underlying cognitive maps in the hippocampus is provided.

rows.title: Transcriptional adaptation upregulates utrophin in Duchenne muscular dystrophy
rows.summary: Transcriptional adaptation upregulates UTRN in Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) patients, as supported by several lines of evidence, including the use of splice-switching antisense oligonucleotides to induce the skipping of out-of-frame exons of the DMD gene.

rows.title: Transcriptomic neuron types vary topographically in function and morphology
rows.summary: Transcriptomic profiling of neurons from the zebrafish optic tectum identified more than 60 cell types; functional imaging revealed that response tuning, morphology and connectivity of specific cell types vary systematically with the neurons’ positions in the tissue.

rows.title: Topological segregation of stress sensors along the gut crypt–villus axis
rows.summary: Serotonergic enterochromaffin cells of the intestine exhibit distinct sensory, secretory and physiological properties depending on their location within the complex crypt–villus architecture of the gut.

rows.title: A metagenomic ‘dark matter’ enzyme catalyses oxidative cellulose conversion
rows.summary: A metalloenzyme capable of oxidatively cleaving cellulose, found in a microbial community specialized in lignocellulose degradation, could enable sustainable biofuel production.

rows.title: σ-Bond insertion reactions of two strained diradicaloids
rows.summary: A new synthetic method provides a coveted motif, the bicyclo[2.1.1]hexane scaffold, using the uncommon coupling of two strained diradicaloid fragments: transiently generated cyclic allenes and bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes.

rows.title: UM171 glues asymmetric CRL3–HDAC1/2 assembly to degrade CoREST corepressors
rows.summary: UM171 promotes corepressor degradation by acting as a molecular glue to induce KBTBD4–HDAC1/2 interactions with the help of inositol hexakisphosphate.

rows.title: Global engineering effects of soil invertebrates on ecosystem functions
rows.summary: A meta-analysis of more than 1,000 studies reveals the global ecosystem functions provided by termites, ants and earthworms as they improve soil quality by making biogenic structures such as termite mounds, ant hills and earthworm casts.

rows.title: Genetic architecture in Greenland is shaped by demography, structure and selection
rows.summary: We illustrate that including data from Greenlandic Inuit can greatly reduce inequity in genomic-based healthcare in Greenland and other indigenous Arctic populations.

rows.title: Macrophages protect against sensory axon loss in peripheral neuropathy
rows.summary: A study in a mouse model of obesity and prediabetes demonstrates that recruitment of macrophages to nerves has a protective role in diet-induced peripheral neuropathy.

rows.title: Manipulation of the altermagnetic order in CrSb via crystal symmetry
rows.summary: The altermagnetic order in CrSb films can be manipulated via crystal symmetry; the reconstructed altermagnetic order generates a room-temperature spontaneous anomalous Hall effect and designable switching modes as field-assisted and field-free modes.

rows.title: Shielding Pt/γ-Mo 2 N by inert nano-overlays enables stable H 2 production
rows.summary: Atomically dispersed inert oxide nano-overlays on a highly active Pt/γ-Mo 2 N catalyst can block the redundant surface sites of γ-Mo 2 N responsible for surface oxidation of this reactive support and the resulting deactivation, without compromising the intrinsic activity of active Pt@Mo2N interface.

rows.title: Intrinsic electrical activity drives small-cell lung cancer progression
rows.summary: Electrical excitability in neuroendocrine SCLC cells promotes tumour progression through action potential firing, increasing ATP demand and oxidative phosphorylation dependency, whereas non-neuroendocrine cells provide metabolic support, driving a tumour-autonomous cycle that enhances tumorigenesis and metastasis.

rows.title: Hydrogen escaping from a pair of exoplanets smaller than Neptune
rows.summary: Ongoing hydrogen loss from two sibling exoplanets provides support for the role of such hydrogen loss in the evolution of close-orbiting sub-Neptunes.

rows.title: Aqueous-based recycling of perovskite photovoltaics
rows.summary: A recycling strategy based predominantly on the use of water to restore and reuse valuable components from perovskite photovoltaic waste is described, with recycled devices showing similar efficiency and stability compared with fresh devices.

rows.title: Learned magnetic map cues and two mechanisms of magnetoreception in turtles
rows.summary: Loggerhead sea turtles, which undergo long-distance migrations, can learn magnetic signatures associated with different geographic areas and have two different magnetic senses, each based on a different underlying mechanism.

rows.title: MorPhiC Consortium: towards functional characterization of all human genes
rows.summary: This Perspective discusses strategies and challenges for the Molecular Phenotypes of Null Alleles in Cells (MorPhiC) Consortium as it aims to catalogue the molecular and cellular phenotypes associated with null alleles of all human genes.

rows.title: Observation of plastic ice VII by quasi-elastic neutron scattering
rows.summary: Quasi-elastic neutron scattering measurements show the existence of a body-centred cubic structure, similar to that of ice VII, where water molecules exhibit picosecond rotational dynamic and rapid orientational jumps characteristic of liquid water.

rows.title: The neuroimmune connectome in health and disease
rows.summary: A review of studies on communication between the nervous and immune systems redefines the neuroimmune connectome with a focus on health and disease, and discusses how the latest techniques can advance our understanding.

rows.title: Direct experimental constraints on the spatial extent of a neutrino wavepacket
rows.summary: An innovative method using superconducting sensors precisely measures the recoil energy of lithium-7 nuclei, setting a lower limit on the spatial extent of neutrino wavepackets, advancing understanding of neutrino properties and weak nuclear decays.

rows.title: Earliest short-tailed bird from the Late Jurassic of China
rows.summary: Two recently discovered bird fossils from the Late Jurassic Zhenghe Fauna demonstrate that highly derived bird-like features and the origin of birds appeared much earlier in the Jurassic period than previously estimated.

rows.title: Stronger and coarser-grained biodegradable zinc alloys
rows.summary: Extruded zinc alloys of dilute compositions can achieve ultrahigh strength and excellent durability when their micron-scale grain size is increased.

rows.title: Converging mechanism of UM171 and KBTBD4 neomorphic cancer mutations
rows.summary: We show that gain-of-function cancer mutations in the KBTBD4 E3 ligase promote neodegradation of substrates via a shape-complementarity-based mechanism, which converges with the mechanism of action of the UM171 molecular glue degrader and can be blocked by HDAC1/2 inhibitors.

rows.title: The bulk motion of gas in the core of the Centaurus galaxy cluster
rows.summary: X-ray spectroscopic observations of the Centaurus galaxy cluster with the X-Ray Imaging and Spectroscopy Mission satellite show that the hot gas flows along the line of sight relative to the central galaxy.

rows.title: Balanced plant helper NLR activation by a modified host protein complex
rows.summary: In Arabidopsis , mechanisms for NRG1A activation by recognition of a modified host EDS1–SAG101 complex, and NRG1A inhibition by NRG1C through sequestration of activated EDS1–SAG101, show activation and constraint of a central plant immune response system.

rows.title: A crucial role for the cortical amygdala in shaping social encounters
rows.summary: The posterolateral cortical amygdala and other connected brain regions have a key role in mediating the transition from investigative to aggressive behaviour in male mice.

rows.title: Activation and inhibition mechanisms of a plant helper NLR
rows.summary: In plant immunity, sensor NLR resistosomes can generate heterotrimer complexes comprising the helper NLR NRG1, and investigation of cryo-EM structures shows the mechanisms of these heterotrimers in immune activation and suppression.

rows.title: Measuring racial educational disparities over time amongst top achievers
rows.summary: Data from Michigan, USA, systematically document that comparatively fewer students from racial minorities excel in maths and reading, and that this gap grows as students progress through school.

rows.title: External Li supply reshapes Li deficiency and lifetime limit of batteries
rows.summary: A strategy is reported that improves the performance and lifetime of lithium-ion batteries by adding organic Li salt after assembly, which decomposes during cell formation, liberating Li ions and expelling organic ligands as gases.

rows.title: Global biodiversity loss from outsourced deforestation
rows.summary: An analysis of global deforestation linked to consumption of products in the supply chains of large economies finds greater losses for vertebrate species’ ranges outside these countries than in them.

rows.title: Outdated rules on expenses prevent academics from travelling more sustainably
Amazing Australopithecus — excitement from 1925 about a ‘man ape’ fossil find
rows.summary: A skull discovered in South Africa provides key evidence about human evolution, and early plans for a tunnel to connect England and France, in this week’s pick from the Nature archive.

rows.title: Close the biodiversity funding gap by teaching conservation to financial professionals
Author Correction: High fatigue resistance in a titanium alloy via near-void-free 3D printing
Scientific societies need to modernize
‘Aqua tweezers’ manipulate particles with water waves
rows.summary: Researchers create precise 3D patterns with water.

rows.title: Nature markets are nothing new — they are widespread, regulated and instructive
Federico Mayor Zaragoza obituary: former UNESCO chief who championed neonatal screening
rows.summary: The biochemist introduced the first heel-prick tests for newborn babies in Spain, protecting infants from life-changing metabolic conditions.

rows.title: Your brain is full of microplastics: are they harming you?
rows.summary: Plastics have infiltrated every recess of the planet, including your lungs, kidneys and other sensitive organs. Scientists are scrambling to understand their effects on health.

rows.title: Scientists fight Norway’s language law, warning of talent exodus
rows.summary: Mandatory language courses for foreign researchers could harm Norway’s ability to attract the best talent, Nobel laureate says, as rule prompts legal challenge.

rows.title: Daily briefing: ‘Devastating’ cuts to NIH grants blocked by legal challenge
rows.summary: Earth’s inner core is changing shape. Plus, a judge has blocked ‘devastating’ cuts to NIH grants in the United States.

rows.title: ‘Male-dominated campuses belong to the past’: the University of Tokyo tackles the gender gap
rows.summary: A range of initiatives, from financial-support schemes to awareness campaigns, is already changing the university’s environment.

rows.title: Japan can be a science heavyweight once more — if it rethinks funding
rows.summary: The nation must lose its tight focus on individual disciplines if it is to keep pace with the evolving requirements of scientific enquiry.

rows.title: Earth’s mysterious inner core really is changing shape
rows.summary: Earthquakes ringing through the planet illuminate how its heart is transforming.

rows.title: The Greenland Ice Sheet is fracturing faster than expected
rows.summary: Three-dimensional maps of glacier surfaces across Greenland reveal that cracks are growing rapidly where land ice meets the sea — and climate change is to blame.

rows.title: I grow medicinal mushrooms in my renewable-energy laboratory
rows.summary: When Ho Thi Thanh Van isn’t creating materials for fuel cells, she is cultivating traditional medicines.

rows.title: Breaking language barriers: ‘Not being fluent in English is often viewed as being an inferior scientist’
rows.summary: Biologist Tatsuya Amano works to make science a fairer place for non-fluent speakers.

rows.title: How to end outrage and detoxify politics: share stories, not statistics
rows.summary: A book on human morality claims that although liberals and conservatives prioritize different victims, mutual understanding is still possible.

rows.title: A man was destined for early Alzheimer’s — these genes might explain his escape
rows.summary: Scientists identify nine genetic variants that could have helped a man to avoid dementia for at least two decades longer than expected.

rows.title: Daily briefing: How did childhood evolve?
rows.summary: An AI system is crushing it at the International Mathematical Olympiad. Plus, what an iconic fossil teaches us about the evolution of childhood.

rows.title: ‘Devastating’ cuts to NIH grants by Trump’s team put on hold by US judge
rows.summary: The ruling temporarily halts a policy slashing research-overhead costs that left some universities wondering how to make ends meet.

rows.title: Author Correction: A map of the rubisco biochemical landscape
How and why my company pivoted from energy to agritechnology
rows.summary: Lambda Agri chief executive Monica Saavedra describes funding strategies and the circumstances leading to the company changing strategic direction.

rows.title: Poetry on Mars and robots on Earth: Books in brief
rows.summary: Andrew Robinson reviews five of the best science picks.

rows.title: Bonobos know when you’re in the know ― and when you’re not
rows.summary: The apes can tailor their communications to account for a human partner’s level of knowledge.

rows.title: Scientists globally are racing to save vital health databases taken down amid Trump chaos
rows.summary: The mass-archiving effort is in response to the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention removing some of its web pages.

rows.title: ‘We are a target’: scientific society under pressure after Trump DEI crackdown
rows.summary: The American Society for Microbiology deleted terms such as equity from its website, sparking protests from members.

rows.title: Have Trump’s anti-DEI orders hit private funders? HHMI halts inclusive science programme
rows.summary: The Howard Hughes Medical Institute, a huge funder of biomedical research, has cut a $60-million initiative to boost diversity in science education.

rows.title: DeepMind AI crushes tough maths problems on par with top human solvers
rows.summary: The company’s AlphaGeometry 2 reaches the level of gold-medal students in the International Mathematical Olympiad.

rows.title: How my research focus exposed me to threats and harassment
rows.summary: Researchers who investigate highly-politicized topics can face harassment, others for their race, gender identity or disability. Two scientists share their stories.

rows.title: Daily briefing: How mantis shrimps survive landing the world’s fastest punch
rows.summary: What’s behind the mantis shrimp’s powerful punch? Plus, six ways to cultivate allyship for a diverse, equitable and inclusive academia.

rows.title: From viral variants to devastating storms, how names shape the public's reaction to science
rows.summary: In episode 2 of What's in a name we look at how choosing names can help, or hinder, attempts to communicate important messages.

rows.title: Mantis shrimp have the world’s fastest punch — here’s how their limbs survive
rows.summary: Insights from probing the shock-absorbing layer inside the crustacean’s club-like claw could inspire the design of tough new materials.

rows.title: Record-setting trove of buried beads speaks to power of ancient women
rows.summary: A Copper Age burial in Spain holds the largest collection of beads ever found ― enough to require a tonne of shellfish as raw material.

rows.title: How to make the perfect egg: give it lukewarm baths
rows.summary: Process turns out eggs with delectable texture and high nutritional value.

rows.title: How to sell your science without selling out
rows.summary: A five-step guide to communicating your science ethically and accurately.

rows.title: These Gaza scientists are keeping research alive amid war, destruction and uncertainty
rows.summary: Researchers in Gaza tell Nature of ‘unwavering commitment to education and knowledge’ as most universities lie damaged or destroyed.

rows.title: How the brain suppresses fear: mouse study offers path to anxiety treatments
rows.summary: Two brain regions work together when mice learn to override the instinct to run and hide from a potential threat.

rows.title: OpenAI’s ‘deep research’ tool: is it useful for scientists?
rows.summary: The model produces cited, pages-long reports that might be helpful for generating literature reviews.

rows.title: Engineered nose bacteria sneak drugs into the brain
rows.summary: Microbes that reside peaceably in the nasal passageways and on the skin can be harnessed for taking drugs to target cells.

rows.title: Daily briefing: People in dense crowds move in swirls
rows.summary: People begin to move in vortices in densely packed crowds. Plus, the scientists who kept research alive in Gaza during the Israel–Hamas conflict.

rows.title: ‘It is chaos’: US funding freezes are endangering global health
rows.summary: Abrupt changes to programmes including USAID inhibit global efforts to stop diseases such as HIV, malaria and more, say researchers.

rows.title: The weight-loss drugs being tested in 2025: will they beat Ozempic?
rows.summary: Drug companies are trialling a host of medications that they hope will offer benefits beyond weight loss.

rows.title: Granzyme K activates the entire complement cascade
rows.summary: A study finds that a protease called granzyme K can activate the entire complement cascade, explaining how it can drive destructive inflammation in inflammatory diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis.

rows.title: Crowd crush: Could fluid dynamics save lives?
rows.summary: Scientists studying the controversial 'running of the bulls' discover unique crowd movements they hope could prevent overcrowding deaths

rows.title: Out of Africa: celebrating 100 years of human-origins research
rows.summary: A landmark study reporting the discovery of Australopithecus africanus one century ago put the African continent at the centre of the story of humanity.

rows.title: A personalized cancer vaccine to prevent the return of high-risk kidney cancer
rows.summary: In a phase I clinical trial, nine adults with kidney cancer were treated with a personalized cancer vaccine that targets neoantigens (mutant proteins expressed by tumour cells). The vaccine generated immune responses in all nine individuals, and although all of them were at high risk of disease recurrence, none experienced a return of their cancer during the study.

rows.title: ‘Taung Child’ fossil offers clues about the evolution of childhood
rows.summary: A fossil found in South Africa 100 years ago provides insights into the emergence of a crucial — and unusual — life stage.

rows.title: Fossil bird skull suggests Antarctic waterfowl survived Cretaceous mass extinction
rows.summary: The fossilized skull of a bird called Vegavis , which lived in the Antarctic some 68.7 million years ago, confirms it was an early member of the waterfowl group. However, the skull also suggests that, unlike most modern waterfowl, Vegavis used to dive for its fish prey.

rows.title: Kids’ real-world arithmetic skills don’t transfer to the classroom
rows.summary: Research also shows that skills don’t transfer in the other direction either — plus, a new study of crowd movements could help prevent tragedy.

rows.title: Daily briefing: Genetically modified pig-organ transplant trial gets green light
rows.summary: The first pig-organ transplant trial in humans has been approved. Plus, the internet doesn't affect our memories, but AI might.

rows.title: Are the Internet and AI affecting our memory? What the science says
rows.summary: Search engines, GPS maps and other tech can alter our ability to learn and remember. Now scientists are working out what AI might do.

rows.title: School smart or street smart? Maths skills of children in India tested
rows.summary: Do mathematical skills that children acquire in the classroom transfer to real-world settings — and vice versa? Evidence from five large groups of children in India reveals that current school-based teaching practices are failing to bridge the gap. An innovative approach is needed to connect abstract maths to intuitively meaningful contexts and problems.

rows.title: Cancer outcomes predicted using AI-extracted data from clinical notes
rows.summary: Electronic health records and tumour-genome profiling offer promising real-world data with which to model cancer outcomes. Models built by using artificial intelligence (AI) to annotate clinical reports from more than 20,000 individuals with cancer can predict survival, as well as identify genomic features associated with metastasis and response to immunotherapy.

rows.title: How one language family took over the world: ancient DNA traces its spread
rows.summary: Millennia-old genomes suggest Indo-European tongues originated from the Caucasus mountain region.

rows.title: ‘Unconventional’ superconductivity probed in twisted graphene
rows.summary: A superconducting state can be induced in a twisted carbon-based material, but it can’t be described with conventional theory. A technique using high-frequency circuits could reveal the mechanism behind this fascinating state.

rows.title: An atlas of cells in the human brain’s control hub
rows.summary: A comprehensive atlas of the human hypothalamus, a brain region that regulates many bodily functions, including temperature, sleep and appetite, has been built using single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics. The atlas reveals previously unappreciated anatomical and cellular diversity, insights into obesity genetics and key therapeutic differences between humans and mice.

rows.title: Crowds start to spin when their densities hit a threshold
rows.summary: Overcrowding can lead to disaster, and yet the dynamics of dense groups of people are poorly understood. Analysis of a festival uncovers collective rotational movements that emerge at critical densities, which could be universal.

rows.title: Top universities warned against unfair research partnerships on their doorstep
rows.summary: Domestic helicopter research — in which wealthy institutions exploit local communities — is on the rise.

rows.title: Future legal
rows.summary: A rude awakening.

rows.title: Lineage tracing of stem cells decades after blood and bone-marrow transplantation
rows.summary: In individuals receiving an allogeneic haematopoietic cell transplant, stem cells in the bone marrow, which give rise to blood and immune cells, are replaced with those from a donor. Genome-sequencing analyses in donor–recipient pairs years after transplantation show an accelerated loss of clonal diversity in the blood stem cells of recipients compared with those of donors.

rows.title: Crowds suck people into a vortex — surprising physicists
rows.summary: Studying crowd dynamics could inform strategies that help to prevent dense gatherings from becoming dangerous.

rows.title: Superkiller complex problems expose a cancer-cell vulnerability
rows.summary: When a cancer cell no longer makes a particular functioning protein, it can become dependent on another protein for survival. The identification of one such relationship has uncovered a therapeutic target.

rows.title: Poke, twist, vibrate: a wearable device that delivers touch to the skin
rows.summary: A miniaturized electromechanical device has been developed that attaches directly to the skin, utilizing it as an elastic, energy-storing element for delivering touch stimuli. This wireless, conformable interface enables sensory substitution for individuals with sensory impairments, such as problems with sight, sense of balance or foot orientation during walking.

rows.title: Why a standard method overlooks the real reason some antibiotics fail
rows.summary: Antibiotics show limited effectiveness against Salmonella bacteria in infected mice. Conventional methods of analysing bacterial growth suggest that a small subset of hyper-resilient bacteria is the main cause of this poor efficacy. However, direct monitoring of antibiotic action in real time reveals that such methods are misleading, and that Salmonella resilience is a population-wide trait.

rows.title: Genetic and geographical origins of Eurasia’s influential Yamna culture
rows.summary: Ancient genomes from modern Ukraine and Russia reveal the origins of the Yamna people, pastoralists who migrated from the Eurasian steppe to Europe 5,000 years ago, spreading their ancestry, culture and, probably, language.

rows.title: Superfluid stiffness of twisted trilayer graphene superconductors
rows.summary: Measurements of the superfluid stiffness in twisted trilayer graphene reveal unconventional nodal-gap superconductivity, where the superconducting transition is controlled by phase fluctuations rather than Cooper-pair breaking.

rows.title: The genetic origin of the Indo-Europeans
rows.summary: Ancient DNA reveals how the explosive expansion of Yamnaya steppe pastoralists began with a small community north of the Black Sea speaking ancestral Indo-European, and detects genetic links with Anatolian speakers, stemming from a common Indo-Anatolian homeland in the North Caucasus–lower Volga region.

rows.title: Directly imaging the cooling flow in the Phoenix cluster
rows.summary: Observations of the Phoenix cluster using the James Webb Space Telescope reveal rapid cooling in galaxy cluster cores, driven by black hole jets, with gas temperatures mapped between 10 5 K and 10 6 K and cooling rates of 5,000–23,000 M ⊙ yr −1 .

rows.title: Distributed quantum computing across an optical network link
rows.summary: The distribution of quantum computations is demonstrated between two photonically interconnected trapped-ion modules, using repeatable, deterministic teleported controlled-Z gates to perform Grover’s search algorithm.

rows.title: Cretaceous Antarctic bird skull elucidates early avian ecological diversity
rows.summary: A new, nearly complete fossil skull of Vegavis from the James Ross Basin, Antarctic Peninsula, provides insight into its feeding ecology and exhibits morphologies that support placement among waterfowl within crown-group birds.

rows.title: Metal-halide porous framework superlattices
rows.summary: Using zirconium metal–organic frameworks as the host template for directed nucleation and precise growth of metal-halide sublattices, multi-dimensional single-crystalline porous superlattices can be achieved through a one-pot synthesis.

rows.title: IL-27 elicits a cytotoxic CD8 + T cell program to enforce tumour control
rows.summary: IL-27 promotes tumour control by preventing dysfunction and enhancing cytotoxicity of tumour-specific CD8 + T cells.

rows.title: Superfluid stiffness of magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene
rows.summary: Research on superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene reveals unconventional behaviour, an anisotropic gap and a significant role of quantum geometry, using combined d.c. transport and microwave measurements, suggesting new insights into superconductivity mechanisms.

rows.title: Fungal impacts on Earth’s ecosystems
rows.summary: This Review delves into the fungal kingdom, exploring the relationships among fungi, animals, plants and the environment, and investigating both the threats posed by fungi and their potential benefits.

rows.title: Engineering a genomically recoded organism with one stop codon
rows.summary: Ochre, a strain of Escherichia coli engineered to have a single stop codon, enables reassignment of four codons for non-degenerate functions, such as incorporation of non-standard amino acids into proteins.

rows.title: Limited impact of Salmonella stress and persisters on antibiotic clearance
rows.summary: Experiments in infected mice and tissue-mimicking chemostats show that resilience of Salmonella against antimicrobial compounds is largely a result of starvation-induced general resilience rather than survival of a small subset of hyper-resilient cells.

rows.title: Synthetic lethality of mRNA quality control complexes in cancer
rows.summary: PELO–HBS1L and SKI complexes in the human mRNA quality control pathway exhibit a synthetic lethal interaction and may represent novel targets for the development of cancer therapies.

rows.title: Quantum coarsening and collective dynamics on a programmable simulator
rows.summary: A programmable quantum simulator based on Rydberg atom arrays is used to study the collective dynamics of a quantum phase transition and observe the phenomenon of quantum coarsening.

rows.title: A genomic history of the North Pontic Region from the Neolithic to the Bronze Age
rows.summary: Whole-genome sequencing analysis of 81 prehistoric individuals reveals how the genetic makeup of people from the North Pontic region was influenced by waves of migration during the Eneolithic period and Early Bronze Age.

rows.title: SKI complex loss renders 9p21.3-deleted or MSI-H cancers dependent on PELO
rows.summary: Analysis of large-scale CRISPR screening data, combined with experiments in patient-derived tumour organoid models, identifies PELO as a potential therapeutic target in chromosomal 9p21.3-deleted cancers and microsatellite-unstable cancers harbouring specific mutations.

rows.title: Transforming US agriculture for carbon removal with enhanced weathering
rows.summary: A state-level analysis of the impact of enhanced weathering deployment on carbon sequestration on agricultural land suggests that enhanced weathering could help the USA meet net-zero 2050 goals.

rows.title: Topological water-wave structures manipulating particles
rows.summary: Interfering water waves can be tailored to realize topological structures, namely wave vortices, skyrmions and polarization Möbius strips, that can be used to manipulate particles floating on the water surface.

rows.title: A comprehensive spatio-cellular map of the human hypothalamus
rows.summary: HYPOMAP integrates single-nucleus RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomic data to create a comprehensive spatio-cellular map of the human hypothalamus.

rows.title: RUNX2 promotes fibrosis via an alveolar-to-pathological fibroblast transition
rows.summary: The use of two mouse models of pulmonary fibrosis helped the identification of the transcription factor RUNX2 as a regulator of the transition of alveolar fibroblasts to pathological fibroblasts.

rows.title: Differential protection against SARS-CoV-2 reinfection pre- and post-Omicron
rows.summary: Two distinct patterns in the protective effect of natural infection against reinfection in the Omicron variant versus pre-Omicron eras show that SARS-CoV-2 immune protection is shaped by dynamic interaction between host immunity and viral evolution.

rows.title: Multi-interface licensing of protein import into a phage nucleus
rows.summary: This study uncovers a highly conserved jumbo phage protein, Imp1, that possesses multiple interfaces to license protein import into a proteinaceous nucleus-like compartment, using a genetic selection that forces the phage to decrease or abolish the import of specific proteins.

rows.title: Children’s arithmetic skills do not transfer between applied and academic mathematics
rows.summary: Children who learn maths working in markets and children who learn maths only from school were both unable to transfer their skills to new contexts, highlighting a need to reconsider how maths is taught in school.

rows.title: A neoantigen vaccine generates antitumour immunity in renal cell carcinoma
rows.summary: A phase I trial of a neoantigen-targeting personalized cancer vaccine led to durable and polyfunctional T cell responses and antitumour recognition, and was associated with no recurrence in patients with high-risk clear cell renal cell carcinoma.

rows.title: H-bonded organic frameworks as ultrasound-programmable delivery platform
rows.summary: The concept of using hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks triggered by non-invasive focused ultrasound for programmable drug activation is explored and demonstrated practically with the designer drug clozapine N-oxide for deep brain stimulation in mice and rats.

rows.title: Emergence of collective oscillations in massive human crowds
rows.summary: Analysis of the confined crowds at the San Fermín festival in Spain shows that dense crowds can self-organize into macroscopic chiral oscillators, coordinating the orbital motion of hundreds of individuals without external guidance.

rows.title: Two-dimensional polyaniline crystal with metallic out-of-plane conductivity
rows.summary: A multilayer-stacked two-dimensional polyaniline crystal shows high electrical conductivity and unique out-of-plane metallic transport behaviour, indicating potential for strong electronic coupling beyond in-plane interactions and three-dimensional metallic conductivity.

rows.title: Thermalization and criticality on an analogue–digital quantum simulator
rows.summary: A hybrid analogue–digital quantum simulator is used to demonstrate beyond-classical performance in benchmarking experiments and to study thermalization phenomena in an XY quantum magnet, including the breakdown of Kibble–Zurek scaling predictions and signatures of the Kosterlitz–Thouless phase transition.

rows.title: Polytype switching by super-lubricant van der Waals cavity arrays
rows.summary: By etching cavities into a thin lubricant spacer and encapsulating it with functional flakes, electric and mechanical switching of single-crystal, van der Waals stacking configurations is demonstrated.

rows.title: Two-Eyed Seeing and other Indigenous perspectives for neuroscience
rows.summary: Combining Indigenous insights with neuroscience methods through Two-Eyed Seeing can broaden the understanding of brain function and mental wellbeing by merging reductionist and holistic perspectives across various domains, while promoting allyship, humility and inclusive communication.

rows.title: Antibody prophylaxis may mask subclinical SIV infections in macaques
rows.summary: Viral sequencing reveals subclinical infections in animals challenged with simian immunodeficiency virus even in the presence of potent neutralizing antibodies, with implications for clinical trials of antiviral agents against human immunodeficiency virus.

rows.title: Millihertz oscillations near the innermost orbit of a supermassive black hole
rows.summary: A millihertz frequency X-ray quasi-periodic oscillation has been observed near the innermost orbit of an actively accreting supermassive black hole and its frequency has evolved significantly over 2 years, a phenomenon that is difficult to explain with existing models.

rows.title: Grand Canyons on the Moon
rows.summary: How Grand Canyon-sized lunar-valleys could have been carved in mere minutes.

rows.title: Charles Darwin’s brilliance was continuously evolving
rows.summary: The cumulative process of scientific creativity and a noisy lizard’s midnight snack feature in our weekly dive into Nature ’s archive.

rows.title: Net-zero emissions commitments are more threatened than ever
The world must move forwards with plastics treaty
Report both positive and negative effects of gene changes on crops
Guerilla rewilding undermines evidence-based conservation
How are researchers using AI? Survey reveals pros and cons for science
rows.summary: Despite strong interest in using artificial intelligence to make research faster, easier and more accessible, researchers say they need more support to navigate its possibilities.

rows.title: ‘Mind-boggling’: US CDC orders gender-related terms cut from scientific papers
rows.summary: Mandate from health agency is response to President Donald Trump’s crackdown on ‘woke ideology’ and has big implications for researchers.

rows.title: Daily briefing: How scientists can help protect US federal research
rows.summary: Omega-3 supplements seem to slow biological ageing. Plus, how scientific-integrity policies can help protect US scientists from political interference.

rows.title: ‘Research that touches the heart’: the scientists who study sex and love
rows.summary: Romance and relationships are research topics for some scientists in academia and the private sector. Nature asked them for their insights.

rows.title: How the World Health Organization can thrive without the United States
rows.summary: If the 193 remaining member nations want the WHO to succeed, they must find a way to pay for it.

rows.title: Can you ever experience true silence? Intimate exhibition offers insight
rows.summary: An immersive show in Paris leaves you humbled by the awesome power of quiet.

rows.title: The science behind the first pig-organ transplant trial in humans
rows.summary: The small trial will help to establish whether kidneys from genetically modified pigs can be transplanted into people safely and effectively.

rows.title: ‘Despair is not an option’ — how scientists can help protect federal research
rows.summary: Government scientists in the US must be clear-eyed and continue to serve the public.

rows.title: Author Correction: GZMK-expressing CD8 + T cells promote recurrent airway inflammatory diseases
Fish gills and human ears share the same genetic blueprint
rows.summary: Gills and mammalian ears bear little resemblance, yet examination of gene regulation reveals that key supportive cartilage tissue arises from similar embryonic cells guided by an evolutionarily conserved genetic program.

rows.title: Drill, baby, drill? Trump policies will hurt climate ― but US green transition is under way
rows.summary: Market forces could undercut the administration’s plans to increase the use of fossil fuels such as oil and petrol.

rows.title: Can this revolutionary plastics-recycling plant help solve the pollution crisis?
rows.summary: A world-first facility has a new way to break down ‘unrecyclable’ plastic waste.

rows.title: Author Correction: Virus-induced senescence is a driver and therapeutic target in COVID-19
Omega-3 supplements slow biological ageing
rows.summary: The anti-ageing effect was even greater when combined with vitamin D and exercise.

rows.title: Publisher Correction: Placenta-tropic VEGF mRNA lipid nanoparticles ameliorate murine pre-eclampsia
How COVID vaccination keeps a ‘breakthrough’ infection in check

rows.title: Why even physicists still don’t understand quantum theory 100 years on

rows.title: NASA’s ‘most prolific planet hunter so far’ — the story of the Kepler Space Telescope
rows.summary: Ingenuity and decades of planning enabled the mission’s success.

rows.title: Microbes in space: how bacteria could help sustain long-distance space travel
rows.summary: So far, microorganisms have been research subjects or contaminants on space stations, but could they assist longer missions?

rows.title: I spent a year studying campus sexual violence. Here’s what I found out
rows.summary: Institutions that don’t respond to sexual-assault allegations are failing to protect people who could be targeted in future, says Nicole Bedera.

rows.title: Left–right-alternating theta sweeps in entorhinal–hippocampal maps of space
rows.summary: A study in rats proposes a mechanism for how the brain maps the surrounding environment, including places it has never seen, by alternating left and right forward sweeps in successive theta cycles.

rows.title: How a wobbly arrow can achieve superpropulsion
rows.summary: A flexible dart with a weighted tip can have 60% more kinetic energy than a rigid one, experiments show.

rows.title: The AI revolution is running out of data. What can researchers do?
rows.summary: Developers are racing to find new ways to train large language models, after sucking the Internet dry of usable information.

rows.summary: The immune benefits of scratching an itch. Plus, what former NIH director Monica Bertagnolli has to say about everything that’s going on in the United States.

rows.title: Thousands of highly cited scientists have at least one retraction
rows.summary: Database shows that researchers with retracted papers had higher self-citation rates and published more than those without retractions.

rows.title: Mitochondria as you’ve never seen them — January’s best science images
rows.summary: The month’s sharpest science shots — selected by Nature’s photo team.

‘There is life after burnout in academia’
rows.summary: Researchers with lived experience of the chronic workplace stress that typifies burnout describe how they sought help and turned their working lives around.

rows.title: US drug agency approves potent painkiller — the first non-opioid in decades
rows.summary: The FDA’s nod for suzetrigine bolsters confidence in the pharmaceutical industry’s strategy to target sodium channels.

rows.title: ‘London Underground’ mosquito has surprisingly ancient origins
rows.summary: Once thought to have evolved inside the Tube network, a tunnel-dwelling mosquito might actually have emerged thousands of years ago in Egypt.

rows.title: I’ve been wrongly accused of bullying — what do I do?
rows.summary: My ex-supervisor and her new student have levelled serious accusations at me. How do I respond?

rows.title: Author Correction: Stromal changes in the aged lung induce an emergence from melanoma dormancy
Biologists pinpoint neurons that sense how food tastes and feels — in maggots
rows.summary: Fruit fly larvae can perceive the squishy texture of decaying flesh.

rows.title: Who’s the new furry neighbour? It might be a wolverine
rows.summary: The large carnivores are spreading out of remote mountains and into areas settled by humans.

rows.title: Why it feels good to scratch that itch: the immune benefits of scratching
rows.summary: Scratching where it itches reduces the presence of potentially harmful bacteria on the skin, studies in mice show.

rows.title: How China created AI model DeepSeek and shocked the world
rows.summary: Government policies, generous funding and a pipeline of AI graduates have helped Chinese firms create advanced LLMs.

rows.title: ‘High anxiety moment’: Biden’s NIH chief talks Trump 2.0 and the future of US science
rows.summary: Monica Bertagnolli details her concerns about Robert F. Kennedy Jr and his ‘Make America Healthy Again’ campaign.

rows.title: Daily briefing: The pros and cons of DeepSeek
rows.summary: Scientists have found the ingredients for life in the fragments of an asteroid (just not quite the right ones). Plus, researchers weigh up the pros and cons of DeepSeek-R1.

rows.title: Colin Renfrew obituary: archaeologist who shifted thinking on how societies evolve
rows.summary: He brought cutting-edge methods to archaeological analysis, helping to reshape the field.

rows.title: HIV immune evasin Nef enhances allogeneic CAR T cell potency
rows.summary: HIV-1 immune evasin Nef reduces activation-induced cell death and promotes survival of chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells; thus, virus-like immune escape enhances therapeutic efficacy of allogeneic CAR T cells.

rows.title: How flight helped bats become invincible to viruses
rows.summary: The mammals carry immune adaptations that emerged when their ancestors took to the skies.

rows.title: Strange flashes from ancient galaxy deepen mystery of fast radio bursts
rows.summary: Unusual detection bolsters evidence that the mysterious signals can be caused by different astrophysical events.

rows.title: Editorial Expression of Concern: 53BP1 is a reader of the DNA-damage-induced H2A Lys 15 ubiquitin mark
Scientists flock to DeepSeek: how they’re using the blockbuster AI model
rows.summary: Researchers are testing how well the open model can perform scientific tasks — in topics from mathematics to cognitive neuroscience.

rows.title: Asteroid Bennu contains salts from ancient brine
rows.summary: A space mission to an asteroid has returned extremely delicate salts not previously observed in extraterrestrial materials. An analysis of these salts helps to establish the history of water in the early Solar System.

rows.title: Antarctic ice shelf kept its cool during the last interglacial period
rows.summary: There is indirect evidence that, during the last interglacial period, about 125,000 years ago, parts of the West Antarctic Ice Sheet retreated. An ice core drilled from the ice sheet near the bordering Ronne Ice Shelf suggests that, contrary to some model reconstructions, the ice shelf survived this period at almost its current extent.

rows.title: ‘Breakthrough’ stem-cell patches strengthened a woman’s failing heart
rows.summary: Grafting patches of lab-grown muscle to the surface of the heart could offer a lifeline for people waiting for a transplant.

rows.title: Evidence that engineered muscle could patch up failing hearts
rows.summary: Sustainable engraftment of heart muscle cells (cardiomyocytes) can be achieved by implanting patches of engineered heart muscle onto the surface of the heart under immune suppression. Evidence from rhesus macaques and an individual with advanced heart failure suggests that structural and functional augmentation of the failing heart is possible.

rows.title: A shout-out for AI studies that don’t make the headlines
rows.summary: In a year that will see many AI achievements and battles, let’s not forget that not all AI research makes the front pages.

rows.title: Daily briefing: Chaos erupts in US science as Trump’s team declares freeze on federal grants
rows.summary: US scientists are reeling from a Trump-administration freeze on federal grants. Plus, fast radio bursts are even weirder than previously thought.

rows.title: Signs of damage that drive protein degradation
rows.summary: Many environmental toxins damage proteins, which then must be removed to avoid dangerous protein aggregation and disease. How cells dispose of chemically modified proteins has been unclear, but a discovery offers some clues.

rows.title: Asteroid fragments upend theory of how life on Earth bloomed
rows.summary: Samples from Bennu contain the chemical building blocks of life — but with a twist.

rows.title: ‘Dark proteins’ hiding in our cells could hold clues to cancer and other diseases
rows.summary: The human genome encodes potentially thousands of tiny proteins that were previously overlooked. The search is on to find out what they do.

rows.title: Diversity of human gut microbes in Africa reflects geography, lifestyle and health status
rows.summary: Low- and middle-income countries are under-represented in research into the gut microbiome, and addressing this is key to understanding the link between gut-resident microorganisms and health. A large study of the microbiomes of African women provides a resource for microbiome discovery and a framework for equitable research in this area.

rows.title: Dipoles disordered by design to increase capacity of energy-storage devices
rows.summary: Energy-storage devices called capacitors deliver power rapidly, but the amount of energy they can absorb is limited. Deliberately disordered electric dipoles in ‘antiferroelectric’ capacitor materials could solve this problem.

rows.title: Want to get a species protected? Publish in a small, niche journal
rows.summary: Studies are more likely to influence conservation law if they are published in specialist journals — but researchers worry that their true impact is being ignored in hiring and promotion decisions.

rows.title: Asteroid Bennu contains building blocks of life
rows.summary: Bennu gives researchers clues about how the chemicals that make up life arose, how a maize monoculture might have supported a mysterious civilization and why the new AI model DeepSeek R1 has sent shockwaves around the world.

rows.title: Conservation strategies aided by assessment of global genetic diversity
rows.summary: An analysis of published data reveals how genetic diversity has been changing in populations of 622 terrestrial and marine species and the effectiveness of different types of intervention to boost genetic diversity.

rows.title: Underground bacteria serve alcohol to methane-making microbes
rows.summary: Methanol is metabolized into the natural gas methane by many microbes living under Earth’s surface, but its source has been unclear. It emerges that some bacteria convert formate molecules into methanol and transfer it to methane-metabolizing archaea. Such a metabolic transfer of methanol between microbes has not been reported before.

rows.title: After boom
rows.summary: Keeping it real.

rows.title: Viral tolerance enabled by a bat-specific genomic tweak
rows.summary: Bats carry viral pathogens that typically do not lead to severe disease in the bats themselves but can be lethal to humans. Adaptations in certain immune genes might contribute to this resistance.

rows.title: Engineered heart muscle allografts for heart repair in primates and humans
rows.summary: Epicardial engineered heart muscle allografts from induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes can safely and effectively remuscularize chronically failing hearts in rhesus macaques, leading to improved cardiac function and paving the way for human clinical trials.

rows.title: Methanol transfer supports metabolic syntrophy between bacteria and archaea
rows.summary: Zhaonella formicivorans produces methanol, for a novel syntrophic interaction, without requiring methylated compounds as an input.

rows.title: SARS-CoV-2 evolution on a dynamic immune landscape
rows.summary: A modelling approach predicts SARS-CoV-2 variant dynamics on the basis of immunity and cross-neutralization, which was shaped by a region’s SARS-CoV-2 infection history.

rows.title: Structure and mechanism of vitamin-K-dependent γ-glutamyl carboxylase
rows.summary: Structural and cellular assays and molecular dynamics simulations reveal the mechanism of action of γ-glutamyl carboxylase, which involves cholesterol and vitamin K.

rows.title: Warming and cooling catalyse widespread temporal turnover in biodiversity
rows.summary: Global-scale analyses of marine, terrestrial and freshwater assemblages found that temporal rates of species replacement were faster in locations with faster temperature change, including warming and cooling, and vulnerable assemblages were especially responsive.

rows.title: C-terminal amides mark proteins for degradation via SCF–FBXO31
rows.summary: SCF–FBXO31 scans proteins for C-terminal amidation and marks them for subsequent proteasomal degradation.

rows.title: Molecular basis of vitamin-K-driven γ-carboxylation at the membrane interface
rows.summary: Cryo-electron microscopy structures reveal the mechanisms underlying multiple-substrate specificity, coupling of epoxidation with carboxylation and allosteric motions during VKGC catalysis, offering potential strategies for targeting haemostatic and non-haemostatic disorders associated with defects in γ-carboxylation.
