rows.title: Science in 2025: what to expect this year
rows.summary: A new wave of obesity drugs, a multitude of space missions and concern over climate-action policies — we run through what to look out for over the next 12 months.

rows.title: Light turns tiny crystals into force sensors
rows.summary: Two studies show that the light emitted by nanocrystals embedded with luminescent ions can be used to sense forces with high spatial resolution — even when those forces are inside a microscopic living worm.

rows.title: Paradoxical link between senescent cell state and liver cancer resolved
rows.summary: Metabolic-dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is defined by lipid accumulation and inflammation, and makes liver cells enter a tumour-suppressive state called senescence while increasing cancer risk. Investigation of this paradox reveals that MASH-inducing diets trigger senescence by causing DNA damage. However, prolonged metabolic stress allows once-senescent liver cells to start dividing and progress to cancer.

rows.title: Direct fabrication of lasers on silicon suggests solution to chip-production problem
rows.summary: The lack of methods for preparing miniature lasers directly on silicon wafers is holding back photonic technology in a range of applications, including machine learning. The solution could be to construct lasers in nanoscale trenches.

rows.title: Limitations of ice cores in reconstructing temperature seasonality
Gut lining in pregnant and lactating mice expands to ensure offspring health
rows.summary: During pregnancy, several organs are rewired to support the health of the mother and the offspring. A molecular signalling pathway called RANK–RANKL drives the expansion of the layer that lines the inside of the intestine during pregnancy and lactation. This tissue remodelling process has a key role in mammalian life history.

rows.title: Reply to: Limitations of ice cores in reconstructing temperature seasonality
GaAs nano-ridge laser diodes fully fabricated in a 300-mm CMOS pilot line
rows.summary: A new integration approach, nano-ridge engineering, enables electrically driven GaAs-based laser diodes to be fabricated on Si wafers in a complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor (CMOS) pilot line, showing potential for the integration of laser diodes in a Si photonics platform.

rows.title: Bone marrow niches orchestrate stem-cell hierarchy and immune tolerance
rows.summary: Previously undescribed hierarchical arrangements in haematopoietic stem cells and their niches that mediate both regenerative potential and immune privilege are identified.

rows.title: Upconverting microgauges reveal intraluminal force dynamics in vivo
rows.summary: Nanoparticle-based ‘microgauges’ are developed for in vivo force sensing and deployed in C. elegans to investigate how mechanical force correlates with electrical signalling in neuromuscular organs.

rows.title: FBP1 controls liver cancer evolution from senescent MASH hepatocytes
rows.summary: The p53 target FBP1 is elevated in senescent-like metabolic-dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis hepatocytes but suppressed through promoter hypermethylation and proteasomal degradation in most human hepatocellular carcinomas.

rows.title: High-resolution genomic history of early medieval Europe
rows.summary: Twigstats, a method for ancestry reconstruction, provides high-resolution genetic histories and movement patterns of people living in Europe during the first millennium ce .

rows.title: A collicular map for touch-guided tongue control
rows.summary: Touch-guided tongue control in mice relies on a collicular mechanosensorimotor map, analogous to collicular visuomotor maps associated with visually guided orienting across many species.

rows.title: Brain-wide cell-type-specific transcriptomic signatures of healthy ageing in mice
rows.summary: A comprehensive single-cell RNA sequencing study delineates cell-type-specific transcriptomic changes in the brain associated with normal ageing that will inform the investigation into functional changes and the interaction of ageing and disease.

rows.title: Non-Abelian lattice gauge fields in photonic synthetic frequency dimensions
rows.summary: Non-Abelian lattice gauge fields in photonic synthetic frequency dimensions can be used to study lattice physics in a scalable and programmable way.

rows.title: Formation of individual stripes in a mixed-dimensional cold-atom Fermi–Hubbard system
rows.summary: Observations of the formation of individual stripes in a mixed-dimensional cold-atom Fermi–Hubbard quantum simulator are described, enhancing understanding of the phase diagram of high-temperature superconducting materials and the relationship between charge pairs and stripes.

rows.title: Monoallelic expression can govern penetrance of inborn errors of immunity
rows.summary: Somatically determined preferential allelic expression of select genes that when mutated cause inborn errors of immunity corresponds with disease phenotypes, suggesting that the penetrance and expressivity of monogenic disorders is also dependent on the ‘transcriptotype’.

rows.title: Infrared nanosensors of piconewton to micronewton forces
rows.summary: An avalanching-nanoparticle force sensor that can operate in the piconewton-to-micronewton range with exceptional force responsiveness is achieved by using the mechanical sensitivity of the photon-avalanching process.

rows.title: Dysregulation of mTOR signalling is a converging mechanism in lissencephaly
rows.summary: Cellular, transcriptomic and proteomic analyses of organoids derived from human induced pluripotent stem cells show that mTOR pathway hypoactivation is involved in two genetically distinct lissencephaly spectrum disorders.

rows.title: Diversity and biogeography of the bacterial microbiome in glacier-fed streams
rows.summary: Leveraging metabarcoding and metagenomics, a survey of bacteria in the benthic microbiome across 152 glacier-fed streams (GFSs) provides a global reference for future climate-change microbiology studies on the vanishing GFS ecosystem.

rows.title: Magnetospheric origin of a fast radio burst constrained using scintillation
rows.summary: The detection of scintillation caused by inhomogeneous plasma near a fast radio burst indicates an emission process that occurs within or just beyond the magnetosphere of a compact object.

rows.title: Structural diversity of axonemes across mammalian motile cilia
rows.summary: Cryoelectron microscopy, cryoelectron tomography and proteomics are used to resolve the 96-nm modular repeat of axonemal doublet microtubules from both sperm flagella and epithelial cilia of the oviduct, brain ventricles and respiratory tract.

rows.title: Gliomagenesis mimics an injury response orchestrated by neural crest-like cells
rows.summary: A study using glioblastoma mouse models, serial magnetic resonance imaging and single-cell profiling details changes in the identity and balance of cellular states from initiation of tumorigenesis to the end point.

rows.title: Abrupt changes in biomass burning during the last glacial period
rows.summary: An increase in wildfire extent and related greenhouse gas emissions can be linked to abrupt climatic changes during the last glacial period.

rows.title: A pulsar-like polarization angle swing from a nearby fast radio burst
rows.summary: FRB 20221022A, detected by the Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment Fast Radio Burst project, shows a pronounced change in polarization during the burst, providing important clues into the nature of the source.

rows.title: Learning the fitness dynamics of pathogens from phylogenies
rows.summary: Phylowave, an innovative phylogenetic approach, can identify the main circulating pathogen lineages with increased fitness and the associated genetic changes, enabling the timely identification of emergent strains and deployment of targeted interventions.

rows.title: Aspartate signalling drives lung metastasis via alternative translation
rows.summary: Aspartate in the tumour environment activates the N -methyl- d -aspartate receptor in cancer cells to induce cellular programmes that increase the aggressiveness of metastasis.

rows.title: Centrophilic retrotransposon integration via CENH3 chromatin in Arabidopsis
rows.summary: An Arabidopsis long terminal repeat retrotransposon integrates de novo into regions occupied by centromere-specific histone variant, showing the impact of centromeric chromatin on transposable element-mediated rapid centromere evolution, with relevance across eukaryotic genomes.

rows.title: The progression of basaltic–rhyolitic melt storage at Yellowstone Caldera
rows.summary: The resistivity structure of Yellowstone Caldera’s crustal magma reservoir indicates that the magma reservoirs are not eruptible at present and that the locus of future volcanism has shifted to northeast Yellowstone Caldera.

rows.title: Sleep microstructure organizes memory replay
rows.summary: The temporal microstructure of the brain can multiplex distinct cognitive processes during sleep to support continuous learning.
